- भूरेः (*bhūreḥ*)—of abundant wealth
- ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)—and the lord (praise Indra)

### Printed p. 240

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Praise Indra, who comes near to those who praise him in order to favour them, who is of great glory, who in battles does not lose and flee but stands firm against the enemies, who seizes food from the enemies in battle or wins fame, and who by his own power is lord of an immeasurable mass of wealth.

##### English translation
Him who comes nigh, the mighty, the firm in battles, the acquirer of fame, the lord of the vast riches through his prowess.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नकिरस्य शचीनां नियंता सून्मत्तानां ।  
> नकि॑र्व॒क्ता न दा॒दिति॑ ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नकिः । अस्य । शचीनां । नियंता । सूनृतानां ।  
> नकिः । वक्ता । न । दात् । इति ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्येंद्रस्य सूनृतानां शोभनानां शचीनां कर्मणां । धीः शचीति कर्मनामसु पाठात् । नकिर्न कश्चिन्नियंता नियामकः । अयमिंद्रो न दादिति न
> प्रयच्छतीति नकिर्वक्ता न कश्चिद्वदति । किंतु सर्वोऽपि जनोऽयं प्रदातेत्येव
> ब्रवीतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of this Indra, of the good deeds called शचीनां (*śacīnāṃ*), that is, of actions, for it is read so among the names of action, there is no controller, no regulator. And no one says that this Indra does not give, that he does not bestow; rather, everyone says only that he is a giver.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- सूनृतानां (*sūnṛtānāṃ*)—of the excellent or auspicious
- शचीनां (*śacīnāṃ*)—for the deeds
- नियंता (*niyaṃtā*)—one who controls
- नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—there is no one
- न दात् इति (*na dāt iti*)—(and that this Indra) gives nothing to the people who praise him
- नकिः वक्ता (*nakiḥ vaktā*)—there is no one who says so

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

There is no one who controls Indra, saying that he should perform his excellent deeds only so far. Indra is not subject to anyone. And there is no man who says that this Indra gives nothing to the people who praise him. That is, everyone says that Indra gives those who praise him whatever they need.

### Printed p. 241

##### English translation
No one puts a limit to his glorious deeds, no one asserts that he is not generous.

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न नू॒नं ब्र॒ह्मणा॑मृ॒णं प्रा॑शू॒नाम॑स्ति सुन्व॒तां ।  
> न सोमो॑ अप्र॒ता स॑पेः ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । नूनं । ब्रह्मणां । ऋणं । प्राशूनां । अस्ति । सुन्नतां ।  
> न । सोमः । अप्रका । पपे ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्राशूनां । ये सोमं प्राश्नुवंति ते प्राशवः । तेषां सोमं सुन्वतां
> ब्रह्मणां ब्राह्मणानामृणं देवर्णं न नूनमस्ति । न खलु विद्यते । तथा च
> श्रूयते । एष वा अनृणो यः पुत्री यज्ञा ब्रह्मचारिवासी । त्रै. सं. ६-३-१०-५ ।
> इति । किंचाप्रतापिस्तीर्णधनेन सोमो न पपे । न पीयते । प्रभूतधनेनैव
> सोमः पीयत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those who partake of Soma are called प्राशूनां (*prāśūnāṃ*). Of those brahmans who press Soma there is certainly no debt to the gods, no such debt is found. So it is heard: "He alone is free of debt who has a son, has sacrificed and lives as a student of the Veda" (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-10-5). Further, the Soma is not drunk by one whose wealth is not abundant; the meaning is that Soma is drunk only with abundant wealth. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रारूनां (*prārūnāṃ*)—for the people who drink Soma
- सुन्वतां (*sunvatāṃ*)—who perform the Soma pressing in the sacrifice
- ब्रह्मणां (*brahmaṇāṃ*)—for the brahmans
- ऋणं (*ṛṇaṃ*)—the debt to the gods, which has to be repaid to the gods
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—certainly
- न अस्ति (*na asti*)—there is not (and)
- अप्रता (*apratā*)—by those who have not abundant wealth
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the Soma juice
- न पपे (*na pape*)—is not drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the people who drink Soma at sacrifices and the like, and who in performing a sacrifice crush the Soma plants, extract the juice, offer it to the gods according to rule in order to present it to them, and drink it themselves, there is no debt connected with the gods. And by those who lack sufficient wealth to carry out sacrifices and the like, the drinking of Soma is not possible.

### Printed p. 242

##### English translation
Verily no debt is due (to the gods) by those Soma-partaking Brahmans offering libations : the Soma is not drunk without the expenditure of boundless (wealth).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this ṛk, Soma drinking and Soma pressing mean the drinking of Soma performed in the proper manner in the course of the sacrificial rites. For those who drink Soma in this way, following the performance of a sacrifice, there is no debt to the gods. And since persons of small wealth cannot perform a sacrifice, it is said here that such people cannot drink Soma. It is necessary here to explain what the debt to the gods is. On this subject the Taittirīya Śruti says as follows.
जायमानो वै ब्राह्मणस्त्रिभिर्यणवा जायते ब्रह्मचर्येणर्षिभ्यो यज्ञेन देवेभ्यः प्रजया पितृभ्य एष वा अनृणो यः पुत्री यज्वा ब्रह्मचारिवासी ॥ (*jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇastribhiryaṇavā jāyate brahmacaryeṇarṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayā pitṛbhya eṣa vā anṛṇo yaḥ putrī yajvā brahmacārivāsī ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-10-5)
That is, a brahman is born carrying three kinds of debts (loans); one who is born a brahman must repay the three debts called the debt to the sages, the debt to the gods and the debt to the ancestors. Otherwise he has no good destiny. The manner of repaying these debts is this. If, immediately after the initiation, he studies the Veda in the stage of studentship, serving his teacher, he repays the debt to the sages. Then, marrying at the proper time and becoming a householder, if he performs sacrifices and the like in order to worship the gods, he repays the debt to the gods. And by begetting a son on his wedded wife he repays the debt to the ancestors. Therefore the chief meaning of this Vedic sentence is that a brahman, for the discharge of these three kinds of debt, should after the initiation live in the teacher's house, complete the study of the Veda, marry with the teacher's permission, perform sacrifices and so satisfy the gods, beget a son at the proper time and keep doing good deeds. In the present ṛk only the matter of the debt to the gods is indicated. By the words Soma pressing, Soma drinking and the like, the performance of sacrifice is indicated. Since the proper drinking of Soma is prescribed only in sacrifices, the words Soma pressing and Soma drinking mean the performance of sacrifice. The chief meaning of the ṛk is that by doing these the debt to the gods is repaid.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The powerful one who tears apart, face to face, hundreds and thousands of heroes, this Indra, unenclosed by enemies, is praiseworthy. He is the one who, for the sacrificer who has sacrificed according to rule, is the enhancer.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Indra who
- वाजी (*vājī*)—is mighty

- यज्जनः (*yajjanaḥ*)—worshipped according to rule by the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, and
- वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)—makes the sacrificer prosper

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र आहुव आह्वातव्यस्त्वं कृष्णीनां मनुष्याणां स्वधा हवींष्यनु सु
> सुष्टु वि चर । द्वितीयोऽनु पूरणः । सुतानामभिषुतान् सोमांश्च पिब ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you who are to be invoked, move well about the oblations (स्वधा (*svadhā*)) of men, who are called कृष्णीनां (*kṛṣṇīnāṃ*). The second अनु (*anu*) only completes the phrase. And drink the Soma juices that have been pressed.

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- आहुवः (*āhuvaḥ*)—you who are invoked
- कृष्णीनां (*kṛṣṇīnāṃ*)—offered by men
- स्वधाति अनु (*svadhāti anu*)—to the vicinity of the oblation
- सु वि चर (*su vi cara*)—you go, do you not
- सुतानां (*sutānāṃ*)—the Soma juices pressed and made ready
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are invoked at sacrifices and the like, go to the oblation offered by men in order to partake of it. O Indra, drink the Soma juices that have been pressed and made ready.

##### English translation

> यः सोमस्तुग्र उदके । बुसं तुग्रमित्युदकनामसु पाठात् । सचा संसृष्टः
> तमपि सोमं पिब । उतापि च यः सोमस्तव त्वदीयस्त्वामुद्दिश्य गृहीतः
> सोऽयं त्वया पातव्य इति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, drink the Soma belonging to the cow that gives her own milk, that is, Soma bought with a cow. So it is heard: "He buys with a cow." Moreover, drink also the Soma that is in water, mixed with it; water is read among the names of water in the list of synonyms. And the Soma that is yours, taken for you, is to be drunk by you; this last is the word to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- स्वधैनवानां (*svadhainavānāṃ*)—the Soma that has been bought for you by giving cows
- उत (*uta*)—and
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Soma which
- तुग्रे सचा (*tugre sacā*)—is mixed with water
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Soma which
- तव (*tava*)—has been pressed for you alone
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—such Soma as this, may it be drunk by you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, for your drinking, these Soma plants have been bought by giving cows, well pressed, mixed with water and made ready for drinking. Drink such Soma.

##### English translation
Drink of the (Soma) purchased by the milch cow, that (Soma) which is mixed with water, that which, Ida is especially yours.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this ṛk it is said that the Soma has been bought by giving cows. Since the Soma plants grow on some river banks and in high mountain regions, not everyone can easily fetch them. Therefore it has become the custom to buy them, at great cost, from those who have brought them from distant regions, and to use them in sacrifices and the like. This buying is called Soma purchase. It is considered a rite forming part of the sacrifice. When Soma plants are bought, it is the custom to give many kinds of things in exchange. The sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā tells clearly what those things are.
अजया क्रीणाति सतपसमेवैनं क्रीणाति हिरण्येन क्रीणाति सशुक्रमेष्टैनं क्रीणाति धेन्वा क्रीणाति साशिरमेष्टैनं क्रीणात्कृषभेण क्रीणाति सेंद्रमेवैनं क्रीणात्यनडुहा क्रीणाति वह्निर्वा अनड्वान् वह्निनैव वह्नि यज्ञस्य क्रीणाति मिथुनाभ्यां क्रीणाति मिथुनसा वरुध्यै वाससा क्रीणाति सर्वदेवत्यं वै वासः सर्वाभ्य एवैनं देवताभ्यः क्रीणाति दश संपद्यंते ॥ (*ajayā krīṇāti satapasamevainaṃ krīṇāti hiraṇyena krīṇāti saśukrameṣṭainaṃ krīṇāti dhenvā krīṇāti sāśirameṣṭainaṃ krīṇātkṛṣabheṇa krīṇāti seṃdramevainaṃ krīṇātyanaḍuhā krīṇāti vahnirvā anaḍvān vahninaiva vahni yajñasya krīṇāti mithunābhyāṃ krīṇāti mithunasā varudhyai vāsasā krīṇāti sarvadevatyaṃ vai vāsaḥ sarvābhya evainaṃ devatābhyaḥ krīṇāti daśa saṃpadyaṃte ‖*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 6 1-10-1, 2) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 247

It is said that one may buy by giving any one of ten kinds of goods: goat, austerity, gold, śukra, a milch cow, milk, a bull, an ox, a pair, a garment. Among these, it is said in the present ṛk that the Soma bought by giving a dhenu, that is, a cow that gives milk, has been made ready for Indra.

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अती॑हि मन्युषा॒विणं॑ सुषु॒नांस॑मु॒पार॑णे ।  
> इ॒मं रा॒तं सु॒तं पि॑ब ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अति । इहि । मन्युसाविनं । सुसुवांसं । उपअरणे ।  
> इमं । रातं । सुतं । पिब ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र मन्युषाविणं क्रोधेन सोमं सुन्वंतमतीहि । अतिगच्छः । तथोपारणे । ब्राह्मणा उपेत्य यस्मिन्नेशे न रमंते स उपारणः । तस्मिन्नेशे सुषुवांसं सुन्वंतमतीहि । इमं रातं ब्राह्मणोपद्रवरहिते देशेऽस्माभिर्दत्तमिमं
> सुतं सोमं पिब ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, pass beyond the one who presses Soma in anger. Likewise, in a place called उपारणे (*upāraṇe*), where brahmans, having come, do not delight, pass beyond one who presses Soma. Drink this Soma that has been given, that is, pressed and offered by us in a place free from the disturbance of brahmans.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मन्युषाविणं (*manyuṣāviṇaṃ*)—(O Indra) for the Soma drinking prepared by one who presses Soma in a fit of anger
- अति इहि (*ati ihi*)—do not go
- उपारणे (*upāraṇe*)—in a place without brahmans
- सुषुवांसं (*suṣuvāṃsaṃ*)—for the Soma drinking prepared by one who presses, do not go either (but)
- इमं रातं (*imaṃ rātaṃ*)—prepared by us in this place free of disturbance by brahmans
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—this Soma juice
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, do not go there to drink the Soma juice pressed by one who is always filled with anger. And do not drink the Soma pressed in a place without brahmans, that is, in a place where no sacrifice is performed. But this Soma that we have prepared has been pressed in a good place by brahmans, hallowed with mantras, and made ready. Drink such Soma juice.

### Printed p. 248

##### English translation
Indra, pass by the man who offers the libation in anger, him who pours it out upon a spot disapproved of ; drink this presented Soma.

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒हि ति॒स्रः प॑रा॒वत॑ इ॒हि पंच॒ जना॒ अति॑ ।  
> धेना॑ इंद्राव॒चाक॑शत् ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इहि । तिस्रः । परावतः । इहि । पंच । जनान् । अति ।  
> धेनाः । इंद्र । अव्यचाकशत् ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र धेना अस्मदीयाः स्तुतीरवचाकशद्योऽपश्यत् स त्वं पारावतो
> दूरात् । आरे परावत इति दूरनामसु पाठात् । तिस्रोऽग्रपृष्ठ पार्श्वदिश इहि ।
> गच्छ । अनेनाग्रतः पृष्ठतः पार्श्वतश्चेंद्रस्यागमनमाशास्त्रे । अपि च पंच जनान्
> मनुष्यानतीहि । अतिगच्छ । यद्वा। गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसि च पंच
> जनाः । तानतीहीत्यर्थः । तथा च यास्कः । गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीत्येके चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पंचम इत्यौपमन्यवः । नि. ३-८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you who have seen our praises (धेना (*dhenā*) means our praises), come from far away; "far" because परावत (*parāvata*) is read among the names of distance. Come from the three directions, front, back and side; by this the coming of Indra from in front, from behind and from the side is wished for. Further, pass beyond the five peoples, that is, men. Or else: Gandharvas, fathers, gods, asuras and rākṣasas are the five peoples; pass beyond them. So Yāska says: "Gandharvas, fathers, gods, asuras and rākṣasas, say some; the four classes and the Niṣāda as the fifth, say the followers of Upamanyu" (Ni. 3-8).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- धेनाः (*dhenāḥ*)—our praises
- अवचाकशत् (*avacākaśat*)—you who see and know
- परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)—from a distant region
- तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)—from three sides, that is, from the front, the back and the sides
- इहि (*ihi*)—come here
- पंच जनान् (*paṃca janān*)—the five peoples, Gandharvas and the rest
- अति (*ati*)—passing beyond
- इहि (*ihi*)—come here

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who see and know from afar the words of praise we make, come to us from the distant region, from the front, from behind or from the sides. Or, disregarding the five peoples beginning with the Gandharvas, or the people of five tribes, who are on the way, pass beyond them and come to us.

### Printed p. 249

##### English translation
Indra, you have beheld our praises; proceed in three directions from a distance. pass beyond the five orders of beings.

> सूर्यो॑ र॒त्मिं यथा॑ सृ॒जा त्वा॑ यच्छंतु मे॒ गिरः॑ ।  
> नि॒म्म मापो॒ न स॒ध्र्य॑क् ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सूर्यः । रश्मिं । यथा । सृज । आ । त्वा । यच्छंतु । मे । गिरः ।  
> निम्मं । आपः । न । सध्र्यक् ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र सूर्यो यथा रश्मिं रश्मीन्किरणानश्वप्रग्रहान्वा विसृजति तथा मह्यं
> धनं विसृज । अपि च मे मदीया गिरः स्तुतयः सध्यक् सह त्वामा यच्छंतु ।
> निम्ममापो न । यथा निम्मदेशमापः सह परिगृह्णंति तद्वदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, as the sun lets go his rays (that is, his beams, or else the reins of his horses), so let go wealth for me. And may my praises together reach you; as the waters together take hold of a low place, so, is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—(O Indra) the sun
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the way in which
- रश्मिं (*raśmiṃ*)—spreads his rays all around, like that
- सृज (*sṛja*)—give me wealth and the like
- निम्मं (*nimmaṃ*)—in a low region
- आपो न (*āpo na*)—as water flows and comes to rest
- मे (*me*)—my
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—words of praise
- सध्र्यक् (*sadhryak*)—joining together as one
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- यच्छंतु (*yacchaṃtu*)—may they reach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as the sun spreads his rays around himself, make wealth and the like come and gather near me. As flowing water goes to a low place and comes to rest, may the words of praise that I make go to you and join you.

##### English translation
As the sun disperses his rays, so you disperse (wealth upon me):-may my praises rapidly draw you, as waters (reach) the low ground.

#### Ṛk 24

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध्व॑र्य॒वा तु हि षिं॒च सोमं॑ वी॒राय॑ शि॒प्रिणे॑ ।  
> भरा॑ सु॒तस्य॑ पी॒तये॑ ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध्वयो इति । आ । तु । हि । सिंच । सोमं । वीराय । शिप्रिणे ।  
> भर । सुतस्य । पीतये ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्यवः शिप्रिणे हनूमते वीराय शूरायेंद्राय सोमं तु
> हि क्षिप्रमेवा सिंच । सुतस्य सुतं सोमं पीतये पानाय च भर । आहर च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O adhvaryus, to Indra the hero, the brave one, who is शिप्रिणे (*śipriṇe*) (possessed of jaws), pour the Soma quickly. And bring the pressed Soma for his drinking.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वयो (*adhvayo*)—O adhvaryu
- शिप्रिणे (*śipriṇe*)—shining with attractive cheeks
- वीराय (*vīrāya*)—for the brave Indra
- सोमं तु (*somaṃ tu*)—the Soma juice
- हि (*hi*)—quickly
- आ सिंच (*ā siṃca*)—press and make ready
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—the pressed Soma juice
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—for Indra's drinking
- भर (*bhara*)—bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O adhvaryu, quickly make ready the Soma juice for the brave Indra, who shines with attractive cheeks. And bring that pressed Soma juice for the drinking of Indra.

##### English translation
Adhwaryu, quickly pour forth the soma to the hero Indra with the goodly jaws; bring the Soma for his drinking.

#### Ṛk 25

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य उ॒द्दः फ॑लि॒गं भि॒नन्नृ १ १॒॑क्सिंधू॑र॒वासृ॑जत् ।  
> यो गोषु॑ प॒क्वं धा॒रय॑त् ॥ २५ ॥

### Printed p. 251

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । उद्द्नः । फलिगं । भिनत् । न्यक् । सिंधून् । अव्यअसृजत् ।  
> यः । गोषु । पक्वं । धारयत् । २५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उदन्' उदकार्थं फलिगं मेघं । रैवतः फलिग इति मेघनामसु
> पाठात् । भिनत् अभिनत् । सिंधूनपश्चांतरिक्षान्यगर्वागवासृजत् । यश्च गोषु
> पक्वं पयो धारयत् आधारयत् । स इंद्र इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He who, for the sake of water, split the cloud; फलिग (*phaliga*) is read among the names of cloud, the passage being "raivata is phaliga". He let the waters of the atmosphere, called सिंधून् (*siṃdhūn*), flow down; and he who has placed ripe milk in the cows: that is Indra. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Indra who, for the sake of water
- फलिगं (*phaligaṃ*)—the cloud
- भिनत् (*bhinat*)—split
- सिंधून् (*siṃdhūn*)—the waters that were in the cloud
- न्यत् (*nyat*)—downward from the atmosphere
- अवासृजत् (*avāsṛjat*)—made pour
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Indra who
- गोषु (*goṣu*)—in the cows
- पक्वं (*pakvaṃ*)—the ripe milk
- धारयत् (*dhārayat*)—placed; for the drinking of such an Indra, bring the Soma juice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the drinking of Indra of such greatness, who split the cloud in order to pour down rain, who made the water that was in the atmosphere pour down as rain, and who established milk in the cows, O adhvaryu, bring the Soma juice.

##### English translation
Who clove the cloud for (the issue of) the rain, who sent down the waters, who placed the mature (milk) in thc cattle.

#### Ṛk 26

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अह॑न्व॒त्रमृचे॑षम और्णवा॒भम॑ही॒शुवं॑ ।  
> हि॒मेना॑विध्य॒दर्बु॑दं ॥ २६ ॥

### Printed p. 252

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहन् । वृत्रं । यजीषमः । और्णवाभं । अहीशुवं ।  
> हिमेन । अविध्यत् । अर्बुदं ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋचीषम ऋचा दीप्त्या सम इंद्रो वृत्रं वृत्रनामकं शत्रुमहन् ।
> जघान । तथार्णवाभमौर्णवाभनामकमहीशुवमहीशुवनामकं च शत्रुमहन् ।
> तथा हिमेन तुषारेणोदकेन वार्बुदं मेघमविध्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, equal in brilliance, killed the enemy named Vṛtra; likewise he killed the enemies named Aurṇavābha and Ahīśuva. And with frost, that is, with snow-water, he pierced the cloud called Arbuda.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋचीषमः (*ṛcīṣamaḥ*)—the shining Indra
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—the asura called Vṛtra
- अहन् (*ahan*)—killed (and)
- और्णवाभं (*aurṇavābhaṃ*)—the asura called Aurṇavābha
- अहीशुवं (*ahīśuvaṃ*)—and the asura called Ahīśuva he killed
- अर्बुदं (*arbudaṃ*)—the cloud
- हिमेन (*himena*)—with cold water or with frost
- अविध्यत् (*avidhyat*)—he pierced

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, whose body shines exceedingly, killed the asura called Vṛtra and the asuras Aurṇavābha and Ahīśuva. And with frost he split the cloud so that it was torn open.

##### English translation
The brilliant Indra slew Vritra, Aurnavabha, Ahishuva; he smote Arbuda with frost.

#### Ṛk 27

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र व॑ उ॒ग्राय॑ नि॒ष्टुरेऽषा॑ळ्हाय प्रस॒क्षिणे॑ ।  
> दे॒वत्तं॒ ब्रह्म॑ गायत ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वः । उग्राय । निःतुरे । अषाळ्याय । प्रसक्षिणे ।  
> देवत्तं । ब्रह्म । गायत ॥ २७ ॥

### Printed p. 253

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उद्गातारः वो ययमुग्रायोद्दूर्णाय निष्टुरे शत्रून्निस्तरतेऽषाळ्दाय शत्रूणामभिभवित्रे प्रसक्षिणे प्रसहनशीलायेंद्राय देवत्तं देवप्रसादलब्धं ब्रह्म स्तोत्रं प्र गायत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Udgātṛs, to Indra, fierce, that is, exceedingly strong; the अषाळ्हाय (*aṣāḷhāya*), the overcomer of enemies; the प्रसक्षिणे (*prasakṣiṇe*), of an overpowering nature; sing forth the hymn that is gift of the gods, that is, obtained through the favour of the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वः (*vaḥ*)—(O Udgātṛs who sing the Sāman) you
- उग्राय (*ugrāya*)—to the fierce
- निस्तुरे (*nisture*)—who disregards enemies
- अषाळ्हाय (*aṣāḷhāya*)—who defeats enemies
- प्रसक्षिणे (*prasakṣiṇe*)—who is able to bear the violence of enemies in battle, to Indra
- देवत्तं (*devattaṃ*)—obtained through the favour of the gods
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—the hymn
- प्र गायत (*pra gāyata*)—recite with song

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests called Udgātṛs, who sing the Sāman, to Indra, who is terrible to enemies, who in battles and the like disregards the enemies and defeats them, and who is able to bear their violence, sing and recite the Sāman mantras (hymns) obtained through the favour of the gods.

##### English translation
Sing aloud (priests) to the fierce, Victorious (Indra) the overpowerer, the subduer (of foes), the praise inspired by the gods.

#### Ṛk 28

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो विश्वा॑न्य॒भि व्र॒ता सोम॑स्य॒ मदे॒ अंध॑सः ।  
> इंद्रो॑ दे॒वेषु॒ चेत॑ति ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । विश्वानि । अभि । व्रता । सोमस्य । मदे । अंधसः ।  
> इंद्रः । देवेषु । चेतति ॥ २८ ॥

### Printed p. 254

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अंधसोऽद्यमानस्य सोमस्य मदे संजाते विश्वानि सर्वाणि व्रता व्रतानि
> कर्माणि य इंद्रो देवेष्वभि चेतति ज्ञापयति तस्मा इंद्राय देवत्तं ब्रह्म
> गायतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the exhilaration that arises from the Soma-food being consumed, Indra makes known among the gods all pious acts (व्रता (*vratā*) means rites). The sense is: to that Indra sing the hymn obtained through the favour of the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—of the Soma fit to be eaten (fit to be drunk)
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—of the Soma juice
- मदे (*made*)—when exhilaration has arisen
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- व्रता (*vratā*)—deeds of valour
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods
- अभि चेतति (*abhi cetati*)—makes known; sing the Sāman to such an Indra

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Udgātṛs, when Indra is exhilarated by the Soma juice fit to be drunk, that Indra makes many deeds of valour known to the gods. Praise such an Indra by singing Sāman mantras in the form of hymns addressed to him.

##### English translation
Indra who, in the exhilaration of the quaffed Soma, makes known among the gods all pious rites.

#### Ṛk 29

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒ह त्या स॑ध॒माद्या॒ हरी॒ हिर॑ण्यकेश्या ।  
> वो॒ळ्ळाम॒भि प्रयो॑ हि॒तं ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इह । त्या । सधमाद्या । हरी इति । हिरण्यकेश्या ।  
> वोळ्ळां । अभि । प्रयः । हितं ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इह । त्या । सध्वमाद्या । हरी इति । हिरण्यकेश्या ।
> वोळ्हां । अभि । प्रयः । हितं ॥ २९ ॥
> इह यज्ञे त्या तौ प्रसिद्धौ सधमाद्या सह माद्यंतौ हिरण्यकेश्या हिरण्यकेश्यौ
> हरी अश्वा हितं हितकरं प्रयः सोमरूपमन्नमभ्यभिलक्ष्य वोळ्हां । इंद्रं
> वहतां । प्रापयतामिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, in this sacrifice, those two well-known horses of Indra, who rejoice together (सधमाद्या (*sadhamādyā*)) and are golden-maned (हिरण्यकेश्या (*hiraṇyakeśyā*)), are to bring Indra here, conveying him towards the beneficial food, that is, the food in the form of Soma; "let them carry" means let them bring Indra.

### Printed p. 255

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- त्या (*tyā*)—the well-known (two)
- सधमाद्या (*sadhamādyā*)—who are always together and rejoicing
- हिरण्यकेश्या (*hiraṇyakeśyā*)—shining with manes that glitter like gold
- हरी (*harī*)—the two horses of Indra
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—beneficial
- प्रयः अभि (*prayaḥ abhi*)—towards the food in the form of Soma, with the desire for it (in order to eat it)
- वॊळ्तां (*vòḷtāṃ*)—let them bring Indra **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May those well-known horses of Indra, who are always together and happy, adorned with a row of hair on the neck that glitters like gold, bring Indra to this sacrificial ground, towards the food in the form of Soma.

##### English translation
May those two golden-maned steeds, together exulting, bring him hither to the salutaey (sacrificial) food.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒र्वांचं॑ त्वा पुरुष्टुत प्रि॒यमे॑धस्तुता॒ हरी॑ ।  
> सो॒म॒पेया॑य वक्षतः ॥ ३० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, praised by many, your two horses, praised by Priyamedha, are to carry you towards us for the drinking of Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुषत (*puruṣata*)—O Indra, praised by many
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- प्रियमेधस्तुता (*priyamedhastutā*)—praised by me, who am named Priyamedha
- हरी (*harī*)—the horses
- सोमपेयाय (*somapeyāya*)—for the drinking of Soma
- अर्वांचं (*arvāṃcaṃ*)—facing us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, praised by many people, may your horses, praised by me, who am famed by the name Priyamedha, bring you to us, facing us, for the drinking of Soma.

##### English translation
Indra, the glorified of many, let your horses, praised by Priyamedha, bring you down to drink the Soma.

## Sūkta 33 (Maṇḍala 8)
**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वयं घ त्वेत्येकोनविंशत्यृचं तृतीयं सूक्तं काण्वस्य मेध्यातिथेरार्षं
> बृहतीछंदस्कं। षोडश्याद्यास्ति स्रो गायत्र्य एकोनविंश्यनुष्टुप् । इंद्रो देवता।
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । वयं फैकोना मेध्यातिथिर्भार्हतं त्रिगायत्र्यनुष्टुबंतमिति॥
> महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये बार्हततृचाशीतावादितः पंचदशर्चः । तथैव पंचमारण्यके
> शौनकेन सूत्रते । वयं घ त्वा सुतावंत इति पंचदश नो షు त्वा नाघतश्चनेत्येतस्य
> द्विपदां चोद्धरति । ऐ. आ. ५-२-४ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने
> ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिशस्त्रे वयं घ त्वेति तृचो वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियः । तथा च सूत्रं ।
> वयं घ त्वा सुतावंतः क ईं वेद सुते सचा । आ. ७-४ । इति ॥ स्वरसाम्ययमेव
> तृचोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । वयं घ त्वा सुतावंत इति तिस्रो बृहत्यः । आ. ८-५ ।
> इति ॥ तस्मिन्नेव शस्त्रे क ईं वेदेति वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रमुक्तमेव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning वयं घ त्वा (*vayaṃ gha tvā*) is the third hymn, of nineteen Ṛks, with Medhyātithi Kāṇva as seer, in the Bṛhatī metre; the three Ṛks beginning with the sixteenth are Gāyatrī, and the nineteenth is an Anuṣṭubh. Indra is the deity. The Anukramaṇī says the same: Medhyātithi, Bārhata, three Gāyatrīs, ending with an Anuṣṭubh. Use: in the Mahāvrata, in the Niṣkevalya, the first fifteen Ṛks are used as Bārhata tṛcas **NOTE**. Śaunaka states this in the fifth Āraṇyaka (Ai. Ā. 5-2-4) **NOTE**. On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, in the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's recitation, the three Ṛks beginning वयं घ त्वा (*vayaṃ gha tvā*) are an optional Stotriya tṛca; the sūtra says वयं घ त्वा सुतावंतः क ईं वेद सुते सचा (*vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvaṃtaḥ ka īṃ veda sute sacā*) (Ā. 7-4). In the same way this tṛca is the Anurūpa (the bhāṣya reads स्वरसाम्ययमेव (*svarasāmyayameva*) **NOTE**); the sūtra says वयं घ त्वा सुतावंत इति तिस्रो बृहत्यः (*vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvaṃta iti tisro bṛhatyaḥ*) (Ā. 8-5). In that same recitation the tṛca क ईं वेद (*ka īṃ veda*) is the optional Anurūpa; the sūtra has been quoted. **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This hymn, beginning वयं घ त्वा (*vayaṃ gha tvā*), is the third hymn in the fifth Anuvāka. It has nineteen Ṛks. Its seer is Medhyātithi Kāṇva; the deity is Indra; the metre is Bṛhatī, but the three Ṛks from the sixteenth onwards are in the Gāyatrī metre. The Anukramaṇī says: वयं फैकोना मेध्यातिथिर्बार्हतं त्रिगायत्र्यनुष्टुबंतं (*vayaṃ phaikonā medhyātithirbārhataṃ trigāyatryanuṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). In the Mahāvrata rite, at the time of reciting the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras, the first fifteen Ṛks of this hymn are applied to the Ṛks of Bṛhatī metre, as is expounded by the sage Śaunaka in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by the sūtra वयं घ त्वा सुतावंत इति पंचदश मो षु त्वा वाघतश्च नेत्येतस्य द्विपदां चोद्धरति (*vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvaṃta iti paṃcadaśa mo ṣu tvā vāghataśca netyetasya dvipadāṃ coddharati*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-4). In the day called Cāturviṃśika of the sacrifice, at the time of the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras that the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin has to recite, the three Ṛks beginning with वयं घ त्वा (*vayaṃ gha tvā*) are to be recited as the optional Stotriya tṛca
### Printed p. 257
as is expounded by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, वयं घ त्वा सुतावंतः क ईं वेद सुते सजा (*vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvaṃtaḥ ka īṃ veda sute sajā*) (Ā. 2-4). In the rite called स्वरसाम्मियॆंब (*svarasāmmiyèṃba*) too, these three Ṛks are to be recited as the Anurūpa tṛca, as expounded by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, वयं घ त्वा सुतावंतॆ इति तिस्रो बृहत्यः (*vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvaṃtè iti tisro bṛhatyaḥ*) (Ā. 2-5). In the śastra mantras of the same rite, the tṛca beginning क ईं वेद (*ka īṃ veda*) (the Ṛks 7 to 9 of this hymn) is to be recited as the Anurūpa tṛca; the sūtra that lays this down (Ā. 2-4) is thus indicated.

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala: 8
- Anuvāka: 5
- Sūkta: 33
- Aṣṭaka: 6
- Adhyāya: 3
- Varga: 7, 8, 9, 10
- Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 19
- Ṛṣi: Medhātithi Kāṇva
- Devatā: Indra
- Chandas: Ṛks 1 to 15 Bṛhatī; Ṛks 16 to 18 Gāyatrī; Ṛk 19 Anuṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व॒यं घ॑ त्वा सु॒तावं॑त॒ आपो॒ न वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषः ।  
> प॒वित्र॑स्य प्र॒स्रव॑णेषु वृत्रह॒न्परि॑ स्तो॒तार॑ आसते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वयं । घ । त्वा । सुतवंतः । आपः । न । वृक्तबर्हिषः ।  
> पवित्रस्य । प्रस्रवणेषु । वृत्तहन् । परि । स्तोतारः । आसते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृत्रहन्निंद्र त्वा त्वां वयं घ वयं खलु सुतवंतः सोममभिषुतवंत
> आपो नाप इव प्रवणमभिगच्छामः । पवित्रस्य सोमानां प्रस्रवणेषु व्यक्तबर्हिषः
> स्तीर्णबर्हिषः स्तोतारश्च त्वां पर्युपासते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, we, who have pressed the Soma, come to you as waters go to a slope. And at the flowing of the pure Soma, the praisers who have strewn the grass (व्यक्तबर्हिषः (*vyaktabarhiṣaḥ*), glossed स्तीर्णबर्हिषः (*stīrṇabarhiṣaḥ*), "with grass spread") sit around and attend you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra
- त्वा (*tvā*)—with reference to you
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- सुतवंतः (*sutavaṃtaḥ*)—pressing the Soma juice
- आपोन (*āpona*)—like water that flows down to a low-lying entrance
### Printed p. 258
- पवित्रस्य (*pavitrasya*)—of the pure Soma
- प्रस्रवणेषु (*prasravaṇeṣu*)—when it has been pressed and prepared; we are performing the pressing of Soma
- व्यक्तबर्हिषः (*vyaktabarhiṣaḥ*)—who have spread, as a seat for you to come and sit in the sacrifice, the cut darbha grass and prepared it
- स्तोत्रारः (*stotrāraḥ*)—the priests who are reciting hymns, attend you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, just as water flows to low ground and comes to rest, the Soma juice that we press for you flows in the sacrifice that we perform, gathers together and comes to rest in one place. When such Soma has been prepared for you, the priests, having made ready a seat of darbha grass for your coming and sitting, serve you with hymns and the like.

##### English translation
We are pouring forth to you the Soma juice like water: the praisers strewing the clipped sacred grass, worship you, slayer of Vritra, in the, streams (falling) from the filter.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्वरं॑ति त्वा सु॒ते नरो॒ वसो॑ निरे॒क उ॒क्किनः॑ ।  
> क॒दा सु॒तं तृ॑षा॒ण ओक॒ आ ग॑म॒ इंद्र॑ स्व॒ब्दीव॒ वंस॑गः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्वरंति । त्वा । सुते । नरः । वसो इति । निरेके । उक्किनः ।  
> कदा । सुतं । तृषाणः । ओकः । आ । गमः । इंद्र । स्वब्दीऽइव । वंसगः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वसो वासयितरिंद्र त्वा त्वां सुतेऽभिषुते सोमे निरेके निर्गमन
> उक्तिनो नरो नेतारः स्वरंति । शब्दायंते । अपि चेंद्रः सुतं सोमं प्रति
> तृषाणस्तृष्यन् स्वद्बीव स्वभूतशब्द इव वंसगो वननीयगमनो वृषभः शब्दं
> कुर्वन् तदौकः स्थानमागमत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vasu, bestower of dwelling, Indra, when the Soma has been pressed, at its outflow (निर्गमन (*nirgamana*), "coming forth"), the leaders, the priests who speak praises, sound your praise. And Indra, thirsty for the pressed Soma, like a bull of lovely gait that utters a roar, came to that abode (स्थानमागमत् (*sthānamāgamat*), "to the place").

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे वसो (*he vaso*)—O Indra, giver of dwelling
- सुते (*sute*)—the Soma juice, the creepers having been crushed and pressed
- निरेके (*nireke*)—as it is flowing fresh
- उक्तिनः (*uktinaḥ*)—reciting the hymns that have been spoken
- वरः (*varaḥ*)—the priests and others who take the chief parts in the sacrifice **NOTE**
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- स्वरंति (*svaraṃti*)—praise with a loud voice (such an Indra)
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—the pressed and prepared Soma juice, desiring it
- तृषाणः (*tṛṣāṇaḥ*)—being thirsty
- स्वद्व वंसगः (*svadva vaṃsagaḥ*)—bellowing like a bull
- कदा (*kadā*)—when
- ओकः (*okaḥ*)—to this place where the sacrifice is performed
- आ गमः (*ā gamaḥ*)—will he come?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, giver of dwelling, when the Soma creepers are crushed with a stone, the Soma juice that comes out of them flows. At that time the priests and sacrificers who lead the sacrifice praise you with a firm, loud voice. When will such an Indra, thirsty like a bellowing bull, come to this sacrificial place for the drinking of Soma?

##### English translation
The leaders (of rites), repeating praises, shout to you, Vasu, when the libation issues forth; when, Indra, bellowing like a bull, do you come to the dwelling thirsting for the Soma?

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कण्व॑भिर्धृष्ण॒वा धृ॒षद्वाजं॑ दर्षि सह॒स्रिणं॑ ।  
> पि॒शंग॑रूपं मघवन्वि चर्षणे म॒क्षु गोमं॑तमीमहे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कण्वभिः । धृष्णो इति । आ । धृषत् । वाजं । दर्षि । सहस्रिणं ।  
> पिशंगरूपं । मघवन् । विचर्षणे । मक्षु । गोमंतं । ईमहे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे धृष्णो धर्षकेंद्र कण्वेभिः कण्णानुद्दिश्य ॥ विभक्तिव्यत्ययः ॥ सहस्रिणं
> सहस्रसंख्याकं वाजमा दर्षि । देहि । हे मघवन्थनवन् विचर्षणे विद्रष्टरिंद्र
> धृषद्धृष्टं पिशंगरूपं गोमंतं च वाजं मक्षु शीघ्रमीमहे । याचामहे ।
> श्वामिति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O bold Indra, assailant of foes, give to the Kaṇvas (the Sanskrit has कण्वेभिः (*kaṇvebhiḥ*), glossed as "with reference to the Kaṇvas", an interchange of case) food numbering a thousand. O wealthy Indra, far-seeing, we quickly ask for food that is bold, tawny in form and rich in cattle; the word "you" is to be supplied. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे धृष्णो (*he dhṛṣṇo*)—O Indra, assailant of foes
- कण्णेभिः (*kaṇṇebhiḥ*)—with reference to the sons of the sage Kaṇva
- सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*)—numbering a thousand (much)
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- आ दर्षि (*ā darṣi*)—give
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—wealthy
- विचर्षणे (*vicarṣaṇe*)—O Indra, who sees and knows everything
- धृषक् (*dhṛṣak*)—that which gives strength
- पिशंगरूपं (*piśaṃgarūpaṃ*)—that which has ripened (matured) and turned yellow in colour
- गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)—barley
- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—quickly
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we pray to obtain from you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, assailant of foes, give to us, the descendants of the sage Kaṇva, food and eatables numbering a thousand, that is, of many kinds or in abundance. O Indra, who sees all and are wealthy, we pray to you to give us quickly barley (rice), which is nourishing, well ripened and yellow in colour.

##### English translation
Resolute (Indra) bestow abundantly upon the descendants of Kauwa thousands of viands; wise Maghavan, we earnestly solicit you for (wealth) of gold and cattle.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पा॒हि गायांध॑सो॒ मद॒ इंद्रा॑य मेध्यातिथे ।  
> यः संमि॑श्लो॒ हर्यो॒र्यः सु॒ते सचा॑ व॒ज्री रथो॑ हिर॒  ॑
> ण्ययः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पाहि । गाय । अंधसः । मदे । इंद्राय । मेध्यआतिथे !  
> यः । संमिश्लः । हर्योः । यः । सुते । सचा । वज्री । रथः । हिरण्ययः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मेध्यातिथे पाहि । सोमं पिब । अंधसः पीतस्य सोमस्य मदे तस्मा
> इंद्राय गाय । स्तोत्रं पठ च । य इंद्रो हर्योरश्वयोः संमिश्लः स्वरथे
> संमिश्लयिता । यश्च सुते सोमे सचा सहायः । य इंद्रो वज्रे । यस्य रथो
> हिरण्ययो हिरण्मयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Medhyātithi, drink the Soma. In the exhilaration of the drunk Soma, sing, that is, recite a hymn, to that Indra who joins his two horses to his own chariot; who is a companion at the pressed Soma; who bears the thunderbolt **NOTE**; and whose chariot is golden, that is, made of gold.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मेध्यातिथे (*medhyātithe*)—O Medhyātithi
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink the Soma
- अंथगः (*aṃthagaḥ*)—from the drinking of Soma
- मदे (*made*)—when satisfaction has arisen
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- हर्योः (*haryoḥ*)—his two horses

### Printed p. 261
- संमिश्लः (*saṃmiślaḥ*)—yokes to his chariot
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- सुते (*sute*)—when the Soma juice has been pressed
- सचा (*sacā*)—comes and joins with me
- वज्री (*vajrī*)—who holds the thunderbolt
- रथः (*rathaḥ*)—whose chariot
- हिरण्ययः (*hiraṇyayaḥ*)—is made of gold; to that Indra
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—to that Indra
- गाय (*gāya*)—recite a hymn

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Medhyātithi, drink the Soma. When satisfaction has arisen from the drinking of Soma, recite a hymn to that Indra who yokes his two horses to his chariot, who comes and joins us at the time of the pressing of the Soma juice, who bears the thunderbolt, and whose chariot is made of gold.

##### English translation
Drink, Medhyatthi, and in the exhilaration of the draught sing to Indra, to him who has harnessed his horses, who, when the Soma is poured out, is present, the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose chariot is of gold.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यः सु॑ष॒व्यः सु॒दक्षि॑ण इ॒नो यः सु॒क्रतु॑र्गृ॒णे ।  
> य आ॑क॒रः स॒हस्रा॒ यः श॒ताम॑घ॒ इंद्रो॒ यः पू॒र्भिदा॑रि॒तः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । सुसव्यः । सुदक्षिणः । इनः । यः । सुक्रतुः । गृणे ।  
> यॆः । आकरः । सहस्रा । यः । शतमघः । इंद्रः । यः । पूभित् । अरितः । ५॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः सुषव्यः शोभनसव्यहस्तः । यश्च सुदक्षिणः । यश्चेन ईश्वरः । नियुत्वानिन
> इतीश्वरनामसु पातात् । यश्चापि सुक्रतुः सुप्रज्ञः । सहस्रा सहस्राणां बहूनां
> यश्चाकरः कर्ता । यश्चापि शतमघो बहुधनः । यश्च पूर्भित् पुरां भेत्ता ।
> यश्चारितः पत्यृतः स्तोमान् । तथा च यास्कः । य आरितः कर्मण्यकर्मणि स्थिरः
> पत्यृतः स्तोमान् । नि. ५-१५ । इति । स इंद्रो गृणे । आस्माभिः स्तूयते च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Indra who is सुषव्यः (*suṣavyaḥ*), glossed as having a beautiful left hand; who is सुदक्षिणः (*sudakṣiṇaḥ*); who is इनः (*inaḥ*), a lord, for the word is read among the names of lords (the text says इतीश्वरनामसु पातात् (*itīśvaranāmasu pātāt*) **NOTE**); who is सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*), of good understanding; who is the maker of thousands, of many things; who is शतमघः (*śatamaghaḥ*), of much wealth; who is पूर्भित् (*pūrbhit*), the breaker of cities; and who is आरितः (*āritaḥ*), glossed पत्यृतः स्तोमान् (*patyṛtaḥ stomān*). Yāska says accordingly: य आरितः कर्मण्यकर्मणि स्थिरः पत्यृतः स्तोमान् । (*ya āritaḥ karmaṇyakarmaṇi sthiraḥ patyṛtaḥ stomān |*) (Ni. 5-15) **GLOSS** That Indra is praised by us.

### Printed p. 262

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- सुषव्यः (*suṣavyaḥ*)—who has an excellent left hand
- सुदक्षिणः (*sudakṣiṇaḥ*)—who has an excellent right hand
- इनः (*inaḥ*)—who is the lord of the world
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*)—who has excellent understanding
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- सहस्रा (*sahasrā*)—for acts of many kinds
- आकरः (*ākaraḥ*)—who is the performer
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- शतमघः (*śatamaghaḥ*)—who has manifold wealth
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- पूर्भित् (*pūrbhit*)—who destroys the cities of enemies
- अरितः (*aritaḥ*)—who is gratified by praise, Soma and the like
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—that same Indra
- गृणे (*gṛṇe*)—is praised by us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That Indra who has an excellent left hand, who has an excellent right hand, who is the lord of the world, who has excellent understanding, who is the performer of acts of many kinds, who has manifold wealth, who destroys the cities of enemies, who is gratified by praise, Soma and the like, that same Indra is praised by us.

##### English translation
He who is well-handed, both left and right, who is the lord, who is wise, the performer of numerous great acts, the giver of vast wealth, Indra, who is the demolisher of cities, who is gratified by praise, is glorified (by us).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो धृ॑षि॒तो योऽवृ॑तो॒ यो अस्ति॒ श्मश्रु॑षु श्रि॒तः ।  
> विभू॑तद्युम्न॒श्चव॑नः पुरुष्टु॒तः क्रत्वा॒ गौरि॑व शाकि॒नः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । धृषितः । यः । अवृतः । यः । अस्ति । श्मश्रुषु । श्रितः ।  
> विभूतद्युम्नः । च्यवनः । पुरुस्तुतः । क्रत्वा । गौs इव । शाकिनः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो धृषितः शत्रूणां धर्षयिता । यश्चावृतः शत्रुभिरपरिवृतः । यश्चापि
> श्मश्रुषु युद्धेषु । श्रवः श्रयंत्यस्मिन्निति व्युत्पत्तेः श्मश्रु युद्धमिति वृद्धावदंति ।

### Printed p. 263

> श्रितोऽस्ति भवति । यश्चापि विभूतम्यन्नुः प्रभूतधनः । यश्च च्यवनः सोमानां
> च्यावयिता । यश्चापि पुरुष्टुतो बहुस्तुतः । स इंद्रः क्रत्वा कर्मणा शाकिनः
> शक्तस्य यजमानस्य गौरिव यथा गौः पयसो दोग्ध्री तथा कामानां दोग्धा
> भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is the one who subdues (धृषितः (*dhṛṣitaḥ*)) enemies; the one not encircled (अवृतः (*avṛtaḥ*)) by enemies; and the one who is engaged (श्रितोऽस्ति (*śrito 'sti*), "is, exists") in battles (श्मश्रुषु (*śmaśruṣu*)): by derivation, because renown resorts to it, the word for "beard" means battle, as the elders say. He is of abundant wealth (विभूतम्यन्नुः (*vibhūtamyannuḥ*), glossed प्रभूतधनः (*prabhūtadhanaḥ*)) **NOTE**. He is the one who makes the Soma fall (च्यावयिता (*cyāvayitā*)) **NOTE**; and much praised (बहुस्तुतः (*bahustutaḥ*)). That Indra, by his act, becomes for the able sacrificer a giver of desires, as a cow is a giver of milk.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- धृषितः (*dhṛṣitaḥ*)—who beats down enemies
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- अवृतः (*avṛtaḥ*)—who is not surrounded by enemies
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- श्मश्रुषु (*śmaśruṣu*)—in battles
- श्रितः अस्ति (*śritaḥ asti*)—is engaged
- विभूतद्युम्नः (*vibhūtadyumnaḥ*)—who is possessed of very abundant wealth
- च्यवनः (*cyavanaḥ*)—who desires Soma
- पुरुष्टुतः (*puruṣṭutaḥ*)—who is praised by many (that same Indra)
- गौः इव (*gauḥ iva*)—as a cow gives milk abundantly
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—by his acts
- शाकिनः (*śākinaḥ*)—provides abundant wealth to the sacrificer who is able in rites

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That Indra who beats down enemies, who is not surrounded by enemies, who is engaged in battles, who possesses very abundant wealth, who desires Soma and is praised by many, that same Indra, as a cow gives milk abundantly, provides by his acts abundant wealth to the sacrificer who is able in rites.

##### English translation
He who is the subduer (of foes), the unresisted, practised in combats possessed of vast wealth, the demander of the libation, the praised of many who by his acts (of bounty) is like a milch cow to the competent (worshipper).

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क ईं॑ वेद सु॒ते सचा॒ पिबं॑तं॒ कद्वयो॑ दधे ।  
> अ॒यं यः पुरो॑ विभि॒नत्तोज॑सा मंदा॒नः शि॒प्र्यंध॑सः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कः । ईं । वेद । सुते । सचा । पिबंतं । कत् । वयः । दधे ।  
> अयं । यः । पुरः । विभिनत्ति । ओजसा । मंदानः । शिप्री । अंधसः ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 264

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुतेऽभिसुते सोमे सचर्त्विजा सह सोमं पिबंतमीमेनमिंद्र ।
> को वेद । वेत्ति । न कोऽपि वेत्तीत्यर्थः । कत् किं वा वयोऽन्नं दधे । धारयति ।
> योऽयमिंद्रः शिप्री हनूमानंधसः सोमेन मंदानो मंदमान ओजसा
> बलेन पुरो विभिनत्ति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the Soma has been pressed, who knows this Indra drinking the Soma together with the priests? No one knows, is the sense. What food does he hold, that is, carry? This Indra, who has fine jaws, exhilarated by the Soma, splits the cities by his might.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुते (*sute*)—when the Soma has been pressed and made ready
- सचा (*sacā*)—together with the priests
- पिबंतं (*pibaṃtaṃ*)—who drinks the Soma
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Indra
- कः (*kaḥ*)—who indeed
- वेद (*veda*)—knows
- कत् वयः (*kat vayaḥ*)—what kind of food
- दधे (*dadhe*)—Indra holds in his belly
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- शिप्री (*śiprī*)—who has excellent cheeks
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this same Indra
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—by the drinking of Soma
- मंदमानः (*maṃdamānaḥ*)—rejoicing
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—by his strength
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—the cities of enemies
- विभिनत्ति (*vibhinatti*)—splits

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the Soma has been pressed and made ready, who indeed knows this Indra, who drinks the Soma together with the priests? What kind of food does this Indra hold in his belly? This same Indra, who has excellent cheeks, rejoicing in the drinking of Soma, splits the cities of enemies by his strength.

##### English translation
Who knows him drinking with (the priests) when the Soma is effused? what food has he partaken of ? he, the handsome-jawed, who, exhilarated by the (sacrificial) beverage, destroys cities by his might.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दा॒ना मृ॒गो न वा॑र॒णः पु॑रु॒त्रा च॒रथं॑ दधे ।  
> नकि॑ष्ट्वा॒ नि य॑म॒दा सु॒ते ग॑मो म॒हांश्च॑र॒स्योज॑सा ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दाना । मृगः । न । वारणः । पुरुत्रा । चरथं । दधे ।  
> नकिः । त्वा । नि । यमत् । आ । सुते । गमः । महान् । चरसि । ओजसा ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 265

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मृग शत्रुणामन्येषको दारणोगजो दाना मदजलानीव पुरुत्रा बहुषु
> यत्नेषु चरणं चरणशीलं मदं दधे ! इंद्रो धारयति । अथ प्रत्यक्षस्तुतिः । हे
> इंद्र त्वा त्वां नकिर्नि यमत् । न कश्चिन्नियच्छति । सुते सोम आ गमः । आगच्छ ।
> महान् हि त्वमोजसा बलेन सर्वतश्चरसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seeker of enemies, the rending elephant, as with streams of rut-fluid, in many efforts holds an exhilaration that moves about: so Indra holds it. Then follows a direct praise: O Indra, no one restrains you. Come to the pressed Soma. For you are great and move about everywhere by your might.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मृगः (*mṛgaḥ*)—that seeks out hostile creatures
- वारणः न (*vāraṇaḥ na*)—an elephant
- दाना (*dānā*)—as it pours forth its rut-fluid
- पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*)—in many sacrifices
- चरथं (*carathaṃ*)—the exhilaration that is displayed
- दधे (*dadhe*)—Indra holds
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you (O Indra)
- नकिः नि यमत् (*nakiḥ ni yamat*)—no one can restrain
- सुते (*sute*)—when the Soma has been pressed and made ready
- आ गमः (*ā gamaḥ*)—be pleased to come
- महान् (*mahān*)—you, the great one
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—by your strength
- चरसि (*carasi*)—you move about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As an elephant that seeks out hostile creatures pours forth its rut-fluid, Indra holds in many sacrifices the exhilaration that is displayed. O Indra, no one can restrain you. Be pleased to come when the Soma has been pressed and made ready. You, the great one, move about by your own strength.

##### English translation
As a wild elephant emitting the dews of passion, he manifests his exhilaration in many places: no one checks you, (Indra), come to the libation; you are mighty, and go (everywhere) through your strength.

#### Ṛk 9
**NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य उ॒ग्रः सन्ननि॑ष्टृतः स्थि॒रो रणा॑य॒ संस्कृ॑तः ।  
> यदि॑ स्तो॒तुर्म॒घवा॑ शृ॒णव॒द्धवं॒ नेंद्रो॑ योष॒त्या ग॑मत्॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । उग्रः । सन् । अनिःस्तृतः। स्थिरः । रणाय । संस्कृतः ।  
> यदि । स्तोतुः । मघवा । शृणवत् । हवं । न । इंद्रः । योषति । आ । गमत् ॥

### Printed p. 266

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य उग्र उद्धूर्ण ओजस्वी ना सन् भवन्ननिष्टृतः शत्रुभिरनिस्तीर्णः स्थिरोऽचलो रणाय युद्धाय संस्कृतः शस्त्रैरलंकृतः सोमैर्वा संस्कृतः स इंद्रो
> मघवा धनवान् यदि स्तोतुर्हवमाह्वानं शृणवत् शृणोति तर्हन्यत्र न योषति ।
> न गच्छति । किंत्वा गमत् । तत्रैवागच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Indra who is fierce, mighty and vigorous, being unopposed by enemies, firm and immovable, equipped for battle, adorned with weapons or prepared with Somas; that wealthy Indra, if he hears the invocation of the praiser, then does not go elsewhere. He comes only there.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- उग्रः सन् (*ugraḥ san*)—being of exceeding strength
- अनिष्टृतः (*aniṣṭṛtaḥ*)—not withstood by enemies
- स्थिरः (*sthiraḥ*)—and immovable
- रणाय (*raṇāya*)—for battle
- संस्कृतः (*saṃskṛtaḥ*)—adorned with weapons
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—that same Indra
- मघवा (*maghavā*)—being possessed of exceeding wealth
- यदि (*yadi*)—at whatever time
- स्तोतुः (*stotuḥ*)—of the praiser
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—the invocation
- शृणवत् (*śṛṇavat*)—he hears (then)
- न योषत् (*na yoṣat*)—he certainly does not go from this place to another
- आ गमत् (*ā gamat*)—he certainly comes to this sacrificial ground

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That Indra who is of exceeding strength, not withstood by enemies, immovable and adorned with weapons for battle, that same Indra, who is possessed of exceeding wealth, at whatever time he hears the invocation of the praiser, does not then go from that place to another. He certainly comes to this sacrificial ground.

##### English translation
He who is fierce, unmoved (by foes) and firm, ready equipped for battle,—if Maghavan hears the invocation of his adorer, he will not go apart (from us) but come hither.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒त्यमि॒त्था वृषेद॑सि॒ वृष॑जूति॒र्नोऽवृ॑तः ।  
> वृषा॒ ह्यु॑ग्र शृण्वी॒षे प॑रा॒वति॒ वृषो॑ अर्वा॒वति॑ श्रु॒तः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सत्यं । इत्था । वृषा । इत् । असि । वृषजूतिः । नः । अवृतः ।  
> वृषा । हि । उग्र । शृण्वषे । परावति । वृषो इति । अर्वावति । श्रुतः ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 267

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उग्रोद्गर्णेंद्र त्वं सत्यमित्थेत्थं वृषेत्कामानां वर्षक एवासि ।
> वृषजूतिर्वृषभिरा कृष्णो नोऽस्माकमवृतः शत्रुभिरपरिवृतश्चासि । वृषा हि सेचक
> एव श्रुत्वा । श्रूयसे । परावति दूरेऽपि वृषैनार्वावति समीपेऽपि वृषा सेचक
> एव श्रुतः । वृषैनाश्रूयथाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O fierce Indra, you are truly, in this way, a showerer of desires. You are drawn to us by vigorous ones **NOTE**, and you are unencircled by enemies. For you are heard of as a showerer, as one who sprinkles: far away you are a showerer, and near by you are heard of as a showerer who sprinkles.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उग्र (*ugra*)—O Indra, of wondrous power
- इत्था (*itthā*)—in this way
- वृषेत् (*vṛṣet*)—you are a showerer of desires
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- वृषजूतिः (*vṛṣajūtiḥ*)—brought by horses
- अवृतः (*avṛtaḥ*)—you are not surrounded by enemies
- वृषा हि (*vṛṣā hi*)—you are celebrated as the giver of what is desired
- शृण्वीषे (*śṛṇvīṣe*)—you are famed
- परावति (*parāvati*)—even when in a far-off region
- आर्वावति (*ārvāvati*)—even when in a near region
- श्रुतः (*śrutaḥ*)—you are renowned as a showerer of desires

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, of wondrous power, in this way you are a showerer of desires. Brought to us by horses, you are not surrounded by enemies. Whether you are in a far-off region or in a near one, you are renowned as a showerer of desires.

##### English translation
Verily (Indra), in this manner you are the showerer (of benefits), brought by vigorous (steeds) to us, unarrested (by foes); fierce (Indra), you are celebrated as a showerer (of benefits) when afar; you are celebrated as a showerer (of benefits) when nigh.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृष॑णस्ते अ॒भीश॑वो॒ वृषा॒ कशा॑ हिर॒ण्यया ॑।  
> वृषा॒ रथो॑ मघव॒न्वृष॑णा॒ हरी॒ वृषा॒ त्वं श॑तक्रतो ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषणः । ते । अभीशवः । वृषा । कशा । हिरण्यया ।  
> वृषा । रथः । मघवन् । वृषणा । हरीइति । वृषा । त्वं । शतक्रतो इति  
> शतक्रतो ॥ ११ ॥

### Printed p. 268

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन् ते तवाभीशवो रश्मयोऽश्वरशना वृषणो वर्षितारः ।
> हिरण्ययी हिरण्मयी कशापि वृषा । रथोऽपि दृष्टा वर्षिता । हरी अश्वावपि वृषणा
> वृषणौ वर्षितारौ । हे शतक्रतो बहुप्रज्ञेंद्र त्वं च वृषा वर्षिता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maghavan, your reins (glossed as the rays, that is, the bridle-straps of the horses) are showerers, givers of the rain of desires. The golden whip too is a showerer; the chariot too is seen to be a showerer. Your two horses too are showerers. O Śatakratu, of many kinds of wisdom, you too are a showerer.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra, who are wealthy
- ते (*te*)—your
- अभीशवः (*abhīśavaḥ*)—the bridles of the horses (the reins)
- वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—are bestowers of desires
- हिरण्यया (*hiraṇyayā*)—made of gold
- कता (*katā*)—the whip
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—is a bestower of what is wished for
- रथः (*rathaḥ*)—your chariot too
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—is a bestower of what is wished for
- हरी (*harī*)—your horses too
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—are bestowers of what is wished for
- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O Indra, who perform many kinds of rites
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you too
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—are a bestower of what is wished for

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, the bridles (reins) of your horses are bestowers of desires. The golden whip too is a bestower of what is wished for. Your horses too are bestowers of what is wished for. O Indra, who perform many kinds of rites, you too are a bestower of what is wished for.

##### English translation
Showerers (of benefits) are your reins, such also is your golden whip; your chariot, Maghavan, is a showerer (of benefits), so are your two horses; and you, too, Sathakratu, are the showerer (of benefits).

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृषा॒ सोता॑ सुनोतु ते॒ वृष॑न्नृजीपि॒न्ना भ॑र ।  
> वृषा॑ दधन्वे॒ वृष॑णं न॒दीष्वा तुभ्यं॑ स्थातर्हरीणां ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषा । सोता । सुनोतु । ते । वृषन् । ऋजीपिन् । आ । भर ।  
> वृषा । दधन्ने । वृषणं । नदीषु । आ । तुभ्यं । स्थातः । हरीणां ॥ १२ ॥

### Printed p. 269

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृषन् वर्षितरिंद्र ते तव सोशाभिषवकर्ता वृषा वर्षिता सन् सुनोतु ।
> सोममभिषुणोतु । हे ऋजीपिन्नजुगमनेंद्र आ भर ! धनमस्मभ्यमाहर ।
> हरीणामश्वानामाभिमुख्येन हे स्नातरिंद्र तुभ्यं नदीपूदकेषु वृषणं वर्षितारं
> सोमं वृषा वर्षिता दधन्वे । धारितवानभिषवार्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O showering Indra, may the performer of the Soma-pressing for you, himself a showerer, press the Soma. O Indra, straight-going, bring (आ भर (*ā bhara*)) wealth to us. O Indra, who stand **NOTE** before the horses, facing them: the showerer (the sacrificer) has held, for you, for the pressing, the Soma that showers, among the waters of the rivers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषन् (*vṛṣan*)—O Indra, giver of rain
- ते (*te*)—for you
- सोता (*sotā*)—the one who presses the Soma
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—as a bestower of desires
- सुनोतु (*sunotu*)—let him press the Soma
- ऋजीपिन् (*ṛjīpin*)—O Indra, of straight course
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—come bringing wealth for us
- हरीणां (*harīṇāṃ*)—the horses
- आ (*ā*)—facing us
- स्थातः (*sthātaḥ*)—O Indra, who make them stand
- नदीषु (*nadīṣu*)—in the waters
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—the Soma that is to be mixed
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—the sacrificer, bestower of desires
- शुभ्यं (*śubhyaṃ*)—for you
- दधन्ने (*dadhanne*)—stands holding it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, giver of rain, let the sacrificer who presses the Soma for you, as a bestower of desires, press the Soma. O Indra, of straight course, come bringing wealth for us. O Indra, who make the horses stand facing me, the sacrificer, the bestower of desires, holds for you the Soma that is to be mixed with the waters.

##### English translation
Showerer (of benefits), may the offerer of the libation to you effuse the soma as a showerer ; straight-going (Indra), bring (us wealth) : arrester of your horses, the showerer (of the oblation) has prepared the bountiful Soma to be mixed with the waters for you.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> एंद्र॑ याहि पी॒तये॒ मधु॑ शविष्ठ सो॒म्यं ।  
> नायमच्छा॑ म॒घवा॑ शृ॒णव॒द्दिरो॒ ब्रह्मो॒क्षा च॑ सु॒क्रतुः॑ ॥

### Printed p. 270

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । इंद्र । याहि । पीतये । मधु । शविष्ठ । सोम्यं ।  
> न । अयं । अच्छ । मघवा । शृणवत् । गिरः । ब्रह्म । उक्था । च । सुक्रतुः ॥१३॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शविष्ठ बलवत्तमेंद्र सोम्यं सोमात्मकं मध्वमृतं पीतये
> पानाया याहि । आगच्छ । किमर्थमागमनमित्यत आह । यत आगमनमंतरेण
> मघवा धनवान् सुक्रतुः सुकर्मा शोभनप्रज्ञो वायमिंद्रो गिरः स्तुतीर्ब्रह्म
> स्तोत्राणुक्थानि च नाच्छ शृणवत् नाभिशृणोति । अत आगमनमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śaviṣṭha, most powerful Indra, come to drink the Soma, the sweet ambrosia of the nature of Soma. Why is the coming for this purpose? He answers: because without your coming, this wealthy Indra, of good deeds or of good understanding, does not hear fully the praises, the hymns and the chants. Therefore the coming is needed, is the sense.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शविष्ठ (*śaviṣṭha*)—who have exceeding strength
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सोम्य (*somya*)—in the form of Soma
- मधु (*madhu*)—the ambrosia
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—to drink
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be pleased to come (if there is no coming of yours)
- मघवा (*maghavā*)—wealthy
- सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*)—who has excellent deeds
- आयं (*āyaṃ*)—this Indra
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the praises
- उक्ता ब्रह्म चॆ (*uktā brahma cè*)—and our hymns in the form of utterances
- अच्छ (*accha*)—fully
- न शृणवत् (*na śṛṇavat*)—cannot hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra of exceeding strength, be pleased to come to drink the ambrosia in the form of Soma. If you do not come, this Indra, who is wealthy and has excellent deeds, cannot fully utter the praises and our hymns in the form of utterances.

##### English translation
Come, most powerful Indra, to drink of the Soma ambrosia, (for without coming) this Maghavan, the achiever of many exploits, hears not our praises, our chaunts, our hymns.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वहं॑तु त्वा रथे॒ष्ठा मा हर॑यो रथ॒युजः॑ ।  
> ति॒रश्चि॑द॒र्यं सव॑नानि वृत्रहन्न॒न्येषां॒ या श॑तक्रतो ॥ १४ ॥

### Printed p. 271

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वहंतु । त्वा । रथेऽस्थां । आ । हरयः । रथयुजः ।  
> तिर, । टित् । आर्यं । सवनानि । वृत्रहन् । अन्येषां । या । शतक्रतो इति  
> शतक्रतो ॥ १४ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृत्रहञ्चितक्रतो बहुप्रज्ञ रथेषां रथस्थामर्यमीश्वरं त्वा त्वां
> रथयुजो रथे युक्ता हरयोऽश्वा अन्येषां या यानि सवनानि संति तानि
> तिरस्तिरस्कुर्वंतः सवनान्यस्मदीयानि सवनान्या वहंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O slayer of Vṛtra, Śatakratu of many kinds of wisdom, the horses yoked to your chariot are to bring you, who stand in the chariot, the lord, to our pressings, putting aside whatever pressings there are of others.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—slayer of enemies
- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O Indra, who have many kinds of sacrificial rites
- रथेष्ठां (*ratheṣṭhāṃ*)—who sit in the chariot
- अर्यं (*aryaṃ*)—the lord
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- रथयुजः (*rathayujaḥ*)—yoked to the chariot
- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—the horses
- अन्वेषां (*anveṣāṃ*)—that are carried out by others
- या (*yā*)—whatever rites there are
- तिरश्चित् (*tiraścit*)—pushing them back
- सवनानि (*savanāni*)—to our sacrifice
- आ वहंतु (*ā vahaṃtu*)—let them bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, slayer of enemies, who have many kinds of sacrificial rites, may the horses yoked to the chariot bring you, who sit in the chariot and are the lord, pushing back the sacrificial rites that are carried out by others, that is, without going there, to our sacrifice.

##### English translation
Satakrutu, slayer of Vritra, let your horses, yoked to your car. bring you, the lord, riding in your chariot, (to our sacrifices), avoiding those sacrifices (offered) by others.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒स्माक॑म॒द्यांत॑मं॒ स्तोमं॑ धिष्ट महामह ।  
> अ॒स्माकं॑ ते॒ सव॑ना संतु॒ शंत॑मा॒ मदा॑य द्युक्ष सोमपाः ॥

### Printed p. 272

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्माकं । अद्य । अंतमं । स्तोमं । धिष्व । महामह ।  
> अस्माकं । ते । सवना । संतु । शंतमा । मदाय । द्युक्ष । सोमपाः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे महामह महतामपि महन् महापूज वाद्यांतममंतिकतममस्माकं
> मेध्यातिथीनां स्तोमं धिष्ट । धारय । हे द्युक्ष दीप्त सोमपाः सोमस्य
> पातरिंद्र ते तव मदाय मदार्थं सवना सवनान्यस्माकं शंतमा शंतमानि संतु ।
> भवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mahāmaha, great even among the great, of great worship, or: nearest (glossed as "nearest"), accept the praise of us, the Medhyātithis. O shining Soma-drinker Indra, may the pressings be most auspicious for us, for your exhilaration.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महामह (*mahāmaha*)—O Indra, worthy of exceeding worship
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- अंतमं (*aṃtamaṃ*)—that is nearest to you
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—of us, who belong to the family of Medhyātithi
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—the praises
- धिष्ट्व (*dhiṣṭva*)—accept
- द्युक्ष (*dyukṣa*)—who are shining
- सोमपाः (*somapāḥ*)—who drink the Soma, O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- मदाय (*madāya*)—performed for your delight
- सवना (*savanā*)—the sacrifices
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—for us
- शंतमा (*śaṃtamā*)—bringing happiness
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—let them be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, worthy of exceeding worship, at this time of the sacrifice accept (hear) the praises of us, who belong to the family of Medhyātithi and are nearest to you. O shining Indra, who drink the Soma, may our sacrifices, performed for your delight, bring happiness to us.

##### English translation
Greatest of the great, brilliant drinker of the Soma, accept to-day this our present praise; may our sacrifices be most successful in exciting your exhilaration.

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न॒हि षस्तव॒ नो मम॑ शा॒स्त्रे अ॒न्यस्य॒ रण्य॑ति ।  
> यो अ॒स्मान्वी॒र आन॑यत् ॥ १६ ॥

### Printed p. 273

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नहि । सः । तव । नो इति । मम । शास्त्रे । अन्यस्य । रण्यति ।  
> यः । आस्मान् । वीरः । आ । आनयत् ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो वीरः शूरोऽस्मानानयत् स इंद्रस्तव शास्त्रे शासने नहि रण्यति । न
> रमते । ममापि शास्त्रे शासने नो रण्यति । अन्यस्यापि शासने न रण्यति । किंतु रक्षण
> एव रमत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hero who has led us here, that Indra, does not delight in your rule (शास्त्रे (*śāstre*), glossed शासने (*śāsane*)); he does not delight in my rule either, nor in another's rule; he delights only in protection, is the sense.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वीरः (*vīraḥ*)—the hero
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- आस्मान् (*āsmān*)—us
- आनयत् (*ānayat*)—brought on the right path
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Indra
- तव (*tava*)—for you
- शास्त्रे (*śāstre*)—in the giving of harmful punishment
- नहि रण्यति (*nahi raṇyati*)—certainly takes no delight
- मम (*mama*)—in my harmful punishment
- नो (*no*)—takes no delight
- अन्यस्य (*anyasya*)—nor in injuring others who belong to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That heroic Indra who has brought us on the right path certainly takes no delight in giving you a harmful punishment. He takes no delight either in a punishment that brings me harm or in a punishment that injures others who belong to us.

##### English translation
The hero (Indra) who has (ever) guided us delights not in your punishment, nor in my, nor in that of any other.

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑श्चिद्घा॒ तद॑ब्रवीत्स्त्रि॒या अ॑शा॒स्यं मनः॑ ।  
> उ॒तो अह॒ क्रतुं॑ र॒घुं ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । चित् । घ । तत् । अब्रवीत् । स्त्रियाः । आशास्यं । मनः ।  
> उतो इति । आह । क्रतुं । रघुं ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 274

> यो मेध्यातिथेर्धनप्रदाता प्लायोगिरासंगः स पुमान् भूत्वा स्त्र्यभवत् ।
> तदा यदिंद्र उवाच तदिदमाह । तथा चाहुः ॥ प्लायोगिश्चासंगो यः स्त्री
> भूत्वा पुमानभूत् स मेध्यातिथये दानं दत्वेति । इंद्रश्चिद्देंद्रः खलु
> तदब्रवीत् । स्त्रिया मनश्चित्तमशाद्यं पुरुषेणाशिष्यं शासितुमशक्यं प्रबलत्वादिति ।
> उतो अपि च स्त्रीयाः क्रतुं प्रज्ञां रघुं लघुमाह ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Plāyogi Āsaṅga, the giver of wealth to Medhyātithi, having been a man, became a woman. Then Indra spoke what is said here. And so they say: प्लायोगिश्चासंगो यः स्त्री भूत्वा पुमानभूत् स मेध्यातिथये दानं दत्वेति । (*plāyogiścāsaṃgo yaḥ strī bhūtvā pumānabhūt sa medhyātithaye dānaṃ datveti |*) **GLOSS** Indra indeed said that: the mind of a woman cannot be ruled by a man, because of its strength **NOTE**. And he said also that her understanding is light.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्त्रियाः (*striyāḥ*)—of a woman
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—the mind
- अशास्यं (*aśāsyaṃ*)—is not to be brought under control
- इंद्रश्चित् घ (*iṃdraścit gha*)—Indra himself
- तदब्रवीत् (*tadabravīt*)—has himself said this
- उतो (*uto*)—and not only that
- क्रतुं अह (*kratuṃ aha*)—he has said also that her understanding
- रघुं (*raghuṃ*)—is of a low level

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra himself has declared that a woman's mind is not to be brought under a man's control. Not only that, he has declared also that her understanding (intelligence) is of a low level.

##### English translation
Verily Indra said that the mind of woman is not to be controlled he declared also that her intellect was small.

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सप्ति॑ चिद्वा मद॒च्युता॑ मिथु॒ना व॑हतो॒ रथं॑ ।  
> ए॒वेद्दूर्वृष्ण॒ उत्त॑रा ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सप्ति इति । चित् । घ । मदच्युता । मिथुना । वहतः । रथं ।  
> एव । इत् । धूः । वृष्णः । उत्करा ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सप्ति चिद्वेंद्रस्याश्वापि खलु मदच्युता सोमं प्रति गंताराविंद्रस्यैव रथं
> मिथुनौ वहतः । एवेदेवमेव वृष्ण इंद्रस्य रथो धूरुत्तराश्वयोरुत्तरा भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra's two horses, going to the Soma with delight, as a pair carry the chariot of Indra alone. In the same way the yoke of the chariot of the showerer Indra is the higher one of the two horses.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The horses of Indra also draw the chariot of Indra together, for the sake of the exhilarating Soma. In the same way the yoke of Indra, the creator, also rests upon the shoulders of Indra's horses. **NOTE**

##### English translation
The two horses of Indra, hastening to the exhilaration (of the Soma)
draw his chariot ; the pole of the showerer rests upon them.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒धः प॑श्यस्व॒ मोपरि॑ संत॒रां पा॑द॒कौ ह॑र ।  
> मा ते॑ कशप्ल॒कौ दृ॑श्॒यन् स्त्री हि ब्र॒ह्मा ब॒भूवि॑थ ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अधः । पश्यस्व । मा । उपरि । संतरां । पादक् । हर ।  
> मा । ते । कश्यप्लक् । दृश्यन् । स्त्री । हि । ब्रह्मा । बभूविथ ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एवमंतरिक्षादागच्छनथस्थ इंद्रः स्त्रियं संतं स्वस्मात्पुंस्वमिच्छंतं
> प्लायोगिं यदुवाच तदाह । हे प्लायोगे त्वं स्त्री सत्यधः पश्यस्व । एष स्त्रीणां
> धर्मः । उपरि मा पश्यस्व । उपरिदर्शनं स्त्रीणां धर्मो न भवति हि । पादकौ
> पादावपि संतरां संश्लिष्टौ यथा भवतस्तथा हर । यथा पुरुषो विश्लिष्टपादनिधानो भवति तथा त्वया स्त्रिया न कर्तव्यमित्यर्थः । अपि च ते कशप्लका । कशश्च प्लॆ कश्च
> कशप्लकौ । कशतिराहननकर्मा । कशप्लकावुभे अंगे मा दृशन् । पुरुषा न पश्यंतु ।
> तयोरदर्शनं वाससः सुष्टु परिधानेन भवति । अतः सुष्टु वाससा परिधानं
> कुरु । स्त्रियो ह्या गुल्फादभिसंवीता भवंतीत्यर्थः हि यस्मात्कारणाद्ब्रह्मा सन्
> स्त्री बभूविध ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Thus coming from the sky and standing on his chariot, Indra spoke to Plāyogi, who, being a woman, wished for manhood; the verse gives what he said. "O Plāyogi, you who are a woman, look downward. This is the duty of women. Do not look upward; looking upward is not the duty of women. Bring your two feet together so that they are closely joined. As a man stands with his feet set apart, so you, a woman, must not do; this is the meaning. Moreover, let the two kaśaplakas of yours not be seen. Kaśa and plaka are the two (limbs); the root kaśa has the sense of striking. Let men not see the two limbs. Their not being seen is brought about by wearing the garment well; therefore wear your garment properly, for women are wrapped (in their garments) down to the ankles; this is the meaning. And this is because you, being a Brahmā, have become a woman." **NOTE**

- अधः (*adhaḥ*)—(as befits a woman) towards the lower part

- उपरि (*upari*)—upwards
- मा (*mā*)—do not look
- पादकौ (*pādakau*)—your two feet
- संतरां (*saṃtarāṃ*)—as closely joined together

- ते (*te*)—your
- कशप्लकौ (*kaśaplakau*)—knees

- ब्रह्मा (*brahmā*)—having been in the position of a Brahman

- बभूव (*babhūva*)—you have been changed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O son of Playoga, as befits a woman, look only downward. Do not spread your gaze upward. Place your two feet closely together. Let men not see your knees. For you, having been in the position of a Brahman, have been changed into a woman.

##### English translation
Cast your eyes (son of Playoga) downwards, not upwards:-keep your
feet close together; let not (men) behold your ankles, for having been
a Brahman you have become a female.

## Sūkta 34 (Maṇḍala 8)
**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऐंद्र याहीत्यष्टादशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं काण्वस्य नीपातिथेरार्षवानुष्टुभं । षोडशाद्यास्तिस्रो गायत्र्यः । वसुरोचिषोंगिरोगोत्राः सहस्रसंख्याका
> आ यदिंद्रश्चेत्यादीनां तासां तिस्यणामृषयः । इंद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्मणं । ऐंद्र याहि द्व्यूना नीपातिथिरानुष्टुभं तृचोंतो गायत्र्यस्तं
> सहस्रं वसुरोचिषोंगिरसोपश्यन्निति ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the fourth sūkta, beginning ऐंद्र याहि (*aiṃdra yāhi*), of eighteen Ṛks. Its seer is Nīpātithi of the Kāṇva line; its metre is Anuṣṭubh, but the three Ṛks beginning with the sixteenth are Gāyatrī. The seers of those last three Ṛks, beginning with आ यदिंद्रश्च (*ā yadiṃdraśca*), are the Vasurociṣaḥ of the Aṅgirasa gotra, a thousand in number. The deity is Indra. As the Anukramaṇī says: ऐंद्र याहि द्व्यूना नीपातिथिरानुष्टुभं तृचोंतो गायत्र्यस्तं सहस्रं वसुरोचिषोंगिरसोपश्यन्निति ॥ (*aiṃdra yāhi dvyūnā nīpātithirānuṣṭubhaṃ tṛcoṃto gāyatryastaṃ sahasraṃ vasurociṣoṃgirasopaśyanniti ‖*). The application (viniyoga) is लैंगिकः (*laiṃgikaḥ*).

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning ऐंद्र याहि (*aiṃdra yāhi*) is the fourth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It contains eighteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Nīpātithi, born in the line of Kaṇva; the deity is Indra; the three Ṛks from the sixteenth onward are in the Gāyatrī metre. For the last three Ṛks of this sūkta, beginning with आ यदिंद्रश्च (*ā yadiṃdraśca*),

### Printed p. 277
the seers are the Vasurociṣaḥ, a thousand in number and born in the Aṅgirasa line. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: याहि द्यूना नीपातिथिरानुष्टुभं तृचोऽन्नो गायत्रस्तं सहस्रं वसुरोचिषोऽङ्गरसोऽपश्यन् (*yāhi dyūnā nīpātithirānuṣṭubhaṃ tṛco 'nno gāyatrastaṃ sahasraṃ vasurociṣo 'ṅgaraso 'paśyan*). The application is Laiṅgika.

Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 34. Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 3; Vargas 11, 12, 13. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 18. Seer: Ṛks 1-15, Nīpātithi Kāṇva; Ṛks 16-18, Sahasra Vasurociṣaḥ, of the Aṅgirasa line. Deity: Indra. Metre: Ṛks 1-15, Anuṣṭubh; Ṛks 16-18, Gāyatrī. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> निंद्र॑ याहि॒ हरि॑भि॒रुप॒ कण्व॑स्य सुष्टु॒तिं ।  
> दि॒वो अ॒मुष्य॒ शास॑तो॒ दिवं॑ य॒य दि॑वावसो ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । इंद्र । याहि । हरिभिः । उप । कण्वस्य । सुस्तुतिं ।  
> दिवः । अमुष्य । शासतः । दिवं । यय । दिवावसो इति दिवावसो ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र कण्वस्य सुष्टुतिं शोभनां स्तुतिं हरिभिरश्चैरुपा याहि ! दिवो
> द्युलोकं । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी । अमुष्यामुष्मिन्निंद्रे शासतः शासति ॥ विभक्तिव्यत्ययः ॥ तत्र वयं सुखमास्महे । हे दिवावसो दीप्तहविष्केंद्र दिवं स्वर्गं
> यय ! यूयं गच्छत । बहुवचनं पूजार्थं । यद्वा । हे दिवावसो दिवो
> द्युनामकममुष्यामुं लोकं शासनं कुर्वंतो यूयं दिवं स्वर्गं यय ।
> गच्छत । अत्र बहुवचनं पूजार्थमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, come with your horses to the fine praise of Kaṇva. Here दिवो (*divo*) stands for the world of heaven, the genitive being used in the sense of the accusative; and in the phrase अमुष्य (*amuṣya*) शासतः (*śāsataḥ*) the sense is that while this Indra rules, we dwell in comfort there. O Divāvasu, Indra of shining oblations, go to heaven. The plural is used in honour. Or else: O Divāvasu, you who rule this world named Div, go to heaven; here also the plural is used in honour.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- कण्वस्य (*kaṇvasya*)—of Kaṇva
- सुष्टुतिं (*suṣṭutiṃ*)—to hear the excellent praise
- हरिभिः (*haribhiḥ*)—with your horses
- उप आ याहि (*upa ā yāhi*)—be pleased to come
- अमुष्य (*amuṣya*)—this Indra
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—the world of heaven
- शासतः (*śāsataḥ*)—because he rules (we are in comfort)

### Printed p. 278
- दिवावसो (*divāvaso*)—O Indra, shining with oblations
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—to heaven
- यय (*yaya*)—return again
- Or: दिवावसो (*divāvaso*)—O Indra, shining with oblations; अमुष्य (*amuṣya*)—you; शासतः (*śāsataḥ*)—because you rule (we are in comfort)
- Or: दिवः (*divaḥ*)—named Div; अमुष्य (*amuṣya*)—this world; शासतः (*śāsataḥ*)—you who rule; दिवः (*divaḥ*)—to heaven; यय (*yaya*)—go back

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, be pleased to come with your horses to hear the excellent praise of Kaṇva. Because this Indra rules the world of heaven, we are in comfort. O Indra, shining with oblations, return again to heaven.

##### English translation
Come, Indra, with your horses to receive the praise of Kanwa; do you, ruling yonder heaven, O radiant with oblations, return thither.

> दि॒वो अ॒मुष्य॒ शास॑तो॒ दिवं॑ य॒य दि॑वावसो ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । त्वा । ग्रावा । वदन् । इह । सोमीा । घोषेण । यच्छतु ।  
> दिवः । अमुष्य । शासतः । दिवं । यय । दिवावसो इति दिवावसो ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वा त्वामिह यज्ञे ग्रावा सोमाभिषवपाषाणः सोमी
> सोमवान् वदञ्बं कुर्वन् घोषेण ध्वनिना सहा यच्छतु । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥
