- इंद्राग्निभ्यां (*iṃdrāgnibhyāṃ*)—to Indra and Agni
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—praises
- नभाकवत् (*nabhākavat*)—as Nābhāka offered
- प्र इरज्यत (*pra irajyata*)—offer
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Offer praises, as Nābhāka offered them, to Indra and Agni, who cover with their splendours the ocean that has roots seven in number and a closed door, and among whom Indra is lord by his own valour. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
Address like Nabhaka your praises to Indra and Agni, who overspread (with their lustre) the seven-rooted ocean whose gates are hidden, and of whom Indra by his might is the lord : may all our enemies perish.

> समे ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 366

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अपि । वृश्च । पुराणवत् । व्रततेऽइव । गुष्टितं । ओजः । दासस्य । दंभय ।  
> वयं । तत् । अस्य । संभृतं । वसु । इंद्रेण । वि । भजेमहि । नभंतां । अन्यके ।  
> समे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अपि च हे इंद्र पुराणवत्पत्नो यथा व्रततेरिव यथा वल्ल्या गुष्टितं
> निर्गतां शाखां वृश्चति तथा शत्रोणां वृश्च । छेदय । तदेवाह । दासस्य दासनामकस्य शत्रोरोजो बलं दंभय । नाशय । अथ परोक्षस्तुतिः । वयं नाभाका अस्य
> दासस्य संभृतं वस्वींद्रेण हेतुना वि भजेमहि । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, as an old (sickle) cuts the branch that has gone out from a creeper, so cut off the shoots of the enemies, that is, cut them off; he says the same: destroy the might of the enemy named Dāsa. Then an indirect praise: we, the Nābhākas, through Indra as the cause, would share the wealth gathered by this Dāsa. The rest is established. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- व्रततेरिव (*vratateriva*)—from the creeper
- गुष्टितं (*guṣṭitaṃ*)—the excess branch that has gone out
- पुराणवत् (*purāṇavat*)—as an old sickle cuts
- वृश्च (*vṛśca*)—cut off the shoots of the enemies
- दासस्य (*dāsasya*)—of the Asura
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—the valour
- दंभय (*daṃbhaya*)—destroy
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we, the Nābhākas
- अस्य (*asya*)—by this Asura
- संभृतं (*saṃbhṛtaṃ*)—gathered
- तत् वसु (*tat vasu*)—that wealth
- इंद्रेण (*iṃdreṇa*)—with the help of Indra
- वि भजेमहि (*vi bhajemahi*)—may we enjoy
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as an old sickle cuts the excess branch that has come out from a creeper, cut off the shoots of the enemies. Destroy the valour of the Asura. May we, the Nābhākas, enjoy with the help of Indra the wealth that was gathered by this Asura. May our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
Cut off (the foe), Indra, as an old (pruner) the protruding (branch) of a creeper; humble the strength of the Dasa; may we divide his accumulated treasure (despoiled) by Indra: may all our enemies perish.

> अत्माकेभिः । नृपतिः । वयं । ससह्याम । पृतन्यतः । वनुयाम । वनुष्यतः ।  
> नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ ७ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When these people call upon Indra and Agni in a special manner with wealth and with praise, then among them we, the Nābhākas, desiring battle, may overcome with our own men the enemies; desiring praise, may we also vanquish the enemies. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—those who

- वनुयाम (*vanuyāma*)—let us praise
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Among those sacrificers who pray to Indra and Agni in a special manner with wealth and with praise, we, the Nābhākas, confronting the enemies, let us overcome the enemies with our own heroic men. Let us praise those who love praise. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
Inasmuch as these people honour Indra and Agni with gifts and with praises, so may we, defying hosts, overcome (our foes) with our warriors ; let us praise those seeking praise: may all our enemies perish.

> या नु श्वे॒ताव॒वो दि॒व उ॒च्चरा॑त॒ उप॒ द्युभिः॑ ।

> बं॒धादमुं॑चतां॒ नभं॑तामन्य॒के स॑मे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> या । नु । श्वेत् । अवः । दिवः । उत्चरातः । उप । द्युभिः ।  
> इंद्राग्नोः । अनु । व्रतं । उहानाः । यंति । सिंधवः । यान् । सीं । बंधात् ।  
> आमुंचतां । नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> या नु यावेवेंद्राग्नी श्वेतौ श्वेतवर्णौ । सत्त्वगुणोपेतावित्यर्थः ।
> अवोऽधस्ताद्दुभिर्दिप्तिभिर्दिव उपोच्चरातः उच्चरतः तयोरेवेंद्राग्नोरुहाना हनिर्वहंतो यजमाना व्रतं कर्मानु यंति । अपि सीमिमाविंद्राग्नी
> यान्प्रसिद्धान् सिंधवः सिंधून् बंधाद्बंधनादमुंचतां । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those two, Indra and Agni, who are white, that is, endowed with the quality of sattva, rise from below to heaven with their splendours; for those two, the sacrificers who bear the oblation follow the rite, that is, the ritual act. Further, this Indra and Agni have released from bondage those well-known rivers. The rest is established.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificers who bear the oblation perform the rite for those Indra and Agni who, being white in colour, appear from the lower part and fly up with their splendours towards the heavenly world. These same Indra and Agni release the well-known rivers from the obstruction. May our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
Offering oblations, (the worshippers) approach to the worship of Indra and Agni, who are of a white complexion, and rise from below with bright rays to heaven: they verily have liberated the waters from bondage: may all our enemies perish.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, lord of bay horses, wielder of the thunderbolt, instigator: you who please, who shine, the hero, who bestow wealth, those many comparisons of you, and likewise the many praises, are such as have accomplished our understanding, that is, our wisdom. The rest is established. **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt and instigator, from you, who do what pleases, the giver of wealth, the hero and the generous giver, those exemplary gifts, such wealth and the like as make our understanding well refined, are abundant. The excellences of quality too are abundant. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, instigator (of acts), may the numerous merits, the many excellences of you, who are the bestower of affluence and of male offspring, perfect our understandings; may all our enemies perish.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praisers, refine with praises that Indra who is brilliant (tveṣa, the shining one), a distributor (sattvan, one who shares out) of riches, and ṛgmiya, that is, worthy of Ṛks, to be praised. Moreover, that Indra who by his might (ojas, strength) splits the eggs, that is, the offspring, born of the egg, of the asura named Śuṣṇa: may he conquer the celestial waters. The rest is established.

- तं (*taṃ*)—that Indra
- सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—with well-fashioned praises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praisers, refine and worship that Indra, who is radiant, a giver of wealth, and praised with Ṛks, with well-fashioned praises. Moreover, may that Indra who by his might splits the sons and the like of the asura Śuṣṇa (the eggs of Śuṣṇa) conquer the waters belonging to the celestial world. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
Animate with praises that brilliant adorable Indra, the dlstributor (of riches), who by his might breaks the eggs of Sushna : may he conquer the celestial waters : may all our enemies perish.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praisers, refine with praises that Indra who is svadhvara (of a good sacrifice), satya (imperishable), sattvan (a distributor of riches) and ṛtviya (to be worshipped in the proper season). Now follows direct address: moreover, you, Indra, who go toward the sacrifice (ohate) and split the eggs, that is, the offspring born of the egg, of Śuṣṇa, you have conquered (ajaiḥ, that is, ājaiṣīḥ) the celestial waters. The rest is established.

- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—the imperishable one

- ऋत्वियं (*ṛtviyaṃ*)—the one praised in accordance with the season

- शिशीत (*śiśīta*)—adorn with praises
- उतो नु चित् (*uto nu cit*)—moreover
- यः (*yaḥ*)—you who (O Indra)
- ओहते (*ohate*)—go toward the sacrifice
- शुष्णस्य (*śuṣṇasya*)—of Śuṣṇa
- आंडा (*āṃḍā*)—the sons and the like
- भेदति (*bhedati*)—split, such as you are
- स्वर्वतीः (*svarvatīḥ*)—of the celestial world
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- अजैः (*ajaiḥ*)—you have conquered
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praisers, adorn with praises that Indra who has a good sacrifice, is imperishable, a giver of wealth, and is praised in accordance with the season. Moreover, O Indra, you who go toward the sacrifice and split the sons and the like of Śuṣṇa (the eggs), such as you are, you have conquered the waters of the celestial world. May our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
Animate that Indra to whom sacrifice is due,—sincere, bountiful, adorable; him who breaks the eggs of Shushna ; you have conquered the celestial waters: may all our enemies perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the same Indra and Agni, for whom a new hymn of praise has been recited by me too, as by our fathers, as by Māndhātṛ, and as by the seer Aṅgiras, protect us by giving a dwelling with threefold protection. May we become lords of riches.

## Sūkta 41 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मा ऊ स्विति दशर्चमेकादशं सूक्तं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । अस्मा ऊ शु
> दश वारुणं त्विति । नाभाक ऋषिरनुवृत्तत्वात् । महापांक्तं हीत्युक्तत्वादिदमपि
> महापांक्तं । इदमादिके द्वे सूक्ते वरुणदेवत्ये ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥
> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने मैत्रावरुणशस्त्र आरंभणीयाया ऊर्ध्वं स
> क्षप इत्ययं नाभाकतृचः । सूत्रितं च । स क्षपः परि षस्वज इति मैत्रावरुणः । अ. ७-२ ।
> इति ॥ यः ककुभ इत्येतत्पृथतिको वा नाभाकतृचः । सूत्रितं च । यः ककुभो
> निधारय इति वा । आ. ७-२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning अस्मा ऊ (*asmā ū*) is the eleventh sūkta and has ten Ṛks. The Anukramaṇī says of it that the ten are addressed to Varuṇa. The seer is Nābhāka, by continuation from the preceding. As it has been said that the metre is Mahāpāṅkta, this one too is Mahāpāṅkta. This sūkta and the one after it have Varuṇa as deity. The application (viniyoga) is by inference (laiṅgika). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, in the Maitrāvaruṇa's recitation, after the Ārambhaṇīyā verses, the Nābhāka tṛca is to be recited, and it is laid down in the sūtra स क्षपः परि षस्वज इति मैत्रावरुणः (*sa kṣapaḥ pari ṣasvaja iti maitrāvaruṇaḥ*) (A. 7-2) **NOTE**. Or else the Nābhāka tṛca is the one beginning यः ककुभ (*yaḥ kakubha*); and it is laid down in the sūtra यः ककुभो निधारय इति वा (*yaḥ kakubho nidhāraya iti vā*) (A. 7-2).

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta beginning अस्मा ऊ षु (*asmā ū ṣu*) is the eleventh sūkta in the fifth Anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अस्मा ऊ षु दश वारुणं तु (*asmā ū ṣu daśa vāruṇaṃ tu*). The seer of this sūkta is Nābhāka; for this sūkta and the next sūkta Varuṇa is the deity; the metre is Mahāpaṅkti. The application is by inference. On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the midday pressing, after the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa has begun the shastra mantras that he recites, Ṛks 3-5 of this sūkta, beginning स क्षपः (*sa kṣapaḥ*), are to be recited as the Nābhāka tṛca; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, स क्षपः परि षस्वज इति मैत्रावरुणः (*sa kṣapaḥ pari ṣasvaja iti maitrāvaruṇaḥ*) (Ā. 7-2). Or else, in this matter, the tṛca beginning यः ककुभः (*yaḥ kakubhaḥ*) (Ṛks 4-6) is to be recited as the Nābhāka tṛca; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, यः ककुभो निधारय इति वा (*yaḥ kakubho nidhāraya iti vā*) (Ā. 7-2).

Sūkta 41. Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 41. Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 3; Varga 26, 27. Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 10. Seer: Yamaḥ—Nābhākaḥ Kāṣṭhaḥ **NOTE**. Deity: Varuṇā. Metre: Mahāpaṅkti.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, offer praise to this Varuṇa, who by his action protects the cattle of men as a herdsman tends cows, and who is possessed of most excellent wealth, and to the Maruts, who are most wise. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नाभाकस्य । प्रशस्तिभिः । यः । सिंधूनां । उप । उत्आये । सप्तस्वसा । सः ।  
> मध्यमः । नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तमु तमेव वरुणं समना समानया गिरा स्तुत्या स्वभिष्टौमि । पित्थणां
> मन्मभिः स्तोमैश्चाभिष्टौमि । नाभाकस्यर्षेः प्रशस्तिभिः स्तोत्रैश्चाभिष्टौमि । सिंधूनां
> स्यंदमानानां नदीनामुप समीप य उदये उद्दच्छति यश्च सप्तस्वसा स मध्यम
> इति वाग्निर्निरुच्यते । अन्यके दुर्धियः शत्रवः समे सर्वे नभंतां । मा भूवन् ॥
> तथा च यास्कः । तं स्वभिष्टौमि समानया गिरा गीत्या स्तुत्या पित्थणां च मननीयैः
> स्तोमैर्नाभाकस्य प्रशस्तिभिः । ऋषिनाभाको बभूव । यः स्यंदमानानामासामपामुपोदये सप्तस्वसारवेनमाह वाग्निः स मध्यम इति निरुच्यतेऽथैष एव
> भवति । नभंतामन्यके समे मा भूवन्नन्यके सर्वे ये नो द्विषंति दुर्धियः
> पापधियः पापसंकल्पाः । नि. १०-५ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Him, that very Varuṇa, I praise well with a common (samanā, that is, samānayā) voice of praise; and I praise with the mantras, that is, the hymns, of the fathers; and with the praises, that is, the eulogies, of the seer Nābhāka. He who rises (uddacchati) near the flowing rivers and who is saptasvasā: of him it is said that he is middle, thus Vāgni is explained **NOTE**. All our enemies, the evil-minded, may they perish; let them not be. So too Yāska (Ni. 10-5): he praises him well with a common voice, with a song of praise, and with the pleasing hymns of the fathers, with the praises of Nābhāka; Nābhāka became a seer; of him who at the rising of these flowing waters is saptasvasā, Vāgni says that he is called middle **NOTE**. May all those perish, may they not be, who hate us, the evil-minded, those of evil intent.

- समना (*samanā*)—of a single kind

- पितृणां (*pitṛṇāṃ*)—made by the fathers
- मन्मभिः च (*manmabhiḥ ca*)—and with praises I praise

- made by Nābhāka

- सिंधूनां (*siṃdhūnāṃ*)—of the flowing rivers
- उप (*upa*)—near
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- उदये (*udaye*)—rises

- मध्यमः (*madhyamaḥ*)—is described as belonging to the middle world

- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

With a common praise I praise that very Varuṇa. I praise him also with the praises made by the fathers and with the praises made by Nābhāka. He who rises near the flowing rivers, who has seven sisters, is described as belonging to the middle world. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
(I praise) with a like praise, with the praises of (my progenitors, with the eulogies of Nabhaka, that Varuna who rises up in the vicinity of the rivers. and in the midst (of them) has seven sisters : may all our enemies perish.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For this Ṛk **NOTE** Yāska has given the explanation:

तं स्वभिष्टौमि समानया गिरा गीत्या स्तुत्या पितृणां च मननीयैः स्तोमैर्नाभाकस्य प्रशस्तिभिः । ऋषिनाभाको बभूव यः स्यंदमानानामासामपामुपोदये सप्तस्वसारमेनमाह वाग्निः स मध्यम इति निरुच्यतेऽथैष एव भवति । नभंतामन्यके समे मा भूवन्यके सर्वे ये नो द्विषंति दुर्धियः पापधियः पापसंकल्पाः ॥ (*taṃ svabhiṣṭaumi samānayā girā gītyā stutyā pitṛṇāṃ ca mananīyaiḥ stomairnābhākasya praśastibhiḥ | ṛṣinābhāko babhūva yaḥ syaṃdamānānāmāsāmapāmupodaye saptasvasāramenamāha vāgniḥ sa madhyama iti nirucyate 'thaiṣa eva bhavati | nabhaṃtāmanyake same mā bhūvanyake sarve ye no dviṣaṃti durdhiyaḥ pāpadhiyaḥ pāpasaṃkalpāḥ ‖*) (Ni. 10-5)

I praise this god Varuṇa with excellent words of praise, or with words worthy of being sung. How? As our fathers and other elders formerly praised Varuṇa, with just such words, with words equal to the words of praise of those fathers, I praise him. And I also praise him with the words of praise of me, Nābhāka. Nābhāka is a seer who saw the mantras. That seer, in the atmosphere, the place of rising of the waters that flow as rivers, together with seven sisters, praises Varuṇa with words. Here Varuṇa is the deity of the middle region (the atmosphere).

### Printed p. 378

The seven sisters are the seven principal rivers such as the Gaṅgā, or the seven horses. Since Varuṇa also means the Sun, the seven horses of the Sun may be indicated here. The sense appears that Varuṇa stands in the midst of them. For the last sentence of this Ṛk, "may all our enemies perish at the same time": those of sinful tendency, that is, those always attached to evil deeds, who also hate us, the wicked ones, that is, all our enemies, may they perish at one time; such is the meaning.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Varuṇa embraces the nights (kṣapaḥ). Moreover, that Varuṇa, who is worth seeing (darśata) and of a rising, moving nature (usra), sets all around the whole universe by his māyā, that is, by his action. Further, the desiring creatures (venīḥ) increase his work (vrata) at the three times, morning, midday and evening. The rest is established.

- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they come to destruction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Varuṇa embraces the nights. That same Varuṇa, of attractive form and swift-moving, has upheld the whole world all around by his extraordinary action. The people who desire the action of that Varuṇa honour him with worship and the like at all three pressing times. May all our enemies come to destruction at the same time.

##### English translation
He embraces the nights : of goodly aspect, and quick of movement he encompasses the universe by his acts all who are desirous (of his favour) diligently offer him worship at the three diurnal rites: may all our enemies perish.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Varuṇa, who, being worth seeing above the earth, upholds the directions (kakubhaḥ), is the maker (mātā, the builder). The rest is established.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Varuṇa who, standing on the earth, with an attractive form upholds all the directions, that same Varuṇa is the maker of the world. The ancient place, accessible to us, that there is, that too is made by Varuṇa. That same Varuṇa, being the lord, protects us as a herdsman protects cattle. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

He, who visible above the earth sustains the point of the horizon, is the measurer (of the universe); that is the ancient abode of Varuna, to which we have access; he is our lord, like the keeper of cattle : may all our enemies perish

#### Ṛk 5

> नामानि वेद जानाति स वरुणः कविः प्राज्ञः सन् काव्या काव्यानि कविकर्माणि पुरु
> बहूनि रूपं द्यौरिव पुष्यति । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Varuṇa, who is the upholder of the worlds, and who knows the names of the rays (usrāṇām), the abodes of the gods, names that are hidden (apīcya) and placed in secret (guhya): that Varuṇa, being wise (kavi), cherishes the many works (kāvya) of a sage and a form, as heaven does. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Varuṇa
- भुवनानां (*bhuvanānāṃ*)—of all the worlds
- धर्ता (*dhartā*)—is the upholder
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- उस्राणां (*usrāṇāṃ*)—of the divine rays
- अपीच्या (*apīcyā*)—hidden
- गुह्या (*guhyā*)—and secret
- नामानि (*nāmāni*)—the names
- वेद (*veda*)—knows
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Varuṇa
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—being wise
- काव्या (*kāvyā*)—performing all works proper to a sage
- दौरिव (*dauriva*)—like the atmosphere
- पुरु (*puru*)—of many kinds
- रूपं (*rūpaṃ*)—a form
- पुष्यति (*puṣyati*)—assumes
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they come to destruction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Varuṇa who is the upholder of all the worlds, who knows all the names of the divine rays, hidden and secret, that same Varuṇa, being wise and performing all works proper to a sage, assumes forms of many kinds, like the atmosphere. May all our enemies come to destruction at the same time.

##### English translation
He who is the sustainer of the worlds, who knows the hidden and secret names of the (solar) rays, he is the sage who cherishes the acts of sages, as the heaven cherishes numorous forms: may all our enemies perish.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्रितं । जूती । सपर्यत । व्रजे । गावः । न । संयुजे । युजे । अश्वान् । आयुक्तत ।  
> नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्मिन्वरुणे विश्वानि सर्वाणि काव्या काव्यानि कविकर्माणि चक्रे नाभिरिव यथा
> रथस्य चक्रे नाभिस्तथा श्रिता श्रितानि तं त्रितं त्रिस्थानं वरुणं जूती जूत्या क्षिप्रं
> सपर्यत । हे मदीया जनाः परिचरत । किमर्थमित्यत आह । व्रजे गोष्ठे गावो
> न यथा गाः संयुजे संयोगार्थं सह स्थापयितुं युजे युंजंति तथास्माकमभियोगायाश्वानयुक्षत । सपत्ना युंजंति । अतस्तदुपद्रवपरिहाराय वरुणं
> परिचरतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In which Varuṇa all works of a sage (kāvya) are set, as the nave is in the wheel of a chariot, that triple-placed Varuṇa, who has three places, serve quickly (jūtī). O my people, serve him. For what purpose? He says: as in a cow-pen (vraja) cows are yoked together, that is, are made to stand together for union, so for an attack on us the adversaries (sapatnāḥ) harness horses. Therefore, to ward off their harm, serve Varuṇa: such is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चक्रे (*cakre*)—in a wheel
- नाभिरिव (*nābhiriva*)—as all the spokes rest on the nave, the middle part
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in which Varuṇa
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- काव्या (*kāvyā*)—works of a sage
- श्रिता (*śritā*)—rest
- त्रितं (*tritaṃ*)—that same Varuṇa, who pervades the three places
- जूती (*jūtī*)—quickly
- सपर्यत (*saparyata*)—worship
- व्रजे (*vraje*)—in a cow-pen
- गावो न (*gāvo na*)—as cows are all gathered together
- संयुजे (*saṃyuje*)—to join together
- युजे (*yuje*)—as they are driven together
- अश्वान् (*aśvān*)—horses
- आयुक्त (*āyukta*)—the enemies have collected
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As in a wheel all the spokes rest on the nave in the middle, so all the works of a sage rest in Varuṇa; worship quickly that same Varuṇa, who pervades the three places. The enemies have collected assembled horses, as all the cows are gathered together in a cow-pen. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
In whom all pious acts are concentrated, like the nave in the (centre of the) wheel, worship him quickly who abides in the three worlds; as men assemble the cattle in their pasture, so do (our foes) collect their horses (to assail us): may all our enemies perish.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Varuṇa
- आसु (*āsu*)—in all the directions
- अत्नः (*atnaḥ*)—moving about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Varuṇa who, moving about in all the directions, caused all the beings of these worlds to attain a state, and who goes around touching all the worlds, in front of the chariot of that same Varuṇa all the gods carry out their work. May all our enemies come to destruction at the same time.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Varuṇa, from whom the waters come to be like an ocean, is the hidden (apīcya, concealed) ocean (samudra) **NOTE**. Swift (tura), he mounts heaven as the sun mounts the sky; so he mounts nāka. Moreover, that Varuṇa who in these directions has placed the yajus, a gift to the creatures **NOTE**, that Varuṇa shatters on every side the devices (māyāḥ) of the asuras with his radiant (arcin) foot, that is, his place; the sense is: with his splendour. He mounts nāka, heaven. The rest is established.

- यॆत् (*yèt*)—which Varuṇa
- आसु (*āsu*)—in all the directions

- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Varuṇa

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That famous Varuṇa is of the form of the concealed ocean. As the swift-going sun mounts the atmosphere, Varuṇa too mounts the heavenly world. The Varuṇa who has established the sacrificial act in all the directions destroys completely the deceitful acts of the asuras by his own shining place alone, and he also mounts heaven. May our enemies perish.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of that Varuṇa who dwells (adhikṣit) in the atmosphere, the shining (śveta) bright rays (vicakṣaṇa) spread (paprathuḥ) the three earths and the three higher worlds. And so there is a mantra text: तिस्रो भूमिर्धारयन् त्रेरुत द्यून् (*tisro bhūmirdhārayan treruta dyūn*) (Ṛ. 2-27-8) **GLOSS**. The dwelling (sadaḥ) of that Varuṇa is firm, that is, immovable. Further, that Varuṇa is lord (īrajyati) of the seven rivers. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्रिः उत्तराणि (*triḥ uttarāṇi*)—the three upper worlds
- पप्रतुः (*papratuḥ*)—pervade
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—of that same Varuṇa
- सदः (*sadaḥ*)—the dwelling
- ध्रुवं (*dhruvaṃ*)—is immovable

- सप्तानां (*saptānāṃ*)—of the seven rivers
- इरज्यति (*irajyati*)—is the lord
- अन्यके समे (*anyake same*)—all our enemies
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Of the Varuṇa who dwells in the atmosphere, the white-coloured bright rays pervade the three lower worlds and the three upper worlds; the dwelling of that same Varuṇa is immovable. That same Varuṇa is the lord of the seven rivers. May all our enemies perish.

##### English translation
Of whom, present in the three worlds, the brilliant rays pervade the three realms beyond, the eternal dwelling of Varuna, he is a lord of the seven (rivers) : may all our enemies perish.

> अधारयत् । सभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 387

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो वरुणो निर्णज आत्मीयान्रश्मिन्तिवा श्वेतानधि चक्रे अधिकरोति तथा
> रात्रौ कृष्णांश्चक्रे स वरुणोऽनु व्रता कर्माणि लक्ष्मीकृत्योभयविधकर्मानुगुणं
> पूर्व्यं धामांतरिक्षं दिवं वा ममे । निर्ममे । अपि च यः स्कंभेनांतरिक्षेणाजो न यथादित्यो द्यां धारयति तथा रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावधारयत्
> विधारयति स वरुण इत्यर्थः । सिद्धमध्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Varuṇa who makes his own rays (nirṇijaḥ) white by day, and at night makes them dark; that Varuṇa, having regard to his works (vratā) in accordance with both kinds of action **NOTE**, measured out (mame, fashioned) the ancient dwelling, the atmosphere or heaven. Moreover, he who with the pillar (skambha), the atmosphere, upholds heaven and earth (rodasī), as the unborn (aja), the sun, upholds heaven; that Varuṇa, such is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋः (*ṛḥ*)—which Varuṇa
- अधिनिर्णिजः (*adhinirṇijaḥ*)—his rays
- श्वेतान् (*śvetān*)—making white by day
- चक्रे (*cakre*)—and causing to appear
- कृष्णान् (*kṛṣṇān*)—making dark at night-time
- अचः (*acaḥ*)—the sun
- द्यां न (*dyāṃ na*)—as he upholds the heavenly world
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- स्कंभेन (*skaṃbhena*)—with the pillar in the form of the atmosphere
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- व्यधारयत् (*vyadhārayat*)—upholds
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Varuṇa
- आनु व्रता (*ānu vratā*)—in accordance with his works
- पूर्व्यं धाम (*pūrvyaṃ dhāma*)—his dwelling in the form of the atmosphere
- ममे (*mame*)—has fashioned
- अन्यके समे (*anyake same*)—all our enemies
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Varuṇa who makes his rays white by day and dark at night, and who, as the sun upholds the heavenly world, upholds both heaven and earth with the pillar in the form of the atmosphere, that same Varuṇa has fashioned his dwelling in the form of the atmosphere in accordance with his works. May all our enemies perish.

##### English translation
He who in his successive functions emits his bright rays or turns them dark, first made his residence (in the firmament), and, as the unborn sun the sky, supports with the pillar (of the firmament) both heaven and earth; may all our enemies perish.

## Sūkta 42 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्तभ्यादिति षडृचं द्वादशं सूक्तं । अर्चनाना ऋषिः काणो नाभार्को वा
> ऋषिः । उत्तरे त्वर्चनानाः । आद्यस्य चस्रैष्टुभो वरुणदेवत्यो द्वितीयश्च
> आनुष्टुभोऽश्विदेवताकः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अस्तभ्यात् षळर्चनाना वा त्रैष्टुभमंत्यं वा तृचमाश्विनमानुष्टुभमहश्यदिति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ वारुणे
> पशौ हविषो याज्यास्तभ्यादिति । सूत्रितं च । अस्तभ्याद्वामसुरो विश्ववेदा
> इत्यैकादशिनाः । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥ अग्निषोमप्रणयनेऽप्येषोत्तरा परिधानीया ।
> तथा सूत्रितं । अस्तभ्याद्वामसुरो विश्ववेदा इति परिदध्यादुत्तरया वा । आ. ४-१० ।
> इति ॥ एवा वंदस्वेत्येषा वारुणे पशौ हविषोऽनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । विवा
> वंदस्व वरुणं बृहंतं तत्त्वा यामि ब्रह्मणा वंदमान इति द्वे । आ. ३-७ । सोमप्रवहण इमां धियमित्येषा परिधानीया । सूत्रितं च । इमां धियं शिक्षमाणस्य
> देवेति निहिते परिदध्यात् । आ. ४-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning अस्तभ्यात् (*astabhyāt*) is the twelfth sūkta and has six Ṛks. Arcanānā is the seer, or the Kāṇva Nābhārka **NOTE** is the seer; for the later verses it is Arcanānā. The first Ṛk is in the Triṣṭubh metre and has Varuṇa as deity; and the second is in the Anuṣṭubh metre and has the Aśvins as deity. So it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: अस्तभ्यात् षळर्चनाना वा त्रैष्टुभमंत्यं वा तृचमाश्विनमानुष्टुभमहश्यदिति ॥ (*astabhyāt ṣaḷarcanānā vā traiṣṭubhamaṃtyaṃ vā tṛcamāśvinamānuṣṭubhamahaśyaditi ‖*). The application of the sūkta (viniyoga) is by inference. In the animal offering for Varuṇa, अस्तभ्यात् (*astabhyāt*) is the yājyā of the oblation, and it is laid down in the sūtra अस्तभ्याद्वामसुरो विश्ववेदा इत्यैकादशिनाः (*astabhyādvāmasuro viśvavedā ityaikādaśināḥ*) (Ā. 3-7). In the Agniṣoma-praṇayana this Ṛk, or the following one, is the concluding (paridhānīyā) verse, and it is laid down in the sūtra अस्तभ्याद्वामसुरो विश्ववेदा इति परिदध्यादुत्तरया वा (*astabhyādvāmasuro viśvavedā iti paridadhyāduttarayā vā*) (Ā. 4-10). The Ṛk एवा वंदस्व (*evā vaṃdasva*) is the anuvākyā of the oblation in the animal offering for Varuṇa, and it is laid down in the sūtra विवा वंदस्व वरुणं बृहंतं तत्त्वा यामि ब्रह्मणा वंदमान इति द्वे । (*vivā vaṃdasva varuṇaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ tattvā yāmi brahmaṇā vaṃdamāna iti dve |*) (Ā. 3-7). In the Soma-pravahaṇa the Ṛk इमां धियं (*imāṃ dhiyaṃ*) is the concluding verse, and it is laid down in the sūtra इमां धियं शिक्षमाणस्य देवेति निहिते परिदध्यात् (*imāṃ dhiyaṃ śikṣamāṇasya deveti nihite paridadhyāt*) (Ā. 4-4).

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta beginning अस्तभ्नात् (*astabhnāt*) is the twelfth sūkta in the fifth Anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is one named Arcanānā, or the one named Nābhāka of the Kaṇva lineage is the seer; or it may also be said that for the first three Ṛks the seer is Nābhāka Kāṇva, and for the last three Ṛks the seer is Nābhāka Kāṇva or Arcanānā. For the first three Ṛks of the sūkta Varuṇa is the deity and the metre is Triṣṭup; for the last three Ṛks the Aśvin deities are the deity and the metre is Anuṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अस्तभ्नात् षळर्चनाना वा त्रैष्टुभमंत्यं वा तृचमाश्विनमानुष्टुभमपश्यत् ऎ (*astabhnāt ṣaḷarcanānā vā traiṣṭubhamaṃtyaṃ vā tṛcamāśvinamānuṣṭubhamapaśyat è*). The application of the sūkta is by inference. In the animal offering made addressed to the deity Varuṇa, when the oblation is offered, the first Ṛk of this sūkta beginning अस्तभ्नात् (*astabhnāt*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अस्तभ्नाद्दामसुरो विश्ववेदा इत्यैकादशिनाः (*astabhnāddāmasuro viśvavedā ityaikādaśināḥ*) (Ā. 3-2) **NOTE**. In the ritual act called Agniṣoma-praṇayana too this Ṛk or the following Ṛk is to be recited as the paridhānīyā, that is, the last mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अस्तभ्नाद्दामसुरो विश्ववेदा इति परिदध्यादुत्तरया वा (*astabhnāddāmasuro viśvavedā iti paridadhyāduttarayā vā*) (Ā. 4-10). In the offering of the oblation in the animal sacrifice addressed to the deity Varuṇa, the second Ṛk of this sūkta, beginning एवा वंदस्व (*evā vaṃdasva*), is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra एवा वंदस्व वरुणं बृहंतं तत्त्वा यामि ब्रह्मणा वंदॆमाना (*evā vaṃdasva varuṇaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ tattvā yāmi brahmaṇā vaṃdèmānā*)

### Printed p. 389

इति द्वे (*iti dve*) (Ā. 3-7). In the ancillary rite called Soma-pravahaṇa, the third Ṛk of this sūkta, beginning इमां धियं (*imāṃ dhiyaṃ*), is to be recited as the last mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra इमां धियं शिक्षमाणस्य देवेति निहिते परिदध्यात् (*imāṃ dhiyaṃ śikṣamāṇasya deveti nihite paridadhyāt*) (Ā. 4-4).

Sūkta 42. Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 42. Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 3; Varga 28. Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 6. Seer: 1-6. Nābhākaḥ Kāṇva Arcanānā vā. Or 1-3. Nābhākaḥ Kāṇvaḥ. 4-6. Nābhākaḥ Kāṇvaḥ Arcanānā vā. Deity: 1-3. Varuṇaḥ. 4-6. Āśvinau. Metre: 1-3. Triṣṭup. 4-6. Anuṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस्त॑भ्ना॒द्दामसु॑रो वि॒श्ववे॑दा॒ अमि॑मित वरि॒माणं॑ पृथि॒व्याः ।  
> आसी॑द॒द्विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि स॒म्राड्विश्वेत्तानि॒ वरु॑णस्य व्र॒तानि॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आस्तभ्नात् । द्यां । असुरः । विश्ववेदाः । अमिमात । वरिमाणं । पृथिव्या ॥  
> आ । असीदत् । विश्वा । भुवनानि । संराट् । विश्वा । इत् । तानि । वरुणस्य । व्रतानि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्ववेदा विश्वधनोऽसुरो बलवान्वरुणो द्यामस्तभ्नात् । तथा पृथिविश्च
> वरिमाणं परिमाणममिमात । चक्रे । एवं निर्मितानि विश्वा सर्वाणि भुवनानि सम्राड्भूत्वासीदच्च । अध्यतिष्ठच्च । वरुणस्य तान्येतानि व्रतानि कर्माणि विश्वेद्विस्वान्येव ।
> अतो वर्णयितुमशक्यानीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Varuṇa, who is the lord of all wealth (विश्ववेदा (*viśvavedā*)) and mighty (असुरः (*asuraḥ*)), has propped up the heaven. In the same way he has measured out the extent of the earth. Having become the sovereign of all the worlds thus fashioned, he has taken possession of them and presides over them. All these deeds of Varuṇa, without exception, are such that they cannot be described; this is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्ववेदाः (*viśvavedāḥ*)—lord of all wealth
- असुरः (*asuraḥ*)—and possessed of power, Varuṇa
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the firmament
- अस्तभ्नात् (*astabhnāt*)—has made to stand firm
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth
- परिमाणं (*parimāṇaṃ*)—the measure
- अमिमात (*amimāta*)—has fashioned
- सम्राट् (*samrāṭ*)—Varuṇa, the universal sovereign

### Printed p. 390

- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)—the worlds
- आसीदत् (*āsīdat*)—has encompassed and stands over
- विश्वेत् (*viśvet*)—all
- तानि व्रतानि (*tāni vratāni*)—those well-known deeds, all of them
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—are none other than the glory of Varuṇa

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Varuṇa, the lord of all wealth and possessed of power, has made the firmament stand firm. He has fashioned the measure of the earth. Varuṇa, the universal sovereign, has encompassed and stands over all the worlds. All those well-known deeds are none other than the glory of Varuṇa.

##### English translation
The possessor of all wealth, the powerful Varuna has fixed the heaven ; he has meted the measure of the earth ; he presides as supreme monarch over all worlds ; these all are the functions of Varuna.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वा वं॑दस्व॒ वरु॑णं बृ॒हंतं॑ नम॒स्या धीर॑म॒मृत॑स्य गो॒पां।  
> स नः॒ शर्म॑ त्रि॒वरू॑थं॒ वि यं॑सत्पा॒तं नो॑ द्यानाष्कथिवी  ॒॑
> उपस्थे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । वंदस्व । वरुणं । बृहंतं । नमस्य । धीरं । अमृतस्य । गोपां ।  
> सः । नः ! शर्म । त्रिवरूथं । वि । यंसत् । पातं । नः । द्यावापृथिवी इति ।  
> उपस्थे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे स्तोतः बृहंतं महांतं वरुणमेवैवं वंदस्व । स्तुहि । अमृतस्य
> गोपां गोपयितारं धीरं प्राज्ञं वरुणं नमस्य । नमस्कुरु च । स वरुणो
> नोऽस्मभ्यं त्रिवरूथं त्रिस्थानं शर्म गृहं वि यंसत् । प्रयच्छतु । उपस्थ उपस्थाने
> वर्तमानानोऽस्मान्दावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिप्या पातं । रक्षतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, thus praise the great Varuṇa. Reverence Varuṇa, the wise one, the guardian of the immortal. May that Varuṇa grant us a house of threefold protection, one that stands in three places. May Heaven and Earth, while we abide in their proximity, protect us.

- (O praiser) बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—the great one

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, praise the great Varuṇa himself. Reverence that same Varuṇa, the guardian of the immortal and the wise one. May that same Varuṇa provide and give us a house with threefold protection. May Heaven and Earth always protect us who are in their proximity.

##### English translation
Glorify then the mighty Varuna : reverence the wise guardian of ambrosia ; may he bestow upon us a thrice sheltering habitation : may heaven and earth preserve us abiding in their proximity

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मम क्रतुं प्रज्ञानं दक्षं च सं शिशाधि । तीक्ष्णीकुरु । यया नाना यज्ञरूपया
> विश्वा सर्वाणि दुरिता दुरितान्यति तरेम तां सुतर्माणं सुष्टु तारयित्रीं यज्ञरूपां नावमधि रुहेम । वयमारुहेम ! दुःखसागरतरणे हेतुत्पाद्यज्यो
> नौरित्यत्र व्यपदिश्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shining Varuṇa, sharpen the understanding and the skill of me who am performing this rite. By means of that which is of the form of the sacrifice we may cross all sorrows; that well-ferrying boat which is of the form of the sacrifice, may we mount it. The sacrifice is here spoken of as a boat, being the means of crossing the ocean of sorrow. **NOTE**

- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa

- यया (*yayā*)—by which
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining Varuṇa, make the knowledge and the strength of me, who am performing this sacrificial rite, full of vigour. Help us to mount this boat of the form of the sacrifice, which brings safely to the shore, by which we may cross all the afflictions that cause sorrow (to carry it out).

##### English translation

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ वां॒ ग्रावा॑णो अश्विना धी॒भिर्विस्रा॑ अचुच्यवुः ।  
> नास॑त्या॒ सोम॑पीतये॒ नभं॑तामन्य॒के स॑मे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ ! वां । ग्रावाणः । अश्विना । धीभिः । विप्राः । अचुच्यवुः ।  
> नासत्या । सोमपीतये । नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नासत्या सत्यौ सत्यप्रणीतारौ वा । तथा च यास्कः । सत्यावेव वासत्यावित्यार्णवाभः सत्यस्य प्रणीतारौ । नि. ६-१३ । इति । अश्विनाश्विनौ वां युवां सोमपीतये सोमस्य पानाय विप्राः प्राज्ञा ऋत्विजो ग्रावाणः सोमाभिषवपाषाणाश्च
> धीभिः कर्मभिः स्वस्वव्यापारैरचुच्यवुः । अभिगच्छंति । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Nāsatyas, that is, the true ones, or the leaders of truth. So Yāska says: सत्यावेव वासत्यावित्यार्णवाभः सत्यस्य प्रणीतारौ (*satyāveva vāsatyāvityārṇavābhaḥ satyasya praṇītārau*) (Ni. 6-13). O Aśvins, for your drinking of the Soma the wise priests and the pressing stones with which the Soma is pressed come up with their respective functions (धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*), by acts). The rest is established.

## Sūkta 43 (Maṇḍala 8)

**NOTE**

In the sixth Anuvāka there are six sūktas. Among them the first, beginning इमे विप्रस्येति (*ime viprasyeti*), has thirty-three Ṛks and has Agni as its deity; the seer is of the Aṅgirasa line **NOTE**. So it is said in the Anukramaṇī, and the metre is Gāyatrī; in the Āśvina-śastra, and in the Agni-related rite, two sūktas beginning with this one are recited. The sūtra says: इमे विप्रस्येति सूक्ते (*ime viprasyeti sūkte*) (Ā. 4-13). **NOTE**

In the Kārīrī and Avabhṛtha sacrifices the Ṛk of this sūkta beginning स्याप्सग्न (*syāpsagna*) **NOTE** is the anuvākyā of the first ājyabhāga offering (Ā. 2-13). For the Āgnīdhra priest at the morning pressing it is the yājyā of the prasthita offering; and it is heard in the Brāhmaṇa: उक्षान्नाय वशान्नायेत्याग्निध्रो यजति (*ukṣānnāya vaśānnāyetyāgnidhro yajati*) (Ai. Brā. 6-10). In the Agnimatī offering the Ṛk त्वं ह्यग्न (*tvaṃ hyagna*) is the yājyā (Ā. 3-13). It is used also at the kindling of the fire by friction (Ā. 2-16). In the Āgneya offering on eight potsherds for a desired object, the Ṛk beginning तुभ्यं ता अंगिरस्तम (*tubhyaṃ tā aṃgirastama*) is the anuvākyā (Ā. 2-10). When the consecrated fire departs, it is to be offered as a single oblation on the alternative of mounting the fire (Ā. 3-10). In the Agni offering on the union of lightning fire and other fires, the Ṛk beginning यदग्ने दिविजा (*yadagne divijā*) is the yājyā (Ā. 3-13). **NOTE**

In the sixth Anuvāka of the eighth Maṇḍala there are six sūktas. Among them the sūkta beginning विप्रस्य (*viprasya*) is the first. It has thirty-three Ṛks. For this sūkta Virūpa **NOTE**

### Printed p. 396

Aṅgirasa is the seer; Agni is the deity; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इमे त्रयस्त्रिंशद्विरूप अंगिरस आग्नेयं तु (*ime trayastriṃśadvirūpa aṃgirasa āgneyaṃ tu*). At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, for the Gāyatrī-metre Ṛks connected with the Āgneya rite, and for the mantras of the Āśvina-śastra, this sūkta and the next sūkta have their application; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra इमे विप्रस्येति सूक्ते (*ime viprasyeti sūkte*) (Ā. 4-13). In the Kārīrī and Avabhṛtheṣṭi sacrifices, for the first ājyabhāga, the ninth Ṛk of this sūkta, beginning अप्सुग्ये (*apsugye*) **NOTE**, is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अप्सुमंतावाज्यभागावप्पग्ये सधिष्टव (*apsumaṃtāvājyabhāgāvappagye sadhiṣṭava*) (Ā. 2-13). And the priest called Āgnīdhra is to recite this Ṛk at the time of the morning pressing as the prasthita-yājyā mantra; this is indicated by the sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa उक्षान्नाय वशान्नायेत्याग्निध्रो यजति (*ukṣānnāya vaśānnāyetyāgnidhro yajati*) (Ai. Brā. 6-10). In the Agnivatī offering the fourteenth Ṛk of this sūkta, beginning त्वं ह्यग्ने (*tvaṃ hyagne*), is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निनाग्ने त्वमस्मद्युयोध्यमीवाः (*tvaṃ hyagne agnināgne tvamasmadyuyodhyamīvāḥ*) (Ā. 3-13). This Ṛk is to be recited also in the ancillary rite called Agni-manthana (the kindling of fire by friction); this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना तं मर्जयंत सुक्रतुं (*tvaṃ hyagne agninā taṃ marjayaṃta sukratuṃ*) (Ā. 2-16). In the Āgneya offering on eight potsherds, made addressed to Agni with the words "for a desired object", the eighteenth Ṛk of this sūkta, beginning तुभ्यं ता अंगिरस्तम (*tubhyaṃ tā aṃgirastama*), is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra तुभ्यं ता अंगिरस्तमाश्याम तं काममग्ने तवोतीति कामाय (*tubhyaṃ tā aṃgirastamāśyāma taṃ kāmamagne tavotīti kāmāya*) (Ā. 2-10). When the Anvāhitāgni, that is, one who has established the Agnihotra fire, goes on a journey, at the time of the mounting (samāropaṇa) of the fire an oblation is to be offered with this Ṛk; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra तुभ्यं ता अंगिरस्तमेति वाज्याहुतिं हुत्वा समारोपयेत् (*tubhyaṃ tā aṃgirastameti vājyāhutiṃ hutvā samāropayet*) (Ā. 3-10). When the lightning fire comes into contact with other fires, the offering called Agniye-'psumatīṣṭi is to be performed; in that offering the twenty-eighth Ṛk of this sūkta, beginning यदग्ने दिविजाः (*yadagne divijāḥ*), is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra यदग्ने दिविजा अस्यग्निर्हॊर्ता न्यसीदद्यजीयान् (*yadagne divijā asyagnirhòrtā nyasīdadyajīyān*) (Ā. 3-13).

Sūkta 43. Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 43. Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 3; Varga 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35. Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 33. Seer: Virūpa Aṅgirasaḥ. Deity: Agniḥ. Metre: Gāyatrī.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These praisers of ours (स्तोमासः (*stomāsaḥ*), the praisers) send forth (ईरते (*īrate*), impel) songs of praise to Agni, who is wise (विप्रस्य (*viprasya*), learned), the creator (वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*), the ordainer), and whose sacrificer is unharmed. **NOTE**

- वेधसर् (*vedhasar*)—the creator
- अस्तृतयज्जनः (*astṛtayajjanaḥ*)—the unharmed sacrificer, that is
- आग्नेः (*āgneḥ*)—addressed to Agni
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the songs of praise
- ईरते (*īrate*)—recite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Our kinsmen, the praisers, recite songs of praise addressed to Agni, who is wise, the creator, and the unharmed sacrificer.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒रो॒का इ॑व॒ घेदह॑ ति॒ग्मा अ॑ग्ने॒ तव॒ त्विषः॑ ।  
> द॒द्भिर्वना॑नि बप्सति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अरोकाःऽइव । घु । इत् । अह । तिग्माः । अग्ने । तव । त्विषः ।  
> दत्ऽभिः । वनानि । बप्सति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने शव तिग्मास्तीक्ष्णास्तिषो दीप्तय आरोका इवारोचमानाः पशव
> इव दद्भिर्दंतैर्वनान्यरण्यानि बप्संति । भक्षयंति । घेदहेति त्रयं पूरकं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, your sharp flames, like beasts that are not shining (आरोका (*ārokā*) is explained as not shining (arocamāna)), eat up the forests with their teeth. The three words घेदह (*ghedaha*) are fillers. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 399

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- आरोका इव (*ārokā iva*)—like fierce wild animals
- दद्भिः (*dadbhiḥ*)—with their teeth
- वनानि (*vanāni*)—as they devour the plants
- तव (*tava*)—your
- तिग्माः (*tigmāḥ*)—sharp
- त्विषः (*tviṣaḥ*)—flames
- बप्सति (*bapsati*)—eat up everything
- घेदह (*ghedaha*)—this is certain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, as fierce wild animals eat up all plants such as grass with their teeth, so your sharp flames eat up everything. This is certain.

##### English translation
Your fierce flames, Agni, consume the forest, as wild animals destroy (the plants) with their teeth.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हर॑योः धू॒मके॑तवो॒ वात॑जूता॒ उप॒ द्यवि॑ ।  
> यतं॑ते॒ वृथ॑ग॒ग्नयः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हरयः । धूमकेतवः । वात्जूताः । उप । द्यवि ।  
> यतंते । वृथक् । अग्नयः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हरयो हरणशीला वातजूता वातप्रेरिता धूमकेतवो धूमध्वजा अग्नय
> उप द्यव्यंतरिक्षे वृथक् पृथग्यतंते । गच्छंति । पृथगित्यनेन सममव्ययं वृथगिति ।
> पृथगित्येव वाजसनेयिनः पठंति । वा. सं. ३३-२ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The fires that carry off, impelled by the wind, with smoke for their banner, move (यतंते (*yataṃte*), go) apart in the sky (उप द्यवि (*upa dyavi*), in the firmament). Of वृथक् (*vṛthak*) he says that it is an indeclinable equal to pṛthak; the followers of the Vājasaneya school read only pṛthak (Vā. Saṃ. 33-2).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—swift ones that carry off everything
- वातजूताः (*vātajūtāḥ*)—impelled by the wind
- धूमकेतवः (*dhūmaketavaḥ*)—having smoke as their banner
- अग्नयः (*agnayaḥ*)—transformations of Agni
- उप द्यवि (*upa dyavi*)—in the firmament
- वृथक् (*vṛthak*)—in their own individual form
- यतंते (*yataṃte*)—move about

### Printed p. 400

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The transformations of Agni, swift as to carry off everything, impelled by the wind and having smoke as their banner, move about in the firmament, each in its own individual form.

##### English translation
The consuming smoke-bannered fires, borne by the wind, spread diversely in the firmament.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ते त्ये वृथ॑ग॒ग्नय॑ इ॒द्धासः॒ सम॑दृक्षत ।  
> उ॒षसा॑मिव के॒तवः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एते । त्ये । वृथक् । अग्नयः । इद्दासः । सं । अदृक्षत ।  
> उषसां इव । केतवः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एते त्य एतेग्नयो वृथक् पृथगिद्दासोग्निहोतृभिः समिद्धाः संत उषसामिव केतव उषसां प्रज्ञापका इव समदृक्षत । सम्यग्दृश्यंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These fires, kindled separately by the Agnihotra priests, are seen clearly, like the banners of the dawns, that is, like the signs that make the dawns known.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्ये (*tye*)—those well known
- एते (*ete*)—those that are in front
- अग्नयः (*agnayaḥ*)—transformations of Agni
- वृथक् (*vṛthak*)—separately
- इद्भासः (*idbhāsaḥ*)—blazing
- उषसां (*uṣasāṃ*)—of the dawns
- केशव इव (*keśava iva*)—like banners of radiance **NOTE**
- समदृक्षत (*samadṛkṣata*)—appear shining

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The well-known transformations of Agni that are in front blaze separately and appear shining, like the banners of radiance of the dawns.

##### English translation
These fires seperately kindled are beheld like the tokens of the dawn.

### Printed p. 401

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कृ॒ष्णा रजां॑सि पत्सु॒तः प्र॒याणे॑ जा॒तवे॑दसः ।  
> अ॒ग्निर्यद्रोध॑ति॒ क्षमि॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कृष्णा । रजांसि । पत्सुतः । प्रयाने ! जातवेदसः ।  
> अग्निः यत् । रोधति । क्षमि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जातवेदसोग्नेः प्रयाणे पत्सुतः पत्तो रजांसि पांसवः कृष्णानि भवंति ।
> कदेत्यत आह । क्षमि क्षमायां यद्यदाग्नी रोधति शुष्कान्वनस्पतीन्निरुणदि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When Jātavedas, Agni, goes forth, the dust (रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)) raised by the foot becomes black. He says when: when Agni spreads on the earth and covers the dry trees.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋत् (*ṛt*)—when **NOTE**
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- क्षमि (*kṣami*)—on the earth
- रोधति (*rodhati*)—covers the dry trees; then
- जातवेदसः (*jātavedasaḥ*)—of this Agni, of the form of Jātavedas
- प्रयाणे (*prayāṇe*)—at the time of moving
- पत्सुतः (*patsutaḥ*)—that rises up
- रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)—the dust
- कष्टा (*kaṣṭā*)—is black **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When this Agni moves over the earth and covers, that is, seizes, the dry trees, then the dust that rises up at the time of the movement of this Agni, of the form of Jātavedas, is black.

##### English translation
Black dust is raised by the feet of Jathavedas when he moves, when Agni spreads on the earth.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> धा॒सिं कृ॑ष्णा॒न ओष॑धी॒र्बस्स॑द॒ग्निर्न वा॑यति ।  
> पुन॒र्यंतरु॑णी॒रपि॑ ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

### Printed p. 402

> धासिं । कृह्वानः । ओषधीः । बप्सत् । अग्निः । न । वायति ।
> पुनः । यस् । तरुणीः । आपि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निरोषधीर्धासिमन्नं । क्षुद्धासीत्यन्ननामसु पाठात् । कृण्वानः कुर्वन्
> बप्सद्भक्षयन्न वायति । न शाम्यति । पुनश्च तरुणीरोषधीरपि यन् गच्छन् भवति ।
> भक्षयितुमिति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni makes the plants his food: धासिं (*dhāsiṃ*) means food, since क्षुद्धासीत्यन्ननामसु पाठात् (*kṣuddhāsītyannanāmasu pāṭhāt*) it is read among the names of food. Devouring them (बप्सत् (*bapsat*) is explained as eating), he is not appeased (न वायति (*na vāyati*), he does not become calm); and again he goes to the young plants too, the words "in order to eat" being understood.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the plants
- धासिं (*dhāsiṃ*)—in the form of his food
- कृष्णानः (*kṛṣṇānaḥ*)—having provided himself
- बप्सन् (*bapsan*)—even though he eats them
- न वायति (*na vāyati*)—he does not attain appeasement through satisfaction
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- तरुणीः (*taruṇīḥ*)—the tender creepers too
- अपि यन् (*api yan*)—he covers in order to eat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, having provided himself with the plants as his food, even though he eats them all, does not attain appeasement through satisfaction. Again he covers the tender creepers too.

##### English translation
Making the plants his food, Agni devouring them is never satiated, but falls again upon the young (shrubs).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> जि॒ह्वाभि॒रह॒ नंन॑मद॒र्चिषा॑ जंजणा॒भव॑न् ।  
> अ॒ग्निर्वने॑षु रोचते ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जिह्वाभिः । अह । नंनमत् । अर्चिषा । जंजणाभवन् ।  
> अग्निः । वनेषु । शोचते ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 403

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निर्जिह्वाभिरव ज्वालाभिरेव नंनमद्वनस्पतीनत्यंतं नमयन्नर्चिषा तेजसा
> जंजणाभवज्वलन् । जंजणाभवन् मल्मलाभवन्निति ज्वलतिकर्मसु पाठात् ।
> वनेष्टरण्येषु रोचते । प्रकाशते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, with his tongues, that is, with his flames, bends the trees exceedingly, and blazing with his splendour (अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*), with brightness) he shines in the forests. He explains जंजणाभवन् (*jaṃjaṇābhavan*) as blazing, because it is read among the names of acts of burning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- जिह्वाभिरह (*jihvābhiraha*)—with his own tongues of the form of flames
- नंनमत् (*naṃnamat*)—bending trees and the like
- अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*)—with splendour
- जंजणाभवन् (*jaṃjaṇābhavan*)—blazing
- वनेषु (*vaneṣu*)—in the forests
- रोचते (*rocate*)—shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, with his own tongues of the form of flames, bends trees and the like, and blazing with splendour he shines in the forests.

##### English translation
Bowing down (the trees) with his tongues (of flame). and blazing with splendour, Agni shines in the forests.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒प्स्य॑ग्ने॒ सधि॒ष्टव॒ सौष॑धी॒रनु॑ रुध्यसे ।  
> गर्भे॒ सञ्चा॑यसे॒ पुनः॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अप्सनु । अग्ने । सधिः । तव । सः । ओषधीः । अनु । रुध्यसे ।  
> गर्भे । सन् । जायसे । पुनरिति ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आग्ने यस्य तवाप्सु सधिः प्रवेशस्थानं स त्वमोषधीरनु रुध्यसे ।
> अनुरुणत्सि । पुनश्च तासां भूमिष्ठानां गर्भे सन् भवञ्चयसे । प्रादुर्भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you whose place of entry is in the waters, you hold back the plants. And again, being in the womb of those that stand on the earth, you are born, that is, you appear. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- तव (*tava*)—your
- सधि (*sadhi*)—place of entry
- अप्सु (*apsu*)—is in the waters
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, such as you are
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the creepers and the like
- अनु रुध्यसे (*anu rudhyase*)—you cover

### Printed p. 404

- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- गर्भे सन् (*garbhe san*)—being in their womb
- चायसे (*cāyase*)—you are born on the earth **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, your place of entry is in the waters. You, such as you are, cover (burn) the creepers and the like, and again, being in their womb, you are born on the earth.

##### English translation
Your station, Agni, is in the waters: you cling to the plants, and becoming their embroy, are born again

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उद॑ग्ने॒ तव॒ तद्भृ॒ताद॒र्चि रो॑चत॒ आहु॑तं ।  
> निंसा॑नं जु॒ह्वो॒३॒॑ १ मुखे॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । अग्ने । तव । तत् । धृतात् । अर्चिः । रोचते । आहुतं ।  
> निंसानं । जुह्वः । मुखे ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आग्ने तव धृतादाहुतं जुह्वो होमसाधनभूतायाः स्रुचो मुखे
> निंसानं लिहानं तदर्चिरुद्रोचते । प्रकाशते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, that flame of yours, fed with the offering of ghee, licking (निंसानं (*niṃsānaṃ*) is explained as licking) at the mouth of the ladle, which is the means of the oblation, shines up.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- धृतात् (*dhṛtāt*)—with the oblation in the form of ghee
- आहुतं (*āhutaṃ*)—that has been offered the oblation
- जुह्वः (*juhvaḥ*)—of the Juhū vessel, the means of oblation
- मखे (*makhe*)—at the front part **NOTE**
- निंसानं (*niṃsānaṃ*)—and that shines clinging
- तव (*tava*)—your
- तत् अर्चिः (*tat arciḥ*)—that well-known flame
- उत् रोचते (*ut rocate*)—rises and shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, that well-known flame of yours, which has been offered the oblation with the oblation in the form of ghee and which shines clinging at the front part of the Juhū vessel, the means of oblation, rises and shines.

### Printed p. 405

##### English translation
You lustre, Agni lambent in the mouth of the ladle, shines when offered from (the oblation of) butter.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒क्त्वान्ना॑य न॒शान्न्या॑य॒ सोम॑पृष्टाय वे॒धसे॑ ।  
> सॊमैर्विभे माग्नये ! ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत्कृष्टान्याय । वज्रतन्मय । सोमसृष्टाय । नेदसे ।  
> सोम्यैः । विधेम । अग्नये ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उक्षान्नाय । उक्षान्नमवनीयं हविर्यस्यासावुषान्नः । तस्मै वशान्नाय ।
> वशान्नं यस्यासौ वशान्नः । तस्मै सोमपृष्टाय सोमघृतपृष्टाय वेधसे
> विधात्रे कामानामग्नये स्तोमैर्विभेम । परिचरेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

उक्षान्नमवनीयं हविर्यस्यासावुषान्नः (*ukṣānnamavanīyaṃ haviryasyāsāvuṣānnaḥ*): he whose oblation is the ox-food to be brought. To him, and to him whose food is the cow (वशान्नं यस्यासौ वशान्नः (*vaśānnaṃ yasyāsau vaśānnaḥ*)), whose back is moistened with Soma and ghee, the ordainer of desires, to Agni, we would do service (परिचरेम (*paricarema*)) with hymns. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उक्षान्नाय (*ukṣānnāya*)—to him whose food is the bull offered in the form of the oblation
- वशान्नाय (*vaśānnāya*)—and to him whose food is such an animal
- सोमपृष्ठाय (*somapṛṣṭhāya*)—whose back is moistened with ghee
- वेधसे (*vedhase*)—the giver of desired objects
- अग्नये (*agnaye*)—addressed to Agni
- स्तोमैः (*stomaiḥ*)—with hymns
- विधेम (*vidhema*)—let us worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let us worship with hymns Agni, whose food is the bull and the animal offered in the form of the oblation, whose back is moistened with ghee, and who is the giver of desired objects.

##### English translation
Let us adore with hymns Agni, the graanter (of desires), the eater cf the ox, the cater of the marrow, on whose back the libation is poured. **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who bring the gods to the place of sacrifice and have praiseworthy wisdom, we worship you with food in the form of the oblation and with fuel, and ask of you.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । त्वा । भृगुवत् । शुची । मनुष्यत् । अग्ने । आहुत ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शुचे स्वभावतः शुद्धाहुताग्ने त्वा त्वां भृगुवद्यथा भृगुस्तथा मनुष्यद्यथा च मनुस्तथांगिरोवच्च हवामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, pure by nature, to whom pure offerings are made, we invoke you as Bhṛgu did, as Manu did, and as Aṅgiras did.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- शुचे (*śuce*)—who are perfectly pure

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, perfectly pure and receiving the oblation, as the Bhṛgus worshipped you of old, as Manu worshipped you, and as the seer Aṅgiras worshipped you, so do we now worship you and call you for help.

Holy Agni, to whom oblations are offered, we worship you in like manner (as you have been worshipped) by Bhrigu, by Manus, by Angiras.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं ह्य॑ग्ने अ॒ग्निना॒ विप्रो॒ विप्रे॑ण॒ सन्त्स॒ता ।  
> सखा॒ सख्या॑ समि॒ध्यसे॑ ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । हि । आग्ने । अग्निना । विप्रः । विप्रेण । सन् । सता ।  
> सखा । सख्या । संइध्यसे ॥ १४ ॥

### Printed p. 408

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने विप्रो मेधावी सन् विद्यमानः सखा च त्वं विप्रेण सता सख्याग्निना
> समिध्यसे । तथा च ब्राह्मणं । त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना विप्रो विप्रेण सन्त्सतेति विप्र
> इतरो विप्र इतरः सन्नितरः सन्नितरः सखा सख्या समिध्यस इत्येष ह वा अस्य स्वः सखा ।
> ऐ. ब्रा. १-१६ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you are a sage and a friend, and you are kindled by another Agni who is likewise a sage and a friend. Sāyaṇa supports this with the Brāhmaṇa: त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना विप्रो विप्रेण सन्त्सतेति विप्र इतरो विप्र इतरः सन्नितरः सन्नितरः सखा सख्या समिध्यस इत्येष ह वा अस्य स्वः सखा । (*tvaṃ hyagne agninā vipro vipreṇa santsateti vipra itaro vipra itaraḥ sannitaraḥ sannitaraḥ sakhā sakhyā samidhyasa ityeṣa ha vā asya svaḥ sakhā |*) (Ai. Brā. 1-16). The one is a sage and the other is a sage; the one is good and the other is good; the one is a friend and the other is a friend. This, the Brāhmaṇa says, is Agni's own friend.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—being wise
- सखा च (*sakhā ca*)—and a friend
- सन् (*san*)—being
- विप्रेण (*vipreṇa*)—by one who is wise
- सख्या (*sakhyā*)—who is a friend
- सका (*sakā*)—being
- अग्निना (*agninā*)—by another Agni
- समिध्यसे हि (*samidhyase hi*)—you are kindled

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who are wise and a friend are kindled by another Agni who is also wise and a friend.

##### English translation
You, Agni, are kindled by Agni: a sage by a sage, a saint by a saint, a friend by a friend.

> अग्ने॑ वी॒रव॑ती॒मिषं॑ ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यजमानाय सहस्रिणं सहस्रसंख्याकमपरिमितं रयिं धनं वीरवतीं पुत्रपौत्रादिसहितमिषमन्नं च देहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you, the well-known one, give to the wise sacrificer who offers oblations a thousandfold, measureless wealth, and food together with sons, grandsons and the like.

- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- आशत (*āśata*)—approach (in order to please you)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, as cows eagerly enter the stall to give milk to calves bleating with hunger, so my praises approach you to please you.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रदेशेषु विश्वाः सर्वा विशः प्रजा अनु सदृज् समानदर्श्यसि आतस्त्वा त्वां समत्तु
> संग्रामेषु हवामहे । ह्वयामः ॥

O Agni, since you are the lord, you look equally upon all the peoples in many places; therefore we call you, the well-known one, in battles.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, for you alone may we, doers of good works and seers of men, pass through all days over the hard-to-cross places of sorrow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आग्ने (*āgne*)—O Agni
- ते फेत् (*te phet*)—for your worship alone
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- स्वाध्यः (*svādhyaḥ*)—possessing excellent works
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- अहा (*ahā*)—in the days
- नृ चॆक्षसः (*nṛ cèkṣasaḥ*)—possessing the excellent human power of sight
- दुर्गहा (*durgahā*)—the hard situations of sorrow
- तरंतः (*taraṃtaḥ*)—crossing
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, for your worship alone, may we, possessing excellent works and, in all days, the excellent human power of sight, be crossing the hard situations of sorrow.

##### English translation
Agni, through you, may we, skilled in sacrifices and beholding men all our days, pass through (all) difficulties.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is gladdening, dear to many, reclining at sacrifices and of purifying brightness; with heart-pleasing, gladdening hymns we beg of him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मंद्रं (*maṃdraṃ*)—the delighter
- पुरुप्रियं (*purupriyaṃ*)—dear to many
- शीरं (*śīraṃ*)—pervading the sacrificial places
- पावकशोचिषं (*pāvakaśociṣaṃ*)—possessing purifying radiance

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We praise with hymns recited wholeheartedly and causing delight Agni, who is the delighter, dear to many, pervading the sacrificial places and possessed of purifying radiance.

##### English translation
We invoke with cheerful and delightful (hymns) the gladdening Agni, dear to many, who abides in the sacrifice with purifying brilliance.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining the words शीरं पावकशोचिषं । (*śīraṃ pāvakaśociṣaṃ |*) Yāska says in his Nirukta: शीरं पावकशोचिषं । हृद्भिमंद्रेभिरीमहे ॥ ३१ ॥ अग्निं । मंद्रं । पुरुप्रियं । शीरं । पावकशोचिषं । हृत्भिः । मंद्रेभिः । ईमहे ॥ ३० ॥ मंद्रं मादनं पुरुप्रियं बहुप्रियं शीरं यज्ञेषु शयनशीलं पावकशोचिषं पावकदीप्तिमग्निं हृद्भिर्मनोहरैर्मंद्रॆर्मादनैः स्तोत्रैरीमहे । यचामहे ॥ मंद्रं—हर्षकारकनू । पुरुप्रियं—अनेकरिगॆ प्रियनू । शीरं—यज्ञप्रदेश गळल्लि व्यापिसिरुववनू । पावकशोचिषं—शुद्धिकारकवाद प्रभॆयुळ्ळवनू आद । अग्निं— अग्नियन्नु । हृद्भिः—मनःपूर्वकवागि पठितवादवू । मंद्रेभिः—हर्षवन्नुंटुमाडुवुवू आद स्तुतिगळिंद । ईमहे—स्तुतिसुत्तेवॆ. हर्षकारकनू, अनेकरिगॆ प्रियनू, यज्ञप्रदेशगळल्लि व्यापिसिरुववनू, शुद्धिकारकवाद प्रभॆयुळ्ळवनू आद अग्नियन्नु मनःपूर्वकवागि पठितवादवू, हर्षवन्नुंटुमाडुवुवू आद स्तुतिगळिंद स्तुतिसुत्तेवॆ. We invoke with cheerful and delightful (hymns) the gladdening Agni, dear to many, who abides in the sacrifice with purifying brilliance. शीरं पावकशोचिषं—ई शब्दगळ अर्थविवरणॆयन्नु माडुत्ता यास्करु तम्म निरुक्तदल्लि— शीरं पावकशोचिषं । पावकदीप्तिं । अनुशायिनमिति नाशिनमिति ना (*śīraṃ pāvakaśociṣaṃ | hṛdbhimaṃdrebhirīmahe ‖ 31 ‖ agniṃ | maṃdraṃ | purupriyaṃ | śīraṃ | pāvakaśociṣaṃ | hṛtbhiḥ | maṃdrebhiḥ | īmahe ‖ 30 ‖ maṃdraṃ mādanaṃ purupriyaṃ bahupriyaṃ śīraṃ yajñeṣu śayanaśīlaṃ pāvakaśociṣaṃ pāvakadīptimagniṃ hṛdbhirmanoharairmaṃdrèrmādanaiḥ stotrairīmahe | yacāmahe ‖ maṃdraṃ—harṣakārakanū | purupriyaṃ—anekarigè priyanū | śīraṃ—yajñapradeśa gaḷalli vyāpisiruvavanū | pāvakaśociṣaṃ—śuddhikārakavāda prabhèyuḷḷavanū āda | agniṃ— agniyannu | hṛdbhiḥ—manaḥpūrvakavāgi paṭhitavādavū | maṃdrebhiḥ—harṣavannuṃṭumāḍuvuvū āda stutigaḷiṃda | īmahe—stutisuttevè. harṣakārakanū, anekarigè priyanū, yajñapradeśagaḷalli vyāpisiruvavanū, śuddhikārakavāda prabhèyuḷḷavanū āda agniyannu manaḥpūrvakavāgi paṭhitavādavū, harṣavannuṃṭumāḍuvuvū āda stutigaḷiṃda stutisuttevè. We invoke with cheerful and delightful (hymns) the gladdening Agni, dear to many, who abides in the sacrifice with purifying brilliance. śīraṃ pāvakaśociṣaṃ—ī śabdagaḷa arthavivaraṇèyannu māḍuttā yāskaru tamma niruktadalli— śīraṃ pāvakaśociṣaṃ | pāvakadīptiṃ | anuśāyinamiti nāśinamiti nā*) (2-4-14) **NOTE**

Here शीरं (*śīraṃ*) is a name of Agni; since it describes the qualities of Agni, it is the word used to indicate Agni as शीरं (*śīraṃ*). Because he enters all beings (creatures) and abides in the form of heat, or because he pervades all creatures, it is natural to designate Agni by the word शीरं (*śīraṃ*). पावकशोचिषं (*pāvakaśociṣaṃ*) means पावकदीप्तिं (*pāvakadīptiṃ*), one who shines with an exceedingly brilliant radiance.

## Sūkta 44 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समिधाग्निमिति त्रिंशदृचं द्वितीयं सूक्तमांगिरसस्य विरूपस्यार्षं प्राग्वत्वप्रपरिभाषया गायत्रमाग्नेयं । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । समिधाग्निं त्रिंशदिति ॥
> प्रातरनुवाके गायत्रे छंदस्याश्विनशस्त्रे चेदं विनियुक्तं ॥ महाव्रते समिधाग्निमित्याद्याश्चतस्रः सामिधेन्यः । तथा च पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं । समिधाग्नमिति
> चतस्रो वैश्वकर्मण ऋषभः । ऐ. आ. ५-१-१ । इति ॥ आतिथ्यायां समिधाग्निमित्येषा
> प्रथमाज्यभागस्यानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । समिधाग्निं दुवस्यता प्यायस्तॆ समेतु
> ते । आ. ४-५ । इति ॥ अमावास्यायां प्रथमाज्यभागस्यानुवाक्या । सूत्तिके च ।
> वृधन्वंतावमावास्यायामग्निः प्रश्नेन मन्मना । आ १-५ । इति ॥ दर्शपूर्णमासॆयोराग्नॆयस्यानुवाक्याग्निर्मूर्धेत्येषा । सूत्रितं च । अग्निमूर्धा भुवो यज्ञस्य।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning समिधाग्निं (*samidhāgniṃ*) has thirty Ṛks and is the second sūkta of this Anuvāka; its seer is Virūpa the Āṅgirasa, its deity Agni, its metre Gāyatrī, by the rule that the metre is as before. So it is said in the Anukramaṇī: समिधाग्निं त्रिंशदिति (*samidhāgniṃ triṃśaditi*). It is used in the Prātaranuvāka, for the Gāyatrī metre and in the Āśvina-śastra. In the Mahāvrata the first four Ṛks, beginning समिधाग्निं (*samidhāgniṃ*), are the Sāmidhenī verses; and so it is laid down in the fifth Āraṇyaka: समिधाग्नमिति चतस्रो वैश्वकर्मण ऋषभः । (*samidhāgnamiti catasro vaiśvakarmaṇa ṛṣabhaḥ |*) (Ai. Ā. 5-1-1). In the Ātithya rite the Ṛk समिधाग्निं (*samidhāgniṃ*) is the anuvākyā of the first ājyabhāga, and the sūtra says: समिधाग्निं दुवस्यता प्यायस्तॆ समेतु ते । (*samidhāgniṃ duvasyatā pyāyastè sametu te |*) (Ā. 4-5). On the new-moon day it is the anuvākyā of the first ājyabhāga, and it is said in the sūtra: वृधन्वंतावमावास्यायामग्निः प्रश्नेन मन्मना (*vṛdhanvaṃtāvamāvāsyāyāmagniḥ praśnena manmanā*) (Ā. 1-5). In the Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa rites the Ṛk beginning Agni-mūrdhā is the anuvākyā of the Āgneya offering, and the sūtra says: अग्निमूर्धा भुवो यज्ञस्य (*agnimūrdhā bhuvo yajñasya*)

### Printed p. 425

> आ. १-६ । इति ॥ मूर्धन्वद्गुणस्याग्नेरप्येपैवानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । नित्ये मूर्धन्व
> इति ॥ पवमानेष्टिषु द्वितीयस्यामिष्टावग्नेः शुचेरनुवाक्याग्निः शुचिव्रततम
> इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च । अग्निः शुचिव्रततम उदग्ने शुचयस्तव । आ. २-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(Ā. 1-6). The same Ṛk is the anuvākyā for Agni in the character of Mūrdhanvat, and the sūtra says: नित्ये मूर्धन्व इति (*nitye mūrdhanva iti*). In the Pavamāneṣṭis, in the second offering, for Agni Śuci, the Ṛk beginning Agniḥ Śucivratatama is the anuvākyā, and the sūtra says: अग्निः शुचिव्रततम उदग्ने शुचयस्तव (*agniḥ śucivratatama udagne śucayastava*) (Ā. 2-1).

This sūkta beginning समिधाग्निं (*samidhāgniṃ*) is the second sūkta in the sixth Anuvāka. It has thirty Ṛks. Its seer is Virūpa Āṅgirasaḥ; the deity is Agni; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: समिधाग्निं त्रिंशत् (*samidhāgniṃ triṃśat*). At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, for the Ṛks of Gāyatrī metre and for the Āśvina-śastra mantras, this sūkta has its application. In the Mahāvrateṣṭi the first four Ṛks of this sūkta beginning समिधाग्निं (*samidhāgniṃ*) are to be recited as Sāmidhenī mantras; this is indicated in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by the sentence समिधाग्निमिति चतस्रो वैश्वकर्मणि ऋषभः (*samidhāgnimiti catasro vaiśvakarmaṇi ṛṣabhaḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-1-1). In the Ātithyeṣṭi the Ṛk beginning समिधाग्निं (*samidhāgniṃ*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra of the first ājyabhāga; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra समिधाग्निं दुवस्यताप्त्याय समेतु ते (*samidhāgniṃ duvasyatāptyāya sametu te*) (Ā. 4-5). In the Amāvāsyeṣṭi (Darśeṣṭi) also this Ṛk is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra of the first ājyabhāga; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra वृधन्वंतावमावास्यायामग्निः प्रश्नेन मन्मना (*vṛdhanvaṃtāvamāvāsyāyāmagniḥ praśnena manmanā*) (Ā. 1-5). In the Darśa-pūrṇamāseṣṭis the sixteenth Ṛk of this sūkta beginning अग्निमूर्धा (*agnimūrdhā*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अग्निमूर्धा भुवो यज्ञस्य (*agnimūrdhā bhuvo yajñasya*) (Ā. 1-6). In the homa addressed to Agni in the character of Mūrdhanvat this Ṛk also is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra नित्ये मूर्धन्य (*nitye mūrdhanya*). In the Pavamāneṣṭis, in the second iṣṭi, in the homa addressed to the deity Agni Śuci, the twenty-first Ṛk of this sūkta beginning अग्निः शुचिव्रततमः (*agniḥ śucivratatamaḥ*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अग्निः शुचिव्रततम उदग्ने शुचयस्तव (*agniḥ śucivratatama udagne śucayastava*) (Ā. 2-1).

Sūkta 44. Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 44. Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 3; Varga 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41. Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 30. Seer: Virūpa Aṅgirasaḥ. Deity: Agniḥ. Metre: Gāyatriḥ.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒मिधा॒ग्निं दु॑वस्यत घृ॒तैर्बो॑धय॒ताति॑थिं ।  
> आस्मि॑न्ह॒व्या जु॑होतन ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> संइधा । अग्निं । दुवस्यत । घृतैः । बोधयत । अतिथिं ।  
> आ । अस्मिन् । हव्या । जुहोतन ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋत्विजः अतिथिमतिथिवत्प्रियमग्निं समिधा दुवस्यत । परिचरत । धृतैर्दीप्तिसाधनैराज्यैर्बोधयत च । अस्मिन्समिद्देऽग्नौ हव्या हवींष्या जुहोतन ।
> आजुहुत च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O priests, serve Agni, who is dear like a guest, with fuel; awaken him with ghee, the means of kindling; and offer the oblations in him when he is kindled.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*)—worthy of honour like a guest
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- समिधा (*samidhā*)—with fuel sticks
- दुवस्यत (*duvasyata*)—worship
- घृतैः (*ghṛtaiḥ*)—with ghee, the means of kindling
- बोधयत (*bodhayata*)—cause him to blaze
- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—in this kindled Agni
- हव्या (*havyā*)—oblations
- आ जुहोतन (*ā juhotana*)—offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, worship with fuel sticks Agni, who is worthy of honour like a guest. Cause him to blaze with ghee, the means of kindling. Offer oblations in this kindled Agni.

##### English translation
Honour Agni with fuel, awaken him, the guest, with (libations of) butter ; offer the oblations in him.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ स्तोमं॑ जुषस्व मे॒ वर्ध॑स्वा॒ नेन॒ मन्म॑ना ।  
> प्रति॑ सू॒क्तानि॑ हर्य नः ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 427

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । स्तोमं । जुषस्व । मे । वर्धस्व । आनेन । मन्मना ।  
> प्रति । सुउक्तानि । हर्य । नः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने म अंगिरसस्य मम स्तोमं स्तोत्रं जुषस्व । सेवस्व । अनेन
> मन्मना मननीयेन स्तोत्रेण वर्धस्व च । नोऽस्माकं सूक्तानि प्रति हर्य ।
> कामय च !!

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Agni: accept (जुषस्व (*juṣasva*), "serve") my hymn of praise, and grow strong through this prayer, which is worthy of meditation. He also asks Agni to take pleasure in our hymns and to desire them. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- मे (*me*)—my
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—praise
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—accept
- आनेन मन्मना (*ānena manmanā*)—by this prayer, full of meditation
- वर्धस्व (*vardhasva*)—grow strong
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- सूक्तानि (*sūktāni*)—hymns
- प्रति हर्य (*prati harya*)—desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, accept my praise; grow strong through this prayer full of meditation. Desire our hymns.

##### English translation
Agni, accept my praise, be invigorated by this prayer; be favourable to our hymns.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्निं दू॒तं पु॒रो द॑धे हव्य॒वाह॒मुप॑ ब्रुवे ।  
> दे॒वा आ सा॑दयादि॒ह ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निं । मूतं । पुरः । दधे । हव्यवाहं । उप । ब्रुवे ।  
> देवान् । आ । सादयात् । इह ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 428

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दूतं देवानां हव्यवाहं हविषां वोढारं चाग्निं पुरो दधे । पुरस्करोमि । उप ब्रुवे । उपस्तौमि च । सोऽग्निरिह यज्ञे देवाना सादयत् ।
> आसादयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: I place in front (पुरो दधे (*puro dadhe*), "I put forward") Agni, the messenger of the gods and the bearer of the oblations, and I also praise him. May that Agni cause the gods to be seated here at the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दूतं (*dūtaṃ*)—the messenger of the gods
- हव्यवाहं (*havyavāhaṃ*)—the bearer of the oblations
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—in front
- दधे (*dadhe*)—I set up
- उप ब्रुवे (*upa bruve*)—I praise
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice of ours
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- आ सादयत् (*ā sādayat*)—may he cause to sit down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I set in front Agni, the messenger of the gods and the bearer of the oblations, and I praise him. May that same Agni cause the gods to sit down in this sacrifice of ours.

##### English translation
I set Agni in the front as the messager, I adore him as the bearer of the oblations ; may he cause the gods to sit down here.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्ते॑ बृ॒हंतो॑ अ॒र्चयः॑ समिधा॒नस्य॑ दीदिवः ।  
> अग्ने॑ शु॒क्रास॑ ईरते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ते । बृहंतः । अर्चयः । संइधानस्य । दीदिवः ।  
> अग्ने । शुक्रासः । ईरते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे दीदिवो दीप्ताग्ने समिधानस्य समिध्यमानस्य ते तव बृहंतो महांतः
> शुक्रासो ज्वलंतोर्चयो दीप्तय उदीरते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the radiant Agni: when you are kindled, your great, bright, blazing flames and rays rise up.

### Printed p. 429

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दीदिवः (*dīdivaḥ*)—O radiant one
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- समिधानस्य (*samidhānasya*)—who are kindled
- ते (*te*)—your
- बृहंतः (*bṛhaṃtaḥ*)—of great form
- शुक्रासः (*śukrāsaḥ*)—bright
- अर्जयः (*arjayaḥ*)—flames
- उदीरते (*udīrate*)—rise up

**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O radiant Agni, your great and bright flames rise up as you are kindled.

Brilliant Agni, as you are kindled, your great flames start blazing up .

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उप॑ त्वा जु॒हूत्वा॒३॒॑ मम॑ धृ॒ताची॑र्यंतु हर्यत ।  
> अग्ने॑ ह॒व्या जु॑षस्व नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उप । त्वा । जुह्वः । मम । घृताचीः । यंतु । हर्यत ।  
> अग्ने । हव्या । जुषस्व । नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे हर्यत कामयमानाग्ने मम मदीया धृताचीर्घृतमंचंत्यो
> जुह्वः स्रुचस्त्वा त्वामुप यंतु । नोऽस्माकं हव्या हव्यानि जुषस्व । सेवस्व च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हर्यत (*haryata*)—propitious
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- मम (*mama*)—my
- धृताचीः (*dhṛtācīḥ*)—that offer ghee
- जुह्वः (*juhvaḥ*)—ladles
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- उपयॆंतु (*upayèṃtu*)—may they approach
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- हव्या (*havyā*)—oblations
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—accept

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O propitious Agni, may my ladles that offer ghee come near you. Accept our oblations.

### Printed p. 430

Let my ladles, filled with butter, come near you, O propitious one; Agni, recive our oblations.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मं॒द्रं होता॑रमृ॒त्विजं॑ चि॒त्रभा॑नुं वि॒भाव॑सुं ।  
> अ॒ग्निमा॑ळे॒ स उ॑ श्रवत् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मंद्रं । होतारं । ऋत्विजं । चित्रभानुं । विभावसुं ।  
> अग्निं । ईळे । सः । ऊं इति । श्रवत् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मंद्रं मादनं होतारं देवानामाह्वातारमृत्विजमृतौ यष्टव्यं
> चित्रभानुं चित्रदीप्तिं विभावसुं दीप्तिधनमग्निमीळे । स्तौमि । सोऽग्निः श्रवत् ।
> अस्मदीयां स्तुतिं शृणोत्वेव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: I praise Agni, who gladdens, the Hotṛ who calls the gods, the priest to whom offering is made at the proper season, of wonderful radiance, whose wealth is brilliance. May that Agni indeed hear our praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मंद्रं (*maṃdraṃ*)—who causes delight
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—who calls the gods
- ऋत्विजं (*ṛtvijaṃ*)—worthy of worship at the times of sacrifice
- चित्रभानुं (*citrabhānuṃ*)—of attractive lustre
- विभावसुं (*vibhāvasuṃ*)—whose wealth is radiance
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- ईळे (*īḷe*)—I praise
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni
- श्रवत् (*śravat*)—may he hear our praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise Agni, who causes delight, who calls the gods, who is worthy of worship at the times of sacrifice, of attractive lustre, whose wealth is radiance. May that same Agni hear our praise.

##### English translation
I worship Agni, the exhilarating invoker (of the gods), the priest. him who shines forth with various lustre, and is rich in brilliance; may he give ear.

> अध्वराणां । अभिश्रियं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: I praise Agni, the ancient Hotṛ who calls the gods, the praiseworthy, the beloved or served, of wise action, the guest-like resort of the sacrifices (अध्वराणां (*adhvarāṇāṃ*), "of the sacrifices"). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रश्नं (*praśnaṃ*)—the ancient one
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—in the form of the Hotṛ
- ईड्यं (*īḍyaṃ*)—praiseworthy
- जुष्टं (*juṣṭaṃ*)—beloved
- कविक्रतुं (*kavikratuṃ*)—whose action is endowed with wisdom
- अध्वराणां (*adhvarāṇāṃ*)—for the sacrifices
- अभिश्रियं (*abhiśriyaṃ*)—the chief guest (the worshipful one)
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni (I praise)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise Agni, the ancient, in the form of the Hotṛ, praiseworthy, beloved, whose action is endowed with wisdom, the chief guest of the sacrifices.

(I worship) the beloved Agni, the ancient adorable invoker (of the gods), the wise, the frequenter of sacrifices.

- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—continually

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> चिकित्वान् । दैव्यं । जनं ॥ ९ ॥
