#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ त्वा॑ रं॒भं न जिव्र॑यो ररं॒भा श॑वसस्पते ।  
> उ॒श्मसि॑ त्वा स॒धस्थ॒ आ ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । त्वा । रंभं । न । जिव्रयः । ररंभ । शवसः । पते ।  
> उश्मसि । त्वा । सधस्थे । आ ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शवसस्पते बलस्य पते त्वा त्वां वयं जिव्रयो क्षीणा वृद्धा रंभं न
> दंडमिव ररंभ । रभामहे । तथा च यास्कः । आरभामहे त्वा जीर्णा इव दंडं ।
> नि. ३-२१ । अपि च त्वा त्वां सधस्थे यज्ञ उश्मसि । कामायामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O lord of strength (शवसस्पते (*śavasaspate*)), we, worn-out aged people, lean on you as on a staff (रंभं न (*raṃbhaṃ na*) means "like a staff"); ररंभ (*raraṃbha*) means "we take hold". So Yāska: आरभामहे त्वा जीर्णा इव दंडं (*ārabhāmahe tvā jīrṇā iva daṃḍaṃ*) (Ni. 3-21). And in the sacrifice we desire you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शवसस्पते (*śavasaspate*)—O Indra, protector of strength
- जिव्रयः (*jivrayaḥ*)—the aged
- रंभं नॆ (*raṃbhaṃ nè*)—as they rely on a staff
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- ररंभ (*raraṃbha*)—we rely on
- सधस्थे (*sadhasthe*)—in this sacrifice
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- उश्मसि (*uśmasi*)—we desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, lord of all strength, as the aged hold a staff, we rely on you. In this sacrifice we desire you.

##### English translation
Lord of might, we lean on you as the aged on a staff; waiting for you in the sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the meaning of the word रंभ (*raṃbha*), Yāska has given this etymology: रंभः पिनाकमिति दंडस्य । रंभ आरभंत एनं । आ त्वा रंभं न जिव्रयो ररंभ इत्यपि निगमो भवति । आरभामहे त्वा जीर्णा इव दंडं ॥ (*raṃbhaḥ pinākamiti daṃḍasya | raṃbha ārabhaṃta enaṃ | ā tvā raṃbhaṃ na jivrayo raraṃbha ityapi nigamo bhavati | ārabhāmahe tvā jīrṇā iva daṃḍaṃ ‖*) (2. 3-5). **NOTE**

### Printed p. 469

The two words रंभः (*raṃbhaḥ*) and हिनाकं (*hinākaṃ*) are synonyms denoting a staff (daṇḍa). Both words have the one meaning "staff". People hold this staff to lean on when walking; therefore the staff is called रंभ (*raṃbha*). आ त्वा रंभं न जिव्रयोः आरंभ (*ā tvā raṃbhaṃ na jivrayoḥ āraṃbha*) is the example of a Vedic sentence that supports this meaning. The meaning of this sentence is: O Indra, as the aged hold a staff to lean on when walking, so we rely on you. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ज्यो॒त्रमिंद्रा॑य गायत पुरुन्नण्॒णाय॒ सत्व॑ने ।  
> नकि॒र्यं वृ॑ण्व॒ते यु॒धि ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्तोत्रं । इंद्राय । गायत । वुरुन्नण्णाय । सत्वने ।  
> नकिः । यं । वृण्वते । युधि ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमिंद्रं युधि युद्धे नकिर्वृण्वते केऽपि न वारयंति तस्मै सत्वने
> दानशीलाय पुरुनृण्णाय बमधनायेंद्राय स्तोत्रं गायत । पठत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: Him, Indra, whom in battle (युधि (*yudhi*)) no one withstands (नकिर्वृण्वते (*nakirvṛṇvate*): none holds him back), that bountiful one (सत्वने (*satvane*): generous), पुरुनृण्णाय (*purunṛṇṇāya*) with a following word read here as बमधनाय (*bamadhanāya*) (rich), to such Indra sing (गायत (*gāyata*): recite) praise. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यं (*yaṃ*)—the Indra whom
- युधि (*yudhi*)—in battle
- नकिः वृण्वते (*nakiḥ vṛṇvate*)—none can hold back
- सत्वने (*satvane*)—the bountiful
- पुरुनृण्णाय (*purunṛṇṇāya*)—the possessor of much wealth
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—to Indra
- स्तोत्रं (*stotraṃ*)—praise
- गायत (*gāyata*)—recite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Recite praise addressed to that Indra, whom none can hold back in battle, who is bountiful and possessed of abundant wealth.

##### English translation
Sing the praise to Indra, who is rich in wealth and bountiful, whom none can stay in battle.

### Printed p. 470

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि त्वा॑ वृषभा सु॒ते सु॒तं सृ॑जामि पी॒तये॑ ।  
> तृं॒सा व्य॑श्नुही॒ मदं॑ ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । त्वा । वृषभ । सुते । सुतं । सृजामि । पीतये ।  
> तृंप । वि । अश्नुहि । मदं ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृषभेंद्र त्वा त्वां सुते सोमेऽभिषुते सति सुतमभिषुतं सोमं
> पीतये पानायाभि सृजामि । तृंप । तृष्य । मदं मदकरं व्यश्नुहि चॆ क

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, the Showerer, when Soma has been pressed (सुते (*sute*)), I pour out for you the pressed Soma for drinking (पीतये (*pītaye*)). तृंप (*tṛṃpa*): be satisfied; मदं (*madaṃ*): the exhilarating draught, व्यश्नुहि (*vyaśnuhi*) with a closing word read here as चॆ क (*cè ka*). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—O Indra, showerer of desires
- त्वा (*tvā*)—for you
- सुते (*sute*)—when Soma has been pressed
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—the pressed Soma
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—for your drinking
- अभि सृजामि (*abhi sṛjāmi*)—I offer
- तृंप (*tṛṃpa*)—be satisfied
- मदं (*madaṃ*)—the gladdening Soma
- व्यत्नुहि (*vyatnuhi*)—fill yourself

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, showerer of desires, when the Soma has been pressed for you, I offer the pressed Soma for your drinking. Be satisfied. Fill yourself with the gladdening Soma.

##### English translation
When the Soma is effused. I pour out the libation to you, Showerer (of blessings), for your drinking; satiate yourself, enjoy the exalting draught.

#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा त्वा॑ मू॒रा अ॑वि॒ष्यवो॒ मोप॒हस्वा॑न॒ आ द॑भन् ।  
> मार्कीं॑ ब्रह्म॒द्विषो॑ वनः ॥ २३ ॥

### Printed p. 471

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वः ' त्वा । मूराः । अविष्यवः । मा ! उपहस्वानः । आ । दभन् ।  
> मार्कें । ब्रह्मद्विषः । वनः ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वा त्वां मूरा मूरका मूढा मनुष्या अविष्यवः पालनकामा
> मा दभन् । मा हिंसंतु । उपहस्वान उपदसनपराश्च मा भवंतु । ब्रह्मद्विषो
> ब्राह्मणानां द्वेष्टन् माकीं वनः । मा भजेथाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, let not fools (मूरा (*mūrā*): foolish men) who desire protection (अविष्यवः (*aviṣyavaḥ*)) harm you (मा दभन् (*mā dabhan*): let them not injure); let them not be given to mockery (उपहस्वान (*upahasvāna*)). Do not favour (माकीं वनः (*mākīṃ vanaḥ*): do not take to yourself) the haters of Brahmans (ब्रह्मद्विषः (*brahmadviṣaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अविष्यवः (*aviṣyavaḥ*)—desiring protection
- मूराः (*mūrāḥ*)—the unwise
- मा आ दभन् (*mā ā dabhan*)—let them not harm
- उपहस्वानः (*upahasvānaḥ*)—those who mock you
- मा (*mā*)—let them not harm
- ब्रह्मद्विषः (*brahmadviṣaḥ*)—the Asuras who hate Brahmans
- माकीं वनः (*mākīṃ vanaḥ*)—by no means favour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, let the unwise who desire protection not harm you. Let mockers not harm you. Do not favour the Asuras who hate Brahmans.

##### English translation
Let not fools, seeking protection, nor mockers trouble you; favour not the enemies of the Brahmans.

#### Ṛk 24

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒ह त्वा॒ गोप॑रीणसा म॒हे मं॑दंतु॒ राध॑से ।  
> सरो॑ गौ॒रो यथा॑ पिब ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इह । त्वा । गोपरीणसा । महे । मंदंतु । राधसे ।  
> सरः । गौरः । यथा । पिब ॥ २४ ॥

### Printed p. 472

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वा त्वामिह यज्ञे गोपरीणसा गव्येन पयसा संमिश्रितेन
> सोमेन महे महते राधसे धनाय मंदंतु । मनुष्या मादयंतु । त्वं च
> तं सोमं यथा गौरो मृगः सरः पिबति तथा पिब ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, here in the sacrifice let men gladden you (मंदंतु (*maṃdaṃtu*): delight you) with Soma mixed with cow's milk (गोपरीणसा (*goparīṇasā*)), for great wealth (महे (*mahe*) राधसे (*rādhase*)). And you drink that Soma as the gaur, the wild animal, drinks at a lake (सरः (*saraḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- राधसे (*rādhase*)—for wealth
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- गोपरीणसा (*goparīṇasā*)—with Soma mixed with milk
- मंदंतु (*maṃdaṃtu*)—let the sacrificers satisfy
- यथा (*yathā*)—as
- गौरः (*gauraḥ*)—the gaur
- सरः (*saraḥ*)—drinks the water of a lake in thirst, so
- पिब (*piba*)—drink this Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, for the gain of great wealth let the sacrificers satisfy you in this sacrifice with Soma mixed with milk. As the gaur drinks the water of a lake in thirst, so drink this Soma.

##### English translation
Let (the worshippers) gladden you here with the Soma mixed with milk, for the attainment of great wealth; drink it as the buffalo a lake.

#### Ṛk 25

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> या वृ॑त्र॒हा प॑रा॒वति॒ सना॒ नवा॑ च चुच्यु॒वे ।  
> ता सं॒सत्तु॒ प्र वो॑चत ॥ २५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> या । वृक्रहा । परावति । सना । नवा । च । चुच्युवे ।  
> ता । संसत्सु । प्र । वोचत ॥ २५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृत्रहेंद्रः परावति दूरे या यानि सना सनातनानि नवा नवानि नूतनानि च
> धनानि चुच्युवे षेरिशवान् तानि धनानि संसत्तु यज्ञेषु सभासु वा प्रवोचत ।
> प्रब्रूते विद्वज्जनः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: Those wealths, ancient (सना (*sanā*)) and new (नवा (*navā*)), which Indra the slayer of Vṛtra (वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)) sends (चुच्युवे (*cucyuve*)) from afar (परावति (*parāvati*)), those wealths let the learned people proclaim (प्रवोचत (*pravocata*): speak forth) in sacrifices or in assemblies (संसत्तु (*saṃsattu*)). **NOTE**

### Printed p. 473

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra
- परावति (*parāvati*)—from a very distant region
- या (*yā*)—which
- सना (*sanā*)—ancient
- नवा च (*navā ca*)—and new, the riches
- चुच्युवे (*cucyuve*)—he sends
- ता (*tā*)—such riches
- संसत्तु (*saṃsattu*)—in the sacrificial assemblies
- प्र वोचत (*pra vocata*)—praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Praise in the sacrificial assemblies those riches, ancient and new, which Indra the slayer of Vṛtra sends from a very distant region.

##### English translation
Proclaim in our assemblies those perpetual and ever new riches which the slayer of Vritra sends from afar.

#### Ṛk 26

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> असि॑बत्क॒द्रुवः॑ सु॒तमिंद्रः॑ स॒हस्र॑बाह्वे ।  
> अत्रा॑देदिष्ट॒ पौंस्यं॑ ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अपिबत् । कद्रुवः । सुतं । इंद्रः । सहस्रऽबाह्वे ।  
> अत्र । अदेदिष्ट । पौंस्यं ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रः कद्रुवः कद्रुनामकस्यर्षेः संबंधिनं सुतमभिषुतं सोममपिबत् ।
> पीतवान् । सहस्रबाह्वे सहस्रबाहोः शत्रूंश्चाहन्नितिशेषः । आत्रास्मिन्नवसरे
> पौंस्यमिंद्रस्य वीर्यमदेदिष्ट । आदीप्यत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: Indra drank the Soma pressed (सुतं (*sutaṃ*)) by or belonging to the seer named Kadru (कद्रुवः (*kadruvaḥ*)). For the thousand-armed (सहस्रबाह्वे (*sahasrabāhve*)), "he slew the enemies" is to be supplied. Here, on this occasion, Indra's manly power (पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*)) blazed forth (अदेदिष्ट (*adediṣṭa*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- कद्रुवः (*kadruvaḥ*)—by the seer named Kadru
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—the pressed Soma
- अपिबत् (*apibat*)—drank
- सहस्रबाहुः (*sahasrabāhuḥ*)—destroyed the Asura with a thousand arms
- अत्र (*atra*)—on this occasion
- पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*)—Indra's valour
- अदेदिष्ट (*adediṣṭa*)—shone

### Printed p. 474

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra drank the Soma pressed by the seer named Kadru. He destroyed the Asura who had a thousand arms. On this occasion Indra's valour shone forth.

##### English translation
Indra drank the Soma offering of Kadru, (he smote the enemies) of the thousand-armed ; there did his might shine forth.

#### Ṛk 27

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒त्यं तत्तु॒र्वशे॒ यदौ॒ विदा॑नो अहूवा॒य्यं ।  
> व्या॑नट् तु॒र्वणे॒ शमि॑ ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सत्यं । तत् । तुर्वशे । यदौ । विदानः । अहूवाय्यं ।  
> वि । अनट् । तुर्वणे । शमि ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तुर्वशे राज्ञि यदौ च यदुनामके च राज्ञि तत्प्रसिद्धं यागादिलक्षणं शमि
> कर्म । शची शमाति कर्मनामसु पाठात् । सत्यं परमार्थं विदानो जानंस्तयोः
> प्रीत्यर्थमहूवाय्यमहूवाय्यनामकं तयोः शत्रुं तुर्वणे संग्रामे
> व्यानट् । व्याप्तवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: To the king Turvaśa (तुर्वशे (*turvaśe*)) and to the king named Yadu (यदौ (*yadau*)) belongs that well-known act (शमि (*śami*): karma) consisting of sacrifice and the like; शमि (*śami*) is cited as a name of action from the list of names of action. Indra, knowing (विदानः (*vidānaḥ*)) the truth, the real matter, for the pleasure of those two, overcame (व्यानट् (*vyānaṭ*): pervaded) their enemy named Ahūvāyya in battle (तुर्वणे (*turvaṇe*)). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तुर्वशे (*turvaśe*)—in the king named Turvaśa
- यदौ (*yadau*)—and in the king named Yadu
- तत् (*tat*)—well-known
- शमि (*śami*)—the sacrificial act
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—and the dealing of truth
- विदानः (*vidānaḥ*)—Indra, who knew
- अह्नवाय्यं (*ahnavāyyaṃ*)—their enemy named Ahnavāyya
- तुर्वणे (*turvaṇe*)—in battle
- व्यानट् (*vyānaṭ*)—destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who knew the sacrificial act well known in the king named Turvaśa and in the king named Yadu, and the dealing of truth, destroyed their enemy named Ahnavāyya in battle.

### Printed p. 475

##### English translation
Well knowing those (sacrificial) deeds of Turvasa and Yadu, he overcame Ahnavayya in battle.

#### Ṛk 28

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त॒रणिं॑ वो॒ जना॑नां त्र॒दं वाज॑स्य॒ गोम॑तः ।  
> स॒मा॒नमु॒ प्र शं॑सिषं ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तरणं । वः । जनानां । त्रदं । वाजस्य । गोऽमतः ।  
> समानं । ऊं इति । प्र । शंसिषं ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अस्मदीयाः पुरुषाः वो युष्माकं जनानां पुत्रपौत्रादीनां तरणिं
> तारकं त्रयं शत्रुणां तर्दयितारं गोमतः पशुमतोऽन्नस्य दातारं चेंद्रं
> समानमु साधारणमेव प्रशंसिषं । स्तौमि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O our men, I praise Indra, who is common to all (समानमु (*samānamu*): साधारणमेव (*sādhāraṇameva*)), the deliverer (तरणिं (*taraṇiṃ*): तारकं (*tārakaṃ*)) of you, of your people, sons, grandsons and the rest, the one who त्रयं (*trayaṃ*) the enemies, and the giver of food (वाजस्य (*vājasya*)) rich in cattle (गोमतः (*gomataḥ*): possessed of animals). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—for sons, grandsons and the rest
- तरणिं (*taraṇiṃ*)—the protector
- त्रदं (*tradaṃ*)—the destroyer of enemies
- गोमतः (*gomataḥ*)—possessed of cattle
- वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—giver of food
- समानं उ (*samānaṃ u*)—the kinsman common to all of us, Indra
- प्र शंसिषं (*pra śaṃsiṣaṃ*)—I praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sacrificers and the rest, I praise Indra, the protector of your sons, grandsons and the rest, the destroyer of enemies, the giver of food rich in cattle, the kinsman common to all of us.

##### English translation
I praise our common (Indra), the deliverer of your families, the (of your enemies, the bestower) of riches in cattle.

### Printed p. 476

#### Ṛk 29

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒भु॒क्षणं॒ न वर्त॑न उ॒क्फेषु॑ तुग्रा॒वृधं॑ ।  
> इंद्रं॒ सोमे॒ सचा॑ सु॒ते ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋभुक्षणं । न । वर्तवे । उक्षेषु । तुग्र्यवृधं ।  
> इंद्रं । सोमे । सचा । सुते ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋभुक्षणं महांतं तुग्रावृधमुदकस्य वर्धयितारं । तुग्रा बुर्बुरमित्यदकनामसु पाठात् । इंद्रं सोमे सचा स्तोत्रेण सह सुतेऽभिषुते
> सत्युक्थेषु शस्त्रेषु वर्तवे धनं वरितुं प्रशंसामीति शेषः । नेति संप्रत्यर्थे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: I praise the great Ṛbhukṣan (ऋभुक्षणं (*ṛbhukṣaṇaṃ*)), Tugrāvṛdh (तुग्रावृधं (*tugrāvṛdhaṃ*)), the augmenter of water; तुग्रा (*tugrā*) and बुर्बुर (*burbura*) are read among the names of water. Indra, when Soma has been pressed (सुते (*sute*)) with praise (सचा (*sacā*)), I praise in the recitations (the shastras) in order to win (वर्तवे (*vartave*)) wealth; "I praise" is to be supplied. न (*na*) is in the sense of "now". **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यभुक्षणं (*yabhukṣaṇaṃ*)—the great one
- तुग्रावृधं (*tugrāvṛdhaṃ*)—and the increaser of water
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- सोमे (*some*)—when the Soma juice
- सचा (*sacā*)—with praise
- सुते (*sute*)—has been pressed
- वर्तवे (*vartave*)—for the gaining of wealth
- उक्षेषु (*ukṣeṣu*)—in the shastra mantras **NOTE**
- न (*na*)—I now praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise with shastra mantras, for the gain of wealth, Indra, the great one and the increaser of water, when the Soma juice has been pressed with praise.

##### English translation
(I praise) in hymns the mighty Indra, the augmenter of waters, for the attainment of wealth, when the Soma is effused with (song).

#### Ṛk 30

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यः कृं॒तदिद्वि यो॒न्यं त्रि॒शोका॑य गि॒रिं पृ॒थुं ।  
> गोभ्यो॑ गा॒तुं निरे॑तवे ॥ ३० ॥

### Printed p. 477

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । कृंतत् । इत् । ए । योन्यं । त्रिशोकाय । गिरिं । पृथुं ।  
> गोभ्यः । गातुं । निःसितवे ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य इव्य एनेंद्रो योन्यमुदकनिर्गमनद्वारं पृथुं विस्तीर्णं गिरिं
> मेघं ! गिरिव्रज इति मेघनामसु पातात् । त्रिशोकाय त्रिशोकनामर्ष्यर्थं
> वि कृंतत् व्यच्छिनत् स गोभ्यो गमनवद्भ्य उदकेभ्यो निरेतवे निर्गमनाय गातुं
> भूमिं भूमिर्गातुरिति तन्नामसु पातात् । मार्गमित्यर्थः । करोतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: That Indra split for Triśoka (त्रिशोकाय (*triśokāya*): for the seer named Triśoka) the broad (पृथुं (*pṛthuṃ*): extensive) cloud (गिरिं (*giriṃ*)), the womb (योन्यं (*yonyaṃ*)), the door of the outflow of the waters; गिरिव्रज (*girivraja*) is read among the names of cloud. He makes a path (गातुं (*gātuṃ*): the earth; भूमिर्गातुरिति (*bhūmirgāturiti*) is read among the names of earth) for the waters (गोभ्यः (*gobhyaḥ*): those that flow) to go out (निरेतवे (*niretave*)); "he makes" is to be supplied. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इत् (*it*)—that same Indra who
- योन्यं (*yonyaṃ*)—the womb of the waters
- पृथुं (*pṛthuṃ*)—and broad
- गिरिं (*giriṃ*)—the cloud
- त्रिशोकाय (*triśokāya*)—for the seer named Triśoka
- वि कृंतत् (*vi kṛṃtat*)—split
- गोभ्यः (*gobhyaḥ*)—for the waters
- निरेतवे (*niretave*)—for flowing out
- गातुं (*gātuṃ*)—also made room

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That same famous Indra split the broad cloud, the womb of the waters, for the seer named Triśoka, and made a path for the flowing of the waters. **NOTE**

##### English translation
Who clove for Trishoka the broad womb-like cloud, (and made) a path for the cows to issue forth.

#### Ṛk 31

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद्द॑धि॒षे म॑न॒स्यसि॑ मंदा॒नः प्रेदिय॑क्षसि ।  
> मा तत्क॑रिंद्र मृ॒ळय॑ ॥ ३१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यॆत् । वधिषे । मनस्यसि । मंदानः । प्र । इत् । इयक्षसि ।  
> मा । तत् । कः । इंद्र । मृळय ॥ ३१ ॥

### Printed p. 478

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र मंदानो मोदमानस्त्वं यच्चुभं वस्तु दधिषे धारयसि यच्च
> मनस्यसि पूजयसि यदपि च प्रेदियक्षसि प्रयच्छस्येव तत्सर्वं मा कः । किं
> नाकार्षिः । आस्माकं कृतवानेव । किंचास्मान्मृळॆय । सुखय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, rejoicing (मंदानः (*maṃdānaḥ*)), whatever good thing you hold (दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)), whatever you honour in mind (मनस्यसि (*manasyasi*)), and whatever you give forth (प्रेदियक्षसि (*prediyakṣasi*)), all that, do not (मा कः (*mā kaḥ*): do not do; "have you not done it?" — you have indeed done it for us). And bless us (मृळय (*mṛḷaya*): make us happy). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- मंदानः (*maṃdānaḥ*)—you who are joyful
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever feeling
- दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)—you hold
- मनस्यसि (*manasyasi*)—whatever resolve of mind you hold
- प्रेदियक्षसि (*prediyakṣasi*)—whatever you wish to give
- तत् (*tat*)—all that
- मा कः (*mā kaḥ*)—need not be given to us
- मृळॆयु (*mṛḷèyu*)—only make us happy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are joyful, whatever feeling you hold in mind, whatever resolve you hold, whatever you wish to give, all that need not be given to us. Only make us happy.

##### English translation
Whatever you undertake in your exhilaration, whatever you purpose in your mind or are thinking to bestow,—O Indra, do it not but bless us.

#### Ṛk 32

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> द॒भ्रं चि॒द्दि त्वाव॑तः कृ॒तं शृ॒ण्वे अधि॒ क्षमि॑ ।  
> जिगा॑त्त्विंद्र ते॒ मनः॑ ॥ ३२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दभ्रं । चित् । हि । त्वावतः । कृतं । शृण्वे । अधि । क्षमि ।  
> जिगातु । इंद्र । ते । मनः ॥ ३२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वावतस्त्वत्सदृशस्य दभ्रं चिदल्पमपि कृतं कर्माधि क्षमि क्षमायां ॥
> अधीति सप्तम्यर्थानुवादः ॥ शृण्वे । विश्रुतं भवति हि । तथा सति ते तव मनो
> जिगातु । मयि गच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, even a small (दभ्रं चित् (*dabhraṃ cit*)) deed done by one like you (त्वावतः (*tvāvataḥ*)) is renowned (शृण्वे (*śṛṇve*)) upon the earth (क्षमि (*kṣami*)); अधि (*adhi*) is a repetition of the sense of the locative. That being so, let your mind (मनः (*manaḥ*)) come (जिगातु (*jigātu*)) to me.

### Printed p. 479

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वावतः (*tvāvataḥ*)—of a great person like you
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—the deed
- दव्रं चित् (*davraṃ cit*)—even if small
- अधि क्षमि (*adhi kṣami*)—upon the earth
- शृण्वे हि (*śṛṇve hi*)—is renowned
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—your gracious mind
- जिगातु (*jigātu*)—let it turn towards me

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, even if the deed done by a great person like you is small, it is renowned upon the earth. Let your gracious mind turn towards me.

##### English translation
Indra, the least deeds of one like you are renowned in the earth; may your care visit me.

#### Ṛk 33

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तवेदु॒ ताः सु॑की॒र्तयोऽस॑न्नु॒त प्रश॑स्तयः ।  
> यदिं॑द्र मृ॒ळया॑सि नः ॥ ३३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शव । इत् । ऊं इति । ताः । सुकीर्तयः । आसन् । उतॆ । प्रशस्तयः ।  
> यत् । इंद्र । मृळयासि । नः ॥ ३३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं नोऽस्मान्यद्याभिर्मृळयासि सुखयसि ताः सुकीर्तयः
> शोभनाख्यातयस्तवेत्तनैवासन् । भवेयुः । उतापि च ताः प्रशस्तयः स्तुतयश्च
> तवैव भवेयुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, those good fame-giving praises (सुकीर्तयः (*sukīrtayaḥ*): beautiful renown) through which (यत् (*yat*)) you bless us (मृळयासि (*mṛḷayāsi*): make us happy) would be yours alone (तवेत् (*tavet*)); and those eulogies (प्रशस्तयः (*praśastayaḥ*): praises) would be yours alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- यत् (*yat*)—by which praises, being pleased
- मृळॆयासि (*mṛḷèyāsi*)—you make us happy
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—such
- सुकीर्तयः (*sukīrtayaḥ*)—excellent praise-acts
- तवेत् (*tavet*)—dedicated to you alone
- आसन् (*āsan*)—are
- उत (*uta*)—and
- प्रशस्तयः (*praśastayaḥ*)—those excellent praises are made for you alone

### Printed p. 480

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, those excellent praise-acts, by which, being pleased, you make us happy, are dedicated to you alone. Those excellent praises are made for you alone.

##### English translation
Yours be those ascriptions of praise, yours those hymns, through which, Indra, you bless us.

#### Ṛk 34

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा न॒ एक॑स्मि॒न्नाग॑सि॒ मा द्वयो॑रु॒त त्रि॒षु ।  
> वधी॒र्मा शू॑र॒ भूरि॑सु ॥ ३४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । नः । एकस्मिन् । आगसि । मा । द्वयोः । उत । त्रिषु ।  
> वधीः । हू । शूर । भूरिषु ॥ ३४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शूरेंद्र नोऽस्मानेकस्मिन्नागस्यपराधे मा वः     मा हिंसीः ।
> द्वयोरागसोरपि मा वधीः । उतापि च त्रिष्वागःस्वपि मा हिंसीः । भूरिष्टस्यसंख्यातेश्वागःसु मा च वधीः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O heroic Indra, do not strike us (मा वधीः (*mā vadhīḥ*): do not injure) for one offence (एकस्मिन् आगसि (*ekasmin āgasi*)); do not strike us for two offences either, and also not for three. Do not strike us for many (भूरिषु (*bhūriṣu*)) offences. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- एकस्मिन् आगसि (*ekasmin āgasi*)—for one fault
- मा वधीः (*mā vadhīḥ*)—do not injure
- द्वयोः (*dvayoḥ*)—for two faults also
- मा (*mā*)—do not injure
- उत (*uta*)—and
- त्रिषु (*triṣu*)—for three faults also
- मा (*mā*)—do not injure
- भूरिषु (*bhūriṣu*)—even if for exceedingly many sins, do not injure us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valiant Indra, do not injure us for one fault. Do not injure us for two or three faults either. Even if we have committed exceedingly many faults, do not injure us.

### Printed p. 481

##### English translation
Slay us not for one sin, not for two, not for three; O hero, slay us not for many.

#### Ṛk 35

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बि॒भया॒ हि त्वाव॑त उ॒ग्राद॑भिप्रभं॒गिणः॑ ।  
> द॒स्माद्॒हमृ॑ती॒षहः॑ ॥ ३५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बिभयः । हि । त्वावतः । उग्रात् । अभिप्रभंगिनः ।  
> दस्मात् । अहं । ऋत्तिसहः ॥ ३५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वावतस्त्वत्सदृशामग्रामद्रूर्ध्गादभिस्प्रभंगिणः शत्रोणामभिप्रहर्तुर्दस्मात्पानामुपक्षपयितुर्यतीषदः शत्रुकृतां हिंसां सहतोऽहं बिभय हि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, I am afraid (बिभय (*bibhaya*)) of one like you (त्वावतः (*tvāvataḥ*)), formidable (उग्रात् (*ugrāt*)), the smiter of enemies (अभिप्रभंगिणः (*abhiprabhaṃgiṇaḥ*)), the destroyer (दस्मात् (*dasmāt*); he glosses it as one who wastes away the sinful), who endures the violence done by enemies (ऋतीषहः (*ṛtīṣahaḥ*)). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उग्रात् (*ugrāt*)—of one of exceedingly great strength
- अभिप्रभंगिणः (*abhiprabhaṃgiṇaḥ*)—the smiter of enemies
- दस्मात् (*dasmāt*)—the destroyer of sin
- ऋतीषहः (*ṛtīṣahaḥ*)—who can withstand the violence of enemies
- त्वावतः (*tvāvataḥ*)—of a great person like you
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- बिभय हि (*bibhaya hi*)—surely fear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, I surely fear a great person like you, of exceeding strength, the smiter of enemies, the destroyer of sin, who can withstand the violence of enemies.

##### English translation
I am afraid of one like you, terrible, the smiter of enemies, the destroyer, who endures hostile attacks.

#### Ṛk 36

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा सख्युः॒ शून॒मा वि॑दे॒ मा पु॒त्रस्य॑ प्रभूवसो ।  
> आ॒वृत्व॑द्भूतु ते॒ मनः॑ ॥ ३६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

### Printed p. 482

> मा । सख्युः । शूनं । आ । विदे । मा । पुत्रस्य । प्रभुवसो इति प्रभुवसो ।  
> आवृत्वत् । भूतु । ते । मनः ॥ ३६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे प्रभूवसो प्रभूतधनेंद्र ते तव सख्युः शूनं वृद्धं मा विदे ।
> मावेदयामि । पुत्रस्यापि शूनं मा विदे । तव मनोऽस्मास्वावृत्त्वदावर्तनवद्भूतु ।
> भवतु । पुनःपुनः सुखं करोत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, rich in wealth (प्रभूवसो (*prabhūvaso*): of abundant wealth), may I not come to know (मा विदे (*mā vide*): let me not report) the distress (शूनं (*śūnaṃ*): वृद्धं (*vṛddhaṃ*) in the text) of your friend (सख्युः (*sakhyuḥ*)), nor the distress of his son. Let your mind (मनः (*manaḥ*)) turn towards us (आवृत्वत् (*āvṛtvat*): be of the nature of turning); the sense is: may it do us good again and again. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रभूवसो (*prabhūvaso*)—O Indra of abundant wealth
- ते (*te*)—your
- सख्युः (*sakhyuḥ*)—friend's
- शूनं (*śūnaṃ*)—distress
- मा आ विदे (*mā ā vide*)—let me not know
- पुत्रस्य (*putrasya*)—a son's distress too
- मा (*mā*)—let me not know
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—your gracious mind
- आवृत्वत् (*āvṛtvat*)—turned towards us
- भूतु (*bhūtu*)—let it be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra of abundant wealth, let me not know of any distress of your friend, nor the distress of his son. Let your gracious mind be turned towards us.

##### English translation
Wealthy (Indra), may I never have to tell you of the destitution of my friend or my son; may your mind be favourable towards me.

#### Ṛk 37

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> को नु म॑र्या॒ अमि॑थितः॒ सखा॒ सखा॑यमब्रवीत् ॥  
> ज॒हा को अ॒स्मदी॑षते ॥ ३७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कः । नु । मर्याः । अमिथितः । सखा । सखायं । अब्रवीत् ।  
> जहा । कः । अस्मत् । ईषते ॥ ३७ ॥

### Printed p. 483

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> को नुकः खलु हे मर्या मनुष्याः अमिथितः । मेधतिराक्रोशकर्मा ।
> अनाकृश्च इंद्रादन्यः सखा सखायं प्रति जहा अहं कं जघान कः को वास्यदस्मत्तो
> भीत ईषदे पलायत इत्यब्रवीत् । वदति । इंद्र एवैतादृशस्य वचनस्य वक्तेत्यभिप्रायतः । भा च यास्कः । मेधतिराक्रोशकर्मा । अपापकं जघान कमहं जातु
> कोऽस्मद्भूते पलायते । नि. ४-२ । इति । मा न एकस्मिन्नागसीत्यादिकया श्रुत्या
> नूनमृषिमिंद्र आजहारेत्यत्रर्षिविस्मयत इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa construes the verse as the words of Indra. "O men (मर्या (*maryā*) means human beings), what friend, not enraged (the root मेधति (*medhati*) has the sense of abuse or anger), a friend other than Indra, has slain his friend? Or who is it that, afraid of me, runs away?" So Indra spoke. The intention is that Indra alone is the speaker of such a word. Sāyaṇa cites Yāska (Ni. 4-2) for the sense of the words, and refers to the Vedic text that begins "not for a single offence" and to a passage on the seer's astonishment, with Indra bringing the seer. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मर्याः (*maryāḥ*)—O men
- अमिथितः (*amithitaḥ*)—who has not become enraged
- को नु सखा (*ko nu sakhā*)—what friend indeed
- सखायं (*sakhāyaṃ*)—his own friend
- जहा (*jahā*)—has killed
- कः (*kaḥ*)—who indeed
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from me, being afraid
- ईषते (*īṣate*)—has run away (thus)
- अब्रवीत् (*abravīt*)—Indra said

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

"O men, what friend, not given to rage, has killed his own friend? Who indeed has run away in fear of me?" Thus Indra has asked. The purport is that none of his friends has any fear of him.

##### English translation
"Who, O mortals," said (Indra), "unprovoked, has ever, as a friend, slain his friend? Who flees from me?"

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For this verse Yāska has given the following explanation: मर्या इति मनुष्यनाम । मर्यादाभिधानं ना स्यात् । मर्यादा मर्य्यरादीयते । मर्यादामर्यादिनोर्विभागः ॥ मेथतिराक्रोशकर्मा । अपापकं जघान कमहं जातु । कोऽस्मद्भीतः पलायते ॥ (*maryā iti manuṣyanāma | maryādābhidhānaṃ nā syāt | maryādā maryyarādīyate | maryādāmaryādinorvibhāgaḥ ‖ methatirākrośakarmā | apāpakaṃ jaghāna kamahaṃ jātu | ko 'smadbhītaḥ palāyate ‖*) (Ni. 4-2). मर्याः (*maryāḥ*) means men. The word मर्या (*maryā*) also has the meaning of a limit or border: the line between one region and another; the line that separates two different parts and divides them from each other is called मर्या (*maryā*) (Boundary). For the root मेथति (*methati*), to show anger

### Printed p. 484

is the meaning. In the present sentence Indra asks: what man who has done no wrong have I ever killed? What man, seeing me, would run away in fear? Such is the sense of Indra's words. That is, Indra does not kill any man who has done no wrong. Indra's anger acts only against the wicked and those who do wrong. Therefore who would run away in fear on seeing Indra? No one runs away. Those who are not sinners have no need to fear Indra or Indra's anger. This is the main purport.

#### Ṛk 38

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वारे॑ वृषभा सु॒तेऽसि॑न्व॒न्भूर्या॑वयः ।  
> श्व॒घ्नीव॑ नि॒वता॒ चर॑न् ॥ ३८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एवारे । वृषभ । सुते । असिन्वन् । भूरि । अवयः ।  
> श्वघ्नीऽइव । निवता । चरन् ॥ ३८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृषभ कामानां वर्षकेंद्र एवारे । एवारो नाम कश्चित् । तस्मिन्
> सुतेऽभिषुते सोमे सति भूरि बहूनि धनान्यसिन्नन्न बध्नञ्घ्नी । श्वंघ्नी कितवः ।
> तथा च यास्कः । श्वंघ्नी कितवो भवति स्वं हंति.... । नि. ५-२२.... ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Vṛṣabha," that is, Indra, showerer of desires. Evāra is the name of a certain person; when Soma has been pressed (सुते (*sute*)) in his case, abundant wealth (भूरि (*bhūri*) means much) was bound or collected (असिन्वन् (*asinvan*)). श्वंघ्नी (*śvaṃghnī*) is a gambler; Sāyaṇa cites Yāska (Ni. 5-22) for this, with the words श्वंघ्नी कितवो भवति स्वं हंति (*śvaṃghnī kitavo bhavati svaṃ haṃti*). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—O Indra, showerer of desires
- एवारे (*evāre*)—the seer Evāra
- सुते (*sute*)—when the Soma was pressed
- भूरि (*bhūri*)—the abundant Soma
- श्वघ्नीव (*śvaghnīva*)—like a hunter
- असिन्वन् (*asinvan*)—joined you alone
- आवयः (*āvayaḥ*)—all the other gods who were there
- निवता (*nivatā*)—with faces turned downward
- हरन् (*haran*)—went out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, showerer of desires, when the seer Evāra pressed the Soma, the abundant Soma joined you alone, like a hunter. All the other gods who were there went out with faces turned downward.

##### English translation
Showerer (of benefits), when the ready Soma was effused, you devoured much, without stint, rushing down like a gamester.

> यदीं॑ ब्र॒ह्मभ्य॒ इद्ददः॑ ॥ ३९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । ते । एता । वचस्ययुजा । हरी इति । गृब्बे । सुमत् 5 रथा ।  
> यत् । ईं । ब्रह्मभ्यः । इत् । ददः ॥ ३९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ते तव सुमद्रथा कल्याणरथौ वचोयुजा मंत्रेण युज्यमानावेतैतौ
> हरी अश्वाना गृब्बे । अस्मदभिमुखं यातुं हस्ताभ्यामाकर्षामीत्यर्थः ।
> यद्यस्मात्त्वं ब्रह्मभ्य इद्दाह्मणेभ्य एवेमिदं धनं ददः ददासि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Your (ते (*te*)) two horses, Hari, with beautiful chariots, yoked by a mantra (वचोयुजा (*vacoyujā*)), these two, I seize (गृब्बे (*gṛbbe*)): I draw them with my hands to come towards us. This is because (यत् (*yat*)) you give this wealth to Brahmans alone.

- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- ब्रह्मभ्यः इत् (*brahmabhyaḥ it*)—to Brahmans alone
- ईं (*īṃ*)—wealth

- ते (*te*)—your
- सुमद्रथा (*sumadrathā*)—having a beautiful chariot
- वचोयुजा (*vacoyujā*)—joined by mantras
- एता (*etā*)—those well-known
- हरी (*harī*)—horses
- आ गृभ्वे (*ā gṛbhve*)—I draw to this side

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, for which reason you give wealth only to the knowers of Brahman, therefore I draw to this side your well-known horses, which have a beautiful chariot and are joined by mantras. **NOTE**

##### English translation
I draw hither your two steeds, harnessed to a beautiful chariot and yoked by hymns, since you give wealth to the Brahmans.

#### Ṛk 40

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भिं॒धि विश्वा॒ अप॒ द्विषः॒ परि॒ बाधो॑ ज॒ही मृधः॑ ।  
> वसु॑ स्पा॒र्हं तदा भ॑र ॥ ४० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भिंधि । विश्वाः । अप । द्विषः । परि । बाधः । जहि । मृधः ।  
> वसु । स्पार्हं । तत् । आ । भर ॥ ४० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं विश्वाः सर्वा द्विषो द्वेष्ट्रीः शत्रुसेना अप भिंधि । विदारय ।
> बाधो हिंसित्रीर्मृधः संग्रामान् । स्पृधो मृध इति संग्रामनामसु पातात् ।
> परि जहि । हिंधि । अतस्तासां स्पार्हं स्पृहणीयं तत्पसिद्धं वस्वा भर । अस्मभ्यमाहर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, split apart and tear all hostile (द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*), that is, hating) armies of enemies. Strike all around the injuring (बाधः (*bādhaḥ*)) मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*), that is, battles; Sāyaṇa notes that the words for battle are listed together, with the passage beginning स्पृधो मृध इति (*spṛdho mṛdha iti*). Therefore bring to us their desirable, well-known wealth. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—the armies of enemies
- अप भिंधि (*apa bhiṃdhi*)—destroy
- बाधः (*bādhaḥ*)—the injuring
- मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)—their deeds of battle and the like
- परि जहि (*pari jahi*)—destroy completely
- स्पार्हं (*spārhaṃ*)—the attractive
- तत् (*tat*)—the well-known
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—bring and provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, destroy all the armies of enemies. Destroy completely their injuring deeds of battle and the like. Provide us with the attractive and well-known wealth.

##### English translation
Cleave asunder all the hostile hosts, frustrate their destructive attacks, and bestow on us their desirable wealth.

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराज परमेश्वर वैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्री वीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे यक्संहिताभाष्ये षष्ठाष्टके तृतीयोऽध्यायः समाप्तः । (*iti śrīmadrājādhirāja parameśvara vaidikamārgapravartaka śrī vīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe yaksaṃhitābhāṣye ṣaṣṭhāṣṭake tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ |*)

Here ends the third chapter in the sixth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with the bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and the Kannada translation.

यवक्षरदनभ्रष्टं मात्र हीनं तु यद्वृतेत् तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तुते ॥ (*yavakṣaradanabhraṣṭaṃ mātra hīnaṃ tu yadvṛtet tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stute ‖*) **GLOSS**

**Sixth Aṣṭaka, Fourth Adhyāya**

श्री गणाधिपतये नमः (*śrī gaṇādhipataye namaḥ*) **GLOSS**

नागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं । यस्य निश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं । वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*nāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ | yasya niśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ | vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*) **GLOSS**

**Ṛgveda-saṃhitā with the bhāṣya of Sāyaṇa (with the Kannada translation and explanation)**

The fourth chapter in the sixth aṣṭaka. In the eighth maṇḍala, the forty-sixth sūkta.

## Sūkta 46 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning त्वावत (*tvāvata*) has thirty-three Ṛks and is the fourth sūkta; its seer is Vaśa, the son of Aśva. As before, the first and the next two Ṛks are Gāyatrī. Of these the first is Pādanicṛt, since it has the stated mark of three heptasyllabic pādas, as the Anukramaṇī (Anu. 4-4) says. The fifth Ṛk, दधानो गोमदश्ववदित्येषा (*dadhāno gomadaśvavadityeṣā*), is Kakubh, being furnished with pādas of eight, twelve and eight syllables; the rule is "if the middle one is of twelve, Kakubh" (Anu. 5-3). The sixth, तमिंद्रमिति (*tamiṃdramiti*), is Gāyatrī. The seventh, तस्मिन् हि संतीति (*tasmin hi saṃtīti*), is Bṛhatī. The eighth, यस्ते मद (*yaste mada*), is Anuṣṭubh. The ninth, यो दुष्टर (*yo duṣṭara*), is Satobṛhatī; for it is said that the odd and even Jagatī pādas make Satobṛhatī (Anu. 8-4). The tenth, गव्यो शु ण (*gavyo śu ṇa*), is Gāyatrī. The eleventh, नहि ते शूर (*nahi te śūra*), is Bṛhatī. The twelfth, य ऋष्व (*ya ṛṣva*), is the reversed Satobṛhatī, with the first and third pādas of eight syllables and the second and fourth of twelve. The block breaks off in the middle of the next statement. **NOTE**

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The rest of the statement on the metres, as the preceding window left it: the twelfth Ṛk is the reversed Satobṛhatī, as the Anukramaṇī says (Anu. 8-5). The thirteenth, स नो वाजेष्टि (*sa no vājeṣṭi*), is a Dvipadā of twenty-four syllables. The fourteenth, अभि वो वीरं (*abhi vo vīraṃ*), is a Bṛhatī with an ant-waisted middle (Pipīlikamadhyā): between the thirteen-syllabled pādas the middle one has eight syllables (Anu. 7-7). The fifteenth, ददी रेक्च (*dadī rekca*), is Kakumnyaṅkuśirā, having four pādas of Triṣṭubh and Jagatī measure (Anu. 5-4). The sixteenth, विश्वेषां (*viśveṣāṃ*), is Virāj. The seventeenth, महः सु व (*mahaḥ su va*), is Jagatī. The eighteenth, ये पातॆयंत (*ye pātèyaṃta*), is Upariṣṭādbṛhatī, because its fourth pāda has twelve syllables. The nineteenth, प्रभंगं (*prabhaṃgaṃ*), is Bṛhatī. The twentieth, सनितः सुसनितः (*sanitaḥ susanitaḥ*), is Viṣamapadā Bṛhatī, with the unequal pādas as stated (Anu. 7-8). The twenty-first and twenty-second, beginning आ स एतु (*ā sa etu*) and पष्टिं (*paṣṭiṃ*), are Paṅkti. The twenty-third, दश श्यावा (*daśa śyāvā*), is Gāyatrī. The twenty-fourth, दानास (*dānāsa*), is Paṅkti. The twenty-fifth and twenty-seventh are Bṛhatī; the twenty-sixth and twenty-eighth are Satobṛhatī; the twenty-ninth is Gāyatrī. The thirtieth, गावो न यूथं (*gāvo na yūthaṃ*), is a Dvipadā Virāj of twenty syllables. The thirty-first is Uṣṇik, the thirty-second Paṅkti, the thirty-third Gāyatrī. By the four Ṛks beginning आ स एति (*ā sa eti*) the gift of Pṛthuśravas, son of Kanīta, is praised, so they have that gift as deity; the four beginning आ नो वायवित्यादीनां (*ā no vāyavityādīnāṃ*) and the thirty-second have Vāyu as deity; the remaining Ṛks, by the rule for what is not specified, have Indra as deity. All this is said in the Anukramaṇī: त्वावतस्त्रयस्त्रिंशद्वशोऽश्व आ स आदि कानीतस्य पृथुश्रवसो दानस्तुतिराद्या हादनिच्छत् पंचम्यादि ककुब्गायत्रि बृहत्यनुष्टुप् सतोबृहती गायत्रि विपरीतोत्तरः प्रगाथो द्विपदा चतुर्विंशिका बृहती पिपीलिकमध्या ककुम्न्यंकुशिरा विराड्डगत्युपरिष्टाद्दृहतीबृहत्यौ विषमपदोत्तरे पंक्ति गायत्रि पंक्तिः प्रगाथौ च वायव्यौ गायत्रि द्विपदोष्णिक् पंक्तिर्वायव्या गायत्रिति ॥ (*tvāvatastrayastriṃśadvaśo 'śva ā sa ādi kānītasya pṛthuśravaso dānastutirādyā hādanicchat paṃcamyādi kakubgāyatri bṛhatyanuṣṭup satobṛhatī gāyatri viparītottaraḥ pragātho dvipadā caturviṃśikā bṛhatī pipīlikamadhyā kakumnyaṃkuśirā virāḍḍagatyupariṣṭāddṛhatībṛhatyau viṣamapadottare paṃkti gāyatri paṃktiḥ pragāthau ca vāyavyau gāyatri dvipadoṣṇik paṃktirvāyavyā gāyatriti ‖*). In the Mahāvrata, in the Niṣkevalya śastra, the sūkta is used up to सनितः सुसनितः (*sanitaḥ susanitaḥ*); so Śaunaka states in the Fifth Āraṇyaka: त्वावतः पूरूवसविति वशः सनितः सुसनितरित्येतदंतः । (*tvāvataḥ pūrūvasaviti vaśaḥ sanitaḥ susanitarityetadaṃtaḥ |*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-5). **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning त्वावतः (*tvāvataḥ*) is the fourth sūkta in the sixth Anuvāka of the eighth Maṇḍala. It has thirty-three Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is one named Vaśa, the son of Aśva; the first four Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Gāyatrī metre. But the first Ṛk is of the metre called Pādanicṛt. If a Ṛk has three pādas and every pāda has seven syllables each, it is called the Pādanicṛt metre: this is the mark of this metre (Chaṃ. Anu. 4-4). **NOTE** The fifth Ṛk, beginning दधानो गोमदश्ववत् (*dadhāno gomadaśvavat*), is in the Kakup metre. If a Ṛk has three pādas and in those pādas there are, in order, eight, twelve and eight syllables, it is called the Kakup metre (Anu. 5-3). The sixth Ṛk, beginning तमिंद्रं (*tamiṃdraṃ*), is in the Gāyatrī metre; the seventh Ṛk, beginning तस्मिन् हि संति (*tasmin hi saṃti*), is in the Bṛhatī metre; the eighth Ṛk, beginning यस्ते मदः (*yaste madaḥ*), is in the Anuṣṭup metre;

### Printed p. 491

the ninth Ṛk, beginning ये दुष्टरः (*ye duṣṭaraḥ*), is in the Satobṛhatī metre. If in a Ṛk the first and the third pādas are in the Jagatī metre, it is called the Satobṛhatī metre (Anu. 8-4). The tenth Ṛk, beginning गव्यो षु णः (*gavyo ṣu ṇaḥ*), is in the Gāyatrī metre; the eleventh Ṛk, beginning नहि ते शूर (*nahi te śūra*), is in the Bṛhatī metre; the twelfth Ṛk, beginning य ऋष्टः (*ya ṛṣṭaḥ*), is of the metre called Viparītā Satobṛhatī. In this metre the first and third pādas have eight syllables each, and the second and fourth pādas have twelve syllables each. This is the mark of this metre (Anu. 8-5). The thirteenth Ṛk, beginning स नो वाजेषु (*sa no vājeṣu*), is of the metre called Dvipadā of twenty-four syllables. The fourteenth Ṛk, beginning अभि वो वीरं (*abhi vo vīraṃ*), is of the metre called Pipīlikamadhyamā Bṛhatī. If a Ṛk has three pādas, the middle pāda has eight syllables and the other two pādas have thirteen and sixteen syllables, it is of the metre called Pipīlikamadhyā Bṛhatī (Anu. 7-7). The fifteenth Ṛk, beginning ददी रेक्षः (*dadī rekṣaḥ*), is of the metre called Kakumnyaṅkuśirā. If a Ṛk has three pādas, and in the first pāda there are eleven syllables as in the Triṣṭup metre, in the second pāda twelve syllables as in the Jagatī metre, and in the third pāda four syllables, it is called the Kakumnyaṅkuśirā metre (Anu. 5-4). The sixteenth Ṛk, beginning विश्वेषां (*viśveṣāṃ*), is in the Virāṭ metre; the seventeenth Ṛk, beginning महः सु वः (*mahaḥ su vaḥ*), is in the Jagatī metre; because the fourth pāda of the eighteenth Ṛk, beginning ये पातॆयंते (*ye pātèyaṃte*), has twelve syllables, it is of the metre called Upariṣṭādbṛhatī; the nineteenth Ṛk, beginning प्रभंगं (*prabhaṃgaṃ*), is in the Bṛhatī metre; the twentieth Ṛk, beginning सनितः सुसनितः (*sanitaḥ susanitaḥ*), is of the metre called Viṣamapadā Bṛhatī. In this Ṛk the first pāda has nine syllables, the second pāda eight syllables, the third pāda eleven syllables and the fourth pāda eight syllables. This is the mark of this metre (Anu. 7-8). The twenty-first and twenty-second Ṛks, beginning आ स एतु (*ā sa etu*) and षष्ठिं सहस्रा (*ṣaṣṭhiṃ sahasrā*), are in the Paṅkti metre. The twenty-third Ṛk, beginning पर श्यावाः (*para śyāvāḥ*), is in the Gāyatrī metre; the twenty-fourth Ṛk, beginning दानासः (*dānāsaḥ*), is in the Paṅkti metre; the twenty-fifth and twenty-seventh Ṛks are in the Bṛhatī metre; the twenty-sixth and twenty-eighth Ṛks are in the Satobṛhatī metre; the twenty-ninth Ṛk is in the Gāyatrī metre; the thirtieth Ṛk, beginning गावो न यूथं (*gāvo na yūthaṃ*), is in the Dvipadā Virāṭ metre of twenty syllables; the thirty-first Ṛk is in the Uṣṇik metre; the thirty-second Ṛk is in the Paṅkti metre; the thirty-seventh Ṛk is in the Gāyatrī metre. **NOTE** In the four Ṛks beginning आ स एतु (*ā sa etu*) (21-24, the praise of the gift of Pṛthuśravas, the son of Kṛta, is stated, so for those Ṛks the praise of the gift of Pṛthuśravas is the deity. **NOTE** For the four Ṛks beginning आ नो वायो (*ā no vāyo*) (25-28 and 32), and for the thirty-second Ṛk, Vāyu is the deity; the remaining Ṛks have Indra as deity. All this is said in the Anukramaṇī in this way: श्यावतस्त्रयस्त्रिंशद्वशोऽश्वत् आ स आदि कानीतस्य पृथुश्रवसो दानस्तुतिराद्या पादनिच्छत् पंचम्यादि ककुब्गायत्री बृहत्यनुष्टुप् सतोबृहती गायत्री विपरीतोत्तरः प्रगाथो द्विपदा चतुर्विंशिका बृहती पिपीलिकमध्या ककुम्न्यंकुशिरा विराड्डगत्युपरिष्वादृहतीबृहत्या विषमपदोत्तरे पंक्ति गायत्री पंक्तिः प्रगाथौ च वायव्य् गायत्री द्विपदोष्णिक् पंक्तिर्वायव्या गायत्री (*śyāvatastrayastriṃśadvaśo 'śvat ā sa ādi kānītasya pṛthuśravaso dānastutirādyā pādanicchat paṃcamyādi kakubgāyatrī bṛhatyanuṣṭup satobṛhatī gāyatrī viparītottaraḥ pragātho dvipadā caturviṃśikā bṛhatī pipīlikamadhyā kakumnyaṃkuśirā virāḍḍagatyupariṣvādṛhatībṛhatyā viṣamapadottare paṃkti gāyatrī paṃktiḥ pragāthau ca vāyavy gāyatrī dvipadoṣṇik paṃktirvāyavyā gāyatrī*)

### Printed p. 492

is what is said. In the Mahāvrateṣṭi, for the mantras of the Niṣkevalya śastra, the twenty Ṛks (1-20) from the beginning of this sūkta up to the Ṛk beginning सनितः सुसनितः (*sanitaḥ susanitaḥ*) are to be applied, and this is indicated in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, in the Fifth Āraṇyaka, by the sentence त्वावतः पुरूवसविति वशः सुनितः सुसनितरित्येतदंतः (*tvāvataḥ purūvasaviti vaśaḥ sunitaḥ susanitarityetadaṃtaḥ*) (Ai. A. 5-2-5). **NOTE**

##### Particulars

Sūkta 46. Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 46. Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 4; Varga 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 33. Seer: Vaśo 'śvaḥ. Deity: 1 20, 29-31, 33. Indraḥ; 21-24. Dvipādā Bṛhatī; 14. Pipilīkamadhyā; 15. Kakumnyaṅkuśirā; 16. Virāṭ; 17. Jagatī; 18. Upariṣvādahatī; 20. Viṣamapadā; 21, 22, 24, 32. Saṃktiḥ; 30. Dvipadā Virāṭ; 31. Usṭik. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वाव॑तः पुरूवसो व॒यमिं॑द्र प्रणेतः ।  
> स्मसि॑ स्थातर्हरीणां ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वावतः । पुरूवसो इति पुरुषसो । वयं । इंद्र । प्रनेतरिति प्रनेतः ।  
> स्मसि । स्थातः । हरीणां ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पुरूवसो बहुधनेंद्र प्रणेतः कर्मणां पारं प्रकर्षेण प्रापयितरिंद्र त्वावतस्त्वत्सदृशस्य । इंद्रसमानस्यान्य स्याभावात्तवेत्यर्थः । तव स्वभूता वयं
> स्मसि । स्मः । हे हरीणामेतत्संज्ञकानामश्वानां स्थातरधिष्ठातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Purūvasu, rich in wealth, O Indra, Praṇetṛ, who brings rites to their end with full effect: of one like you (त्वावतः (*tvāvataḥ*)), that is, of you, since there is no other equal to Indra; we are yours, belonging to you. स्मसि (*smasi*) stands for स्मः (*smaḥ*). O Sthātṛ, the presiding lord over the horses called Hari.

### Printed p. 493

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरूवसो (*purūvaso*)—one who has abundant wealth
- प्रणेतः (*praṇetaḥ*)—one who helps in carrying out the rites
- हरीणां (*harīṇāṃ*)—of the horses called Hari
- स्थातः (*sthātaḥ*)—the controller; O
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—Indra
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- त्वा वतः (*tvā vataḥ*)—as belonging to you
- स्मसि (*smasi*)—we are

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who have abundant wealth, who help in carrying out the rites, who are the controller of the horses called Hari, we belong to you.

##### English translation
O wealthy Indra, the leader (of rites), we belong to one like you, ruler of horses.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वां हि स॒त्यम॑द्रिवो वि॒द्म दा॒तार॑मि॒षां ।  
> वि॒द्म दा॒तारं॑ रया॒णां ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वां । हि । सत्यं । अद्रिवः । विद्म । दातारं । इषां ।  
> विद्म । दातारं । रयाणां ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अद्रिवः । अत्ति शत्रुमित्यद्रिर्वज्रः । तद्वन्निंद्र त्वां सत्यं निश्चयमिषामन्नानां दातारं विद्म । जानीमः । तथा रयीणां धनानां दातारं विद्म ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Adrivaḥ: अत्ति शत्रुमित्यद्रिर्वज्रः (*atti śatrumityadrirvajraḥ*), he eats the enemy, so adri is the thunderbolt; O Indra, possessor of it. We know you for certain (सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)) as the giver of food (इषां (*iṣāṃ*)), and likewise we know you as the giver of riches (रयीणां (*rayīṇāṃ*), wealth).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt
- त्वां हि (*tvāṃ hi*)—you alone
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—certainly
- इषां (*iṣāṃ*)—of foods
- दातारं (*dātāraṃ*)—as the giver
- विद्म (*vidma*)—we have known
- रयाणां (*rayāṇāṃ*)—of riches
- दातारं (*dātāraṃ*)—as the giver also
- विद्म (*vidma*)—we have known

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, we have known you alone, for certain, as the giver of food, and we have known you as the giver of wealth.

### Printed p. 494

##### English translation
You, thunderer, we verily know to be the giver of food, you, we know to be the giver of riches.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ यस्य॑ ते महि॒मानं॒ शत॑मूते॒ शत॑क्रतो ।  
> गी॒र्भिर्गृ॒णंति॑ का॒रवः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । यस्य । ते । महिमानं । शतंऊते । शतक्रतो इति शतक्रतो ।  
> गीर्भिः । गृणंति । कारवः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शतमूतेऽपरिमितरक्षण हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मयुक्तेंद्र यस्य ते
> महिमानं माहात्म्यं कारवः स्तोतारो गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिर्गृणंति स्तुवंति
> स्वाभीष्टायॆ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śatamūte, of limitless protection; O Śatakratu, Indra, endowed with many deeds: the greatness of you, of whom (यस्य (*yasya*)) it is said, the Kāravas, that is, the worshippers, praise with hymns, for the sake of their own desired aim.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतमूते (*śatamūte*)—one who has protection of many kinds
- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—one who has works of many kinds; O Indra
- यस्य (*yasya*)—you who are famous, such
- ते (*te*)—your
- महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*)—greatness
- कारवः (*kāravaḥ*)—the worshippers
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with hymns
- आ गृणंति (*ā gṛṇaṃti*)—praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who have protection of many kinds and works of many kinds, the worshippers praise the greatness of you, who are famous, with hymns.

##### English translation
O Shatakratu, wielding a hundred protections, whose greatness the worshippers praise with their hymns.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒नी॒थो घा॒ स मर्त्यो॒ यं म॒रुतो॒ यम॑र्य॒मा ।  
> मि॒त्रः पांत्य॒द्रुहः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 495

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुनीधः । घ । सः । मर्त्यः । यं । मरुतः । यं । आर्यमा ।  
> मित्रः । पांति । अद्रुहः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स मर्त्यो मनुष्यो यजमानः सुनीथः सुयज्ञः सुनयनो वा भवति ।
> घेति प्रसिद्धौ । स इत्युक्तं कमित्याह । यं यजमानं मरुतो देवाः पांति
> रक्षंत्यद्रुहोऽद्रोहकर्तारः । तथा यमर्यमा पाति । यं च मित्रः पाति ।
> स एवं भवतीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That mortal, the human sacrificer, becomes सुनीथः (*sunīthaḥ*), a good sacrificer or a good leader. घ (*gha*) is a well-known particle. He is spoken of as "that"; who is meant? The sacrificer whom the Maruts, gods who do no harm, protect; likewise the one whom Aryaman protects, and the one whom Mitra protects: he becomes so.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यं (*yaṃ*)—which sacrificer
- अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*)—who wish no harm
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- पांति (*pāṃti*)—protect
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which man
- आर्यमा (*āryamā*)—Aryaman
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—and Mitra protect
- सति मर्त्यः (*sati martyaḥ*)—that same sacrificer in human form
- सुनीथः घु (*sunīthaḥ ghu*)—certainly becomes an excellent manager of the sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer whom the Maruts, who wish no harm, protect, whom Aryaman and Mitra protect, that same sacrificer in human form certainly becomes an excellent manager of the sacrifice.

##### English translation
Fortunate in sacrifice is that mortal whom the guileless Maruts, whom Aryaman and Mitra, protect.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दधा॑नो॒ गोम॒दश्व॑वत्सु॒वीर्य॑मादि॒त्यजू॑त विधते ।  
> सदा॑ रा॒या पु॑रु॒स्पृहा॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दधानः । गोमत् । अश्ववत् । सुवीर्यं । आदित्यजूतः । विधतॆः ।  
> सदा । राया । पुरुस्पहा ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 496

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आदित्यजूत आदित्यप्रेरित आदित्यानुगृहीतो यजमानो गोमद्गोभिरुपेतमश्ववदश्वैरुपेतं सुवीर्यं शोभनवीयोर्णपेतं पुत्रं दधानो धारयन्नेधते वर्धते सदा सर्वदा । किंच पुरुस्पृहा बहुभिः स्पृहणीयेन राया धनेन
> सडैधते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer who is impelled by Āditya (आदित्यजूत (*ādityajūta*)), that is, favoured by the Ādityas, bearing (दधानः (*dadhānaḥ*)) a son endowed with cows (गोमत् (*gomat*)), with horses (अश्ववत् (*aśvavat*)) and with excellent vigour (सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)), prospers (एधते (*edhate*)) always. Moreover he prospers with wealth (राया (*rāyā*)) that is much desired (पुरुस्पृहा (*puruspṛhā*)), that is, desirable to many. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आदित्यजूतः (*ādityajūtaḥ*)—the sacrificer impelled by Āditya
- गोमत् (*gomat*)—that which is furnished with cows
- अश्ववत् (*aśvavat*)—that which is accompanied by horses
- सुवीर‍्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)—the wealth of sons endowed with excellent vigour
- दधानः (*dadhānaḥ*)—having obtained
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- एधते (*edhate*)—attains increase
- पुरुस्पृहा (*puruspṛhā*)—desired by many
- राया (*rāyā*)—with wealth also he attains increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer impelled by Āditya, having obtained a wealth of sons furnished with cows, accompanied by horses and endowed with excellent vigour, attains increase always. He attains increase also with wealth desired by many.

##### English translation
He who is directed by Aditya ever increases, possessing abundance of cows and horses and vigorous children ; he increases in wealth longed for by many.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमिंद्रं॒ दान॑मीमहे शवसा॒नमभी॑र्वं ।  
> ईशा॑नं रा॒य ई॑महे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । इंद्रं । दानं । ईमहे । शवसानं । अभीर्वं ।  
> ईशानं । रायः । ईमहे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तं प्रसिद्धमिंद्रं दानं देयं रायो धनमीमहे । याचामहे । कीदृशमींद्रं । शवसानं बलमाचरंतमभीर्वमभीरुमीशानं सर्वस्य स्वामिनं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We ask (ईमहे (*īmahe*), we beg) that well-known Indra for a gift (दानं (*dānaṃ*), what is to be given), for wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)). What kind of Indra? One who is practising (शवसानं (*śavasānaṃ*)) strength, fearless (अभीर्वं (*abhīrvaṃ*), not timid), the lord (ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)), the master of all.

### Printed p. 497

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—the well-known Indra
- दानं (*dānaṃ*)—for the things that must be given to us
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—I ask
- शवसानं (*śavasānaṃ*)—one whose work is full of power
- अभीर्वं (*abhīrvaṃ*)—the fearless
- ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)—the lord, Indra
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—for wealth
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—I ask

**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We ask the well-known Indra for the things that must be given to us. We ask Indra, whose work is full of power, who is fearless, who is the lord, for wealth.

##### English translation
We solicit a gift from this Indra, the displayer of might, the fearless ; we solicit wealth from the lord.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तस्मि॒न्हि संतू॒तयो॒ विश्वा॒ अभी॑रवः॒ सचा॑ ।  
> तमा व॑हंतु॒ सप्त॑यः पुरू॒वसुं॒ मदा॑य॒ हर॑यः सु॒तं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तस्मिन् । हि । संति । ऊतयः । विश्वाः । अभीरवः । सचा ।  
> तं । आ । वहंतु । सप्तयः । पुरुवसुं । मदाय । हरयः । सुतं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तस्मिन्निंद्र ऊतयो गंत्रो विश्वाः सर्वा अभीरवोऽकातराः सचा सहायभूता मरुद्रूपाः सेनाः संति । भवंति । अथवा तस्मिन् सर्वा रक्षणाः सह संभवंति ।
> तमिंद्रं सप्त्ययः सर्पणशीला हरयोऽश्वाः पुरूवसुं बहुधनं ! बहुदनप्रदमित्यर्थः ! तं मदाय सुतमभिसुतमभिषुतं सोमं प्रत्या वहंतु ! आगमयंतु !!

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In that Indra (तस्मिन् (*tasmin*)) are all (विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)) the fearless (अभीरवः (*abhīravaḥ*), undaunted) protections (ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)), which are the helping armies in the form of the Maruts; they are present together (सचा (*sacā*)). Or else: in him all protections come into being together. Let the swift (सप्तयः (*saptayaḥ*), of creeping nature) bay horses (हरयः (*harayaḥ*)) bring that Indra, of abundant wealth (पुरूवसुं (*purūvasuṃ*)), that is, a giver of abundant wealth, for his exhilaration (मदाय (*madāya*)) to the pressed Soma (सुतं (*sutaṃ*)). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तस्मिन् हि (*tasmin hi*)—in that same Indra
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- अभीरवः (*abhīravaḥ*)—fearless
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- सचा (*sacā*)—together
- संति (*saṃti*)—are united

### Printed p. 498

- पुरूवसुं (*purūvasuṃ*)—possessing abundant wealth
- तं (*taṃ*)—that same Indra
- सप्तयः (*saptayaḥ*)—of a nature to move swiftly
- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—the horses
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for his delight
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—towards the pressed Soma
- आ वहंतु (*ā vahaṃtu*)—let them bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In that well-known Indra all the fearless protections are united together. Let the horses, of a nature to move swiftly, bring that same Indra, who has abundant wealth, towards the pressed Soma for his delight.

##### English translation
In him abide united all secure protections ; lord of vast wealth, may his gliding steeds bear him to the expressed Soma juice for his exhilaration.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्ते॒ मदो॒ वरे॑ण्यो॒ य इं॑द्र वृत्र॒हंत॑मः ।  
> य आ॑द॒दिः स्व१॒॑ १ र्नृभि॒र्यः पृत॑नासु दु॒ष्टरः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । ते । मदः । वरेण्यः । यः । इंद्र । वृत्रहन्तमः ।  
> यः । आददिः । स्वः । नृभिः । यः । पृतनासु । दुस्तरः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वमंत्रे मदाय हरय इत्युक्तं स मदः स्तूयते । हे इंद्र ते
> शव यो मदो वरेण्यो वरणीयः । यश्च मदः संग्रामे वृत्रहंतमः
> शत्रुणामतिशयेन हंता । यश्चाददिरादाता स्वः स्वरणं धनं नृभिन्नृभ्यः शत्रुभ्यः ।
> यश्च पृतनासु संग्रामेषु दुष्टरोऽनभिभाव्यः । तस्मै मदाय हरयो वर्णश्विति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The exhilaration (मदः (*madaḥ*)) mentioned in the previous mantra, "for exhilaration the bay horses", is now praised. O Indra, your exhilaration that is to be chosen (वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*), desirable); the exhilaration that in battle is the greatest slayer (वृत्रहंतमः (*vṛtrahaṃtamaḥ*)) of enemies; that is the taker (आददिः (*ādadiḥ*)) of wealth (स्वः (*svaḥ*)) from enemies (नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)); and that is hard to overcome (दुष्टरः (*duṣṭaraḥ*)), not to be mastered, in battles (पृतनासु (*pṛtanāsu*)): for that exhilaration let the bay horses **NOTE**

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—satisfaction
- वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*)—is venerable
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which satisfaction
- वृत्रहंतमः (*vṛtrahaṃtamaḥ*)—is completely destructive of enemies
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, that satisfaction of yours which is venerable and completely destructive of enemies, which takes away the wealth of enemy men, which delight is irresistible and strength-giving in battles: for that delight may your horses bring you.

##### English translation
That exhilaration of yours, Indra, which is pre-eminet, which utterly destroys your enemies, which wins wealth from men, and is invincible in battles ;

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो दु॒ष्टरो॑ विश्ववार श्र॒वाय्यो॒ वाजे॒ष्वस्ति॑ तरु॒ता ।  
> स नः॑ शविष्ठ॒ सव॒ना व॑सो गहि ग॒मेम॒ गोम॑ति व्र॒जे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । दुस्तरः । विश्ववार । श्रवाय्य ॥ वाजेषु । अस्ति । तरुता ।  
> सः ! नः । शविष्ठ । सवना । आ । वसो इति । गहि । गमेम । गोऽमति । व्रजे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विश्ववार विश्वैर्वर्णनीयेंद्र वाजेषु युद्धेषु यस्तव दुष्टरो
> दुःखेन तरीतुं शक्यस्तरुता शत्रोणां तारकोऽस्ति भवति हे वसो वासक हे
> शविष्ठातिशयेन बलवन्निंद्र स त्वं नः सवनास्माकं सवनान्या गहि । आगच्छ । :वयं च
> गोमति व्रजे गोमंतं व्रजं गमेम । गच्छेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Viśvavāra, Indra, to be chosen by all: in battles (वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)) that which of yours is hard to cross (दुष्टरः (*duṣṭaraḥ*)), that is, difficult to overcome, and is the overcomer (तरुता (*tarutā*)) of enemies. O Vasu, dweller, O Śaviṣṭha, Indra, exceedingly strong: you, such as you are, come (आ गहि (*ā gahi*)) to our (नः (*naḥ*)) savanas, our sacrifices; and may we reach (गमेम (*gamema*)) a stall (व्रजे (*vraje*)) full of cows (गोमति (*gomati*)). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—in battles
- दुष्टरः (*duṣṭaraḥ*)—irresistible
- श्रवाय्यः (*śravāyyaḥ*)—and renowned
- य (*ya*)—which
- तरुता (*tarutā*)—protection
- अस्ति (*asti*)—there is
- सः (*saḥ*)—you who possess it
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- सवना (*savanā*)—to the sacrifices
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be gracious
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- गोमति (*gomati*)—furnished with cows
- व्रजे (*vraje*)—the stall
- गमेम (*gamema*)—may we reach

### Printed p. 500

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, worthy of the regard of all, giver of dwellings, exceedingly mighty, be gracious to our sacrifices, you who possess the protection that is irresistible and renowned in battles. May we reach a stall furnished with cows.

##### English translation
Which is invincible in contests,—O you desired by all,—well worthy of praise and the deliverer (from enemies) ; come to our oblations, most mighty one, giver of dwellings ; may we obtain a stall full of cows.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ग॒व्यो षु णो॒ यथा॑ पु॒राश्व॒योत र॑थ॒या ।  
> व॒रि॒व॒स्य म॑हामह ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गव्यो इति । सु । नः । यथा । पुरा । अश्वया । उत । रथया ।  
> वरिवस्य । महामह ॥ १०

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे महामह महाधनेंद्र गव्या ॥ गव्या उ इति निपातानिषाद्वयसुमुदायस्यादिवद्भावेन निपातवद्भावात्कृतिभावः ॥ अस्माकं गवामिच्छायास्माकं
> गा दातुं यथा पुरा पूर्वं यथास्माकं गवादिदानाय वरिवस्यसि तद्वदव्यापि सु
> सुष्टु वरिवस्य । परिचर । आगच्छेत्यर्थः । न केवलु गवेच्छया किंत्वश्वयात्मप्रदानेच्छया । उतापि च रथया रथेच्छया च वरिवस्येति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mahāmaha, Indra of great wealth: out of a wish to give us cows (गव्या (*gavyā*)), as formerly (पुरा (*purā*)), as you attended to us to give cows and the like, so now too attend (वरिवस्य (*varivasya*), serve) well (सु (*su*)); come, is the meaning. Not only with the wish for cows, but with the wish to give horses (अश्वया (*aśvayā*)); and also with the wish for chariots (रथया (*rathayā*)), attend.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महामह (*mahāmaha*)—O Indra, who have abundant wealth
- गव्या (*gavyā*)—with the wish to give us cows
- यथा (*yathā*)—in which way
- पुरा (*purā*)—as you came formerly
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- वरिवस्य (*varivasya*)—be gracious
- आश्वया (*āśvayā*)—with the wish to give horses
- रथया (*rathayā*)—with the wish to give chariots, be gracious

### Printed p. 501

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who have abundant wealth, as you came to us formerly with the wish to give us cows, so now also be exceedingly gracious to us. Be gracious with the wish to give horses and with the wish to give chariots.

##### English translation
Lord of wealth, visit us as of old, to give us cows, horses and chariots.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न॒हि ते॑ शूर॒ राध॒सोऽंतं॑ विं॒दामि॑ स॒त्रा ।  
> द॒श॒स्या नो॑ मघव॒न्नू चि॑दद्रिवो॒ धियो॒ वाजे॑भिरावित ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नहि । ते । शूर । राधसः । अंतं । विंदामि । सत्रा ।  
> दशस्य । नः । मघवन् । नु । चित् । अद्रिवः । धियः । वाजेभिः । आविथ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शूर विक्रांतेंद्र ते तव राधसो धनस्यांतमियत्तां सत्रा सत्यं नहि
> विंदामि । न लभे । यस्मादेवं तस्मात् हे मघवन् धनवन् हे आद्रिवो वज्रवन्निंद्र
> नोऽस्माकं नू चित् क्षिप्रमेव दशस्य । देहि तद्धनं । किंच वाजेभिर्वाजैरन्नैर्धियोऽस्मदीयानि कर्माण्याविध । रक्ष ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śūra, valiant Indra, I do not truly (सत्रा (*satrā*)) find the end, that is, the measure, of your wealth (राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*)); I do not obtain it. Since this is so, O Maghavan, wealthy one, O Adrivaḥ, Indra with the thunderbolt, give (दशस्य (*daśasya*)) us that wealth quickly (नू चित् (*nū cit*)). Moreover protect (आविथ (*āvitha*)) our works (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)) with food (वाजेभिः (*vājebhiḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*)—of wealth
- अंतं (*aṃtaṃ*)—the end
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—certainly
- नहि विंदामि (*nahi viṃdāmi*)—I do not know
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—wealthy
- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- नू चित् (*nū cit*)—quickly
- दशस्य (*daśasya*)—give that wealth
- वाजेभिः (*vājebhiḥ*)—with food
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—our
